summary: Instacart addresses the business problem of extracting diverse, high-quality product attributes at scale from millions of SKUs with varying data completeness by deploying PARSE, a multi-modal Large Language Model (LLM)-based platform designed for semantic retrieval of catalog attributes from both text and images. Intended for internal catalog and data teams, PARSE enables automated, flexible attribute extraction—such as flavor, sheet count, and organic claims—through configurable prompts, multi-source reasoning, and confidence scoring, reducing reliance on brittle SQL rules and costly separate ML models. The solution’s key data sources include product titles, descriptions, and images, and it incorporates human-in-the-loop quality checks and auto-evaluation to ensure accuracy. Expected outcomes include improved extraction coverage and precision, faster iteration cycles, and scalable deployment, ultimately enhancing personalized shopping experiences by powering features that narrow searches and highlight key product labels.

Instacart faced the challenge of generating high-quality, accurate product images at scale to enhance online grocery shopping, particularly for prepared foods and fresh items where visuals strongly influence purchase decisions. To address inconsistent and siloed AI image generation efforts across teams, Instacart developed PIXEL, a unified platform providing standardized access to multiple generative AI models, fine-tuned on Instacart’s product categories using DreamBooth techniques, and enhanced by prompt templates with few-shot learning. PIXEL includes automated image quality evaluation via vision-language models that iteratively refine prompts, improving human approval rates from 20% to 85%, and integrates seamlessly with Instacart’s infrastructure for scalable API access and storage. Intended for diverse internal users without deep technical expertise, PIXEL enables rapid, consistent image creation that supports specific use cases like butcher cuts, lifestyle imagery for recommendations, and prepared food catalogs, leading to tangible business benefits such as reduced navigation times, increased cart conversions, and lowered reliance on manual photography.

Grab faced an overwhelming volume of repetitive queries in its ML platform support channels, burdening engineers and hindering innovation; the initial solution to build a chatbot using GPT-3.5-turbo was limited by token constraints and ineffective embedding search, prompting a pivot to develop GrabGPT, an internal ChatGPT-like tool leveraging Grab’s model-serving platform and supporting multiple LLMs to provide secure, auditable, and globally accessible AI interactions for all Grab employees. This tool, which allows authenticated access and ensures sensitive data remains within Grab’s infrastructure, quickly gained widespread adoption, particularly in regions where external ChatGPT access is restricted, transforming internal communication and catalyzing broader LLM strategy discussions within the company.

Instacart faced the business challenge of enhancing customer support by automating issue resolution through an AI-powered chatbot capable of handling complex queries like missing items or delayed deliveries, with intended users being their customers seeking timely assistance. To ensure chatbot effectiveness in real conversations, they developed LACE, an LLM-based automated evaluation framework assessing multi-turn chat sessions across five critical dimensions—query understanding, answer correctness, chat efficiency, client satisfaction, and compliance—using binary True/False criteria supplemented by rationale outputs. LACE incorporates agentic evaluation methods, including reflection and debate among LLM agents simulating different roles to yield nuanced, balanced performance insights. The system leverages structured prompt formatting and iterative human-LACE alignment cycles to refine its criteria and maintain strong concordance with human judgment despite challenges like domain-specific context and subjective measures. Operationalized at scale, LACE continuously monitors chatbot quality, identifying specific failure modes such as contextual lapses or inefficiencies to guide targeted improvements that enhance conversational relevance and responsiveness, thus transforming chatbot development through a robust feedback loop that synergizes advanced LLM capabilities with practical evaluation for superior customer support outcomes.

Delivery Hero addresses the business challenge of efficiently constructing a comprehensive product knowledge base to support its operations and customer service teams. The intended users include product managers, customer support agents, and AI systems requiring detailed product information. The proposed solution leverages agentic AI, which autonomously gathers, organizes, and updates product data from diverse sources, facilitating semantic retrieval of relevant knowledge. Key data considerations involve integrating heterogeneous product details while ensuring accuracy and currency amid frequent updates. The expected outcome is an agile, scalable knowledge base that enhances information accessibility, enabling employees and AI-driven interfaces to deliver faster, more informed responses to customer inquiries and operational needs.

DoorDash addresses the limitations of traditional DNN-generated embeddings for representing consumers, merchants, and items by leveraging large language models (LLMs) to create rich, interpretable narrative profiles that capture semantic nuances such as food preferences and merchant characteristics. These profiles transform raw, diverse input data—including detailed order histories, sales, menu metadata, and reviews—into human-readable JSON-formatted summaries, enabling explainable personalized recommendations, editable user and agent preferences, and rapid prototyping without retraining models. The LLM-powered pipeline uses schema definition, prompt engineering, batch processing with PySpark and Fabricator for scalability and cost efficiency, and post-processing to produce profiles for millions of entities. This approach enhances personalization with storytelling, conversational search, cold-start solutions for new merchants/items, and actionable insights for internal teams, supported by ongoing evaluation, versioned serving APIs, and iterative fine-tuning to maintain accuracy and responsiveness in production.

DoorDash addresses the business challenge of helping small and local restaurants efficiently create personalized, high-quality online menu item descriptions that drive customer conversion but are time-consuming for busy owners. Intended users include restaurant merchants seeking to enhance their digital presence and diners needing accurate, enticing dish details. The solution is a robust, production-grade AI pipeline combining three pillars: an intelligent multimodal retrieval system mining structured data, images, and similar cuisine items to overcome sparse data issues; a generation system using conditional prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and few-shot learning for accuracy and customization aligned with each restaurant’s voice and style; and a hybrid evaluation framework integrating automated quality controls, human-in-the-loop review, and A/B testing to ensure ongoing quality and business impact. This approach resolves cold-start problems, enables real-time merchant customization with multiple tone options, and creates a continuous feedback loop to refine outputs, ultimately enhancing menu content at scale, empowering merchants to showcase offerings online, and improving diner decision-making.

DoorDash addresses the business problem of costly and error-prone manual transcription and updating of restaurant menus on its delivery platform by leveraging an AI solution intended for restaurant partners and internal operations teams. The proposed solution combines optical character recognition (OCR) with large language models (LLMs) to transcribe menu photos into structured data formats, but since diverse menu layouts and variable photo quality reduce LLM transcription accuracy, DoorDash developed a guardrail system—an ML-based quality classifier using image and tabular features—to automatically assess transcription reliability. This hybrid approach filters out low-quality or inconsistent transcriptions for human review while enabling scalable, high-accuracy automation with lower latency and costs. The expected outcome is a more efficient, cost-effective menu maintenance pipeline that balances AI innovation with rigorous quality controls, continuously adapting to evolving AI models and aiming to improve transcription performance through domain-specific fine-tuning and better photo quality management.

Coinbase addresses the challenge of improving machine learning model performance in fraud detection and recommender systems by developing a scalable framework for building and productionizing sequence features from rich user event sequences, such as sign-ins, buys, sells, and crypto sends. Targeted at machine learning engineers, the solution integrates streaming infrastructure (Kafka), batch processing (Databricks Spark), and feature management (Tecton) to automate event registration, schema standardization, and feature view creation, enabling rapid, cost-efficient feature engineering with low latency (sub-100ms online serving, 1-2 second freshness). This approach captures detailed temporal and contextual information lost in traditional hand-crafted aggregated features, allowing deep learning models like Transformers and LSTMs to learn directly from user action sequences up to 1000 events long, significantly boosting model insights and business impact. The framework also supports extensible read-time transformations to tailor sequences for specific applications, streamlining developer workflow while abstracting operational complexity, thus facilitating widespread adoption of sequence learning within Coinbase’s diverse ML ecosystem.

Coinbase aims to enhance its recruiting process by integrating AI to handle large applicant volumes efficiently while maintaining fairness and candidate engagement. Recruiters, rather than being replaced, will use AI for smarter resume screening—prioritizing relevant skills and reducing bias—along with automated interview scheduling that accounts for preferences and conflicts, and AI-assisted interview note-taking to focus on candidate interaction. This AI-driven approach targets non-EU/UK roles initially, emphasizing confidentiality and equal opportunity, with iterative pilots ensuring a positive experience. The expected outcome is a faster, more thorough recruitment funnel where top candidates surface quickly, and recruiters can deepen relationships by focusing on high-value activities instead of administrative tasks.

Plaid addresses core challenges of data accuracy and connectivity reliability for financial services by deploying AI-powered agents aimed at improving product experience and operational efficiency. The AI Annotator accelerates high-quality labeling of anonymized financial transactions using large language models (LLMs) combined with targeted human validation, overcoming scalability limits of manual annotation and enabling enhanced categorization models across use cases like personal finance and credit. Concurrently, the Fix My Connection agent proactively detects and automatically repairs access issues in thousands of bank integrations through intelligent script generation, significantly reducing downtime and manual effort, thereby boosting conversion and user satisfaction. These solutions rely on scalable centralized infrastructures and continuous feedback loops, generating outcomes such as over 95% human alignment in labeling accuracy and a 90% reduction in repair time for integration degradations. Future expansions include broader classification tasks, integration creation, and real-time AI-powered troubleshooting capabilities accessible via APIs, empowering customers with more resilient and intelligent financial data connectivity.

Plaid faced the business challenge of accelerating AI coding tool adoption among hundreds of skilled engineers without disrupting ongoing projects, targeting engineering leaders in mid-to-large tech firms aiming to boost AI-driven productivity. To address this, they implemented a strategic AI engineering program involving rapid pilot testing focused on quick value realization, careful legal and security alignment due to their regulated consumer finance domain, dedicated adoption ownership with usage analytics and user outreach, and creation of in-house, Plaid-specific educational content that demonstrated AI tools working on their actual codebase. The solution emphasized complementing existing IDEs rather than replacing them to ease integration, fostered peer sharing to build organic adoption, and culminated in a company-wide AI Day for hands-on experience. Important constraints included managing variable costs, benchmarking difficulties, and adapting to diverse team needs. Expected outcomes included widespread, sustained AI tool usage (>75% regular adoption), enhanced engineer productivity through more integrated AI-assisted coding workflows, and the foundation for extending AI use beyond coding into broader software development lifecycle tasks like incident response and code review.

LinkedIn addresses the challenge of delivering personalized, high-quality job recommendations to its over one billion members by deploying JUDE, a production platform that fine-tunes large language models (LLMs) to generate semantic embeddings representing jobs, member profiles, and resumes. JUDE integrates fine-tuned LLMs with a scalable, low-latency serving architecture using nearline inference pipelines and GPU-based model serving, enabling real-time updates of embeddings upon job postings or profile changes. The system balances semantic relevance and real-world engagement signals by combining scarce, high-quality annotated labels with large-scale user interaction data during supervised fine-tuning, optimizing architectures and losses for both accuracy and efficiency. JUDE replaces traditional feature engineering and taxonomy dependencies with dense vector representations, leveraging advanced training techniques like LoRA and distributed training on Nvidia H100 GPUs, while achieving substantial improvements in key recruitment metrics such as qualified applications and job application rates.

LinkedIn addressed the limitations of traditional keyword-based job search by developing an AI-powered semantic retrieval system that enables its 1.2 billion members to describe desired roles in natural language and receive highly personalized, nuanced job recommendations. This solution leverages large language models (LLMs), embedding-based retrieval, and multi-objective optimization to understand complex user intents beyond keyword matching, integrating personalized filters from profile data and external context for precise search results. To meet scalability and latency requirements, the architecture separates retrieval and ranking stages, using GPU-accelerated exhaustive nearest neighbor search over job embeddings, fine-tuned via reinforcement learning with a teacher-student distillation framework. The system also employs synthetic training data generation with human and LLM-annotated quality grading to continuously improve relevance. Dynamic query refinement and personalized suggestion engines enhance user interaction, while model pruning and caching optimize inference efficiency. Overall, the platform achieves a semantic-first, interpretable, and scalable job search experience that improves relevance and inclusivity compared to legacy systems, transforming job discovery into a more intuitive and effective process.

LinkedIn addressed the challenge of bridging rapid prototyping by engineers and domain expert insights for enhancing AI-powered features like their Sales Navigator product by creating collaborative prompt engineering playgrounds using Jupyter Notebooks. The solution targets both technical and non-technical users involved in developing LLM-driven capabilities such as AccountIQ, which automates and accelerates company research through orchestrated multi-step prompt chains managed by LangChain and jinja templates. Key constraints included maintaining consistent LLM configurations, managing dynamic prompt templates with complex placeholders linked to real-time external data (e.g., Bing Search), and ensuring high-quality, diverse test datasets representing realistic scenarios. By integrating a Python backend service exposing gRPC endpoints, containerized environments for seamless setup, and Jupyter Notebook interfaces that allow live experimentation and version-controlled collaboration, LinkedIn enabled cross-functional teams to iteratively refine prompts with immediate feedback and robust quality control. This approach yielded a rapid prototyping framework fostering inclusive collaboration, optimizing prompt engineering workflows, and ultimately improving product-market fit and customer impact through continuous, data-driven feature enhancement.

Binance’s Strategy Factory addresses the challenge of manually crafting static, intuition-based risk and fraud detection rules that struggle to adapt to evolving threats and vast, complex transaction data. Intended for risk analysts, this AI-powered rule engine automates the generation, optimization, and refinement of interpretable Boolean-rule sets, using novel methods like the linear, single-path Split algorithm combined with FIT’s iterative, bagged rule creation and a Global Gain utility that aligns rules with specific business goals such as maximizing recall and precision. It incorporates domain-specific constraints and interactive fine-tuning (Squeeze and Grow) to ensure operational viability, while supporting continuous adaptation to data drift. Deployed across Binance’s risk areas (login, KYC, deposits, withdrawals), Strategy Factory accelerates rule creation, reduces false positives, improves coverage, and enhances detection precision, enabling faster, scalable, and business-aware risk control with plans for conversational AI and large language model integration to further streamline and democratize rule management.

Mercado Libre addresses the challenge of interpreting diverse, unstructured financial transaction data across Latin America’s evolving Open Finance landscape by developing a scalable AI-driven semantic retrieval system tailored to regional linguistic and contextual nuances. Initially reliant on error-prone, manual regex rules insufficient for multiple languages and MCC inconsistencies, they transitioned to Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-3.5 Turbo combined with a human-in-the-loop validation process to improve categorization accuracy from ~60% to over 80% while slashing costs and enabling massive scale. To overcome latency and cost barriers of external LLM APIs at hundreds of millions of weekly transactions, Mercado Libre advanced to custom-trained financial semantic embeddings fine-tuned on regional financial text, further boosting accuracy to 90%, reducing operational costs by 30%, and supporting near real-time, model-agnostic workflows. The resulting semantic engine not only enables more precise, context-aware transaction categorization across varied dialects but also lays the foundation for personalized financial insights and fairer services, all built on a strong ethical and privacy framework, ultimately transforming raw transactional data into a shared financial language that empowers users, businesses, and data scientists to engage meaningfully with their financial narratives in LATAM.

Mercado Pago’s Collateral Management team faces the challenge of optimally allocating billions of dollars in loans as collateral across multiple credit lines, each with complex contractual conditions, regulatory compliance requirements, and dynamic market constraints, within tight daily time frames. To automate and optimize this selection process, they developed Enigma, a linear programming-based solution leveraging Google OR-Tools for optimization, enhanced by an in-house grouping heuristic that clusters similar loans to manage the NP-Complete problem’s scalability. Enigma integrates with cloud-based data sources and internal infrastructure (Fury), providing a user-friendly, transparent, and flexible interface that supports adding new constraints and credit lines while delivering detailed reporting for auditing. The solution maximizes collateral value and funding efficiency while ensuring compliance and adapting rapidly to market changes, aiming to improve decision-making and operational agility in the financial industry.

Mercado Libre addressed the complex e-commerce product-matching problem, where inconsistent item listings by various sellers complicate identifying identical products critical for personalization, advertising, inventory management, and pricing. Targeting millions of items, the intended users include marketplace operations and pricing teams. Their solution combines diverse open-source embedding models for feature encoding, Approximate Nearest Neighbors algorithms for candidate retrieval, and a sophisticated machine learning model employing advanced NLP and multimodal embeddings to estimate match probabilities, with selective human review for sensitive high-stakes cases like pricing. To scale cost-effectively under $0.001 per request, they developed a robust system orchestrating multiple large language models (LLMs) in a finely tuned pipeline refined through iterative prompt engineering and model orchestration, using an internal framework (“Verdi”) to rapidly experiment and optimize precision (95%) and recall (>50%) while controlling expenditure and ensuring reliability. This multi-node architecture integrates vector databases, preprocessing pipelines, and APIs, leveraging reflection, task decomposition, and consensus mechanisms among LLMs, resulting in an autonomous matching system achieving human-level performance suited for large-scale production across various product categories despite challenges in ML-only automation.

Airbnb addresses the challenge of delivering efficient voice-based customer support by developing a machine-learning-powered Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system that enables guests and hosts to express issues in natural language rather than navigating rigid menus. The system leverages Airbnb-specific Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) to accurately transcribe noisy phone audio with domain-specific terminology, a Contact Reason Detection model to classify caller intents rapidly, and a semantic help article retrieval framework that indexes Help Center content via vector embeddings and re-ranks results using large language models. To enhance user comprehension and engagement, a paraphrasing model generates clear, concise summaries of the detected intent before presenting relevant help resources. This integrated approach reduces human agent dependency by facilitating self-service resolutions, streamlines call routing when escalation is needed by attaching contextual details, and improves overall customer satisfaction and operational efficiency in Airbnb’s voice support ecosystem.

Airbnb addressed the challenge of surfacing relevant home listings from millions of options, especially for broad geographic queries and flexible dates, by developing an Embedding-Based Retrieval (EBR) system for candidate ranking in search. Intended for Airbnb guests searching for stays, the solution uses contrastive learning on user trip data to train a two-tower neural network that embeds both search queries and home listings into vector representations; positive and negative sample pairs were constructed from users' multi-stage search journeys, focusing on booked homes versus interacted but unbooked ones. The listing embeddings are pre-computed offline daily to reduce latency, while real-time query embeddings enable efficient retrieval. For online serving, Airbnb chose an approximate nearest neighbor approach using an inverted file index (IVF) due to its better speed-memory trade-off and suitability for frequent real-time listing updates and filtering. The system uses Euclidean distance to maintain balanced cluster sizes, optimizing retrieval quality. Deployment led to a significant increase in bookings, reinforcing the model’s ability to incorporate query context for improving search relevance at scale.

Airbnb faced the business challenge of migrating 3,500 React component test files from Enzyme to React Testing Library (RTL), a task initially estimated to require 1.5 years of engineering time due to fundamental differences between the frameworks and the need to preserve test intent and code coverage. The intended users were Airbnb engineers responsible for maintaining reliable testing infrastructure. The solution leveraged large language models (LLMs) combined with a scalable, automated, step-based validation and refactor pipeline, enhanced by retry loops with dynamic prompting and extensive contextual information including related source files and example tests. This approach allowed parallel processing of files and iterative prompt refinement to systematically overcome migration failures. The data constraints involved complex, variable test files and the need to maintain coverage while ensuring correctness. The outcome was a rapid migration completing 75% of files in four hours and 97% after four days of tuning, drastically reducing manual effort to six weeks overall and preserving test integrity, demonstrating LLM-driven automation as a highly efficient method for large-scale codebase transformations.

Glassdoor tackles the business problem of delivering personalized content across its Community Feed, Email, and Push notifications to enhance user engagement by deploying a multi-stage hybrid recommendation system that combines collaborative and content-based filtering. Intended for the platform's users seeking relevant posts, the system first generates candidate posts using user and post embeddings derived from a selected large language model, leveraging Approximate Nearest Neighbor search via OpenSearch over multiple regularly updated inverted indexes. These embeddings capture semantic similarities among content and users, enabling efficient retrieval of highly relevant candidates. Subsequent stages filter out inappropriate content, score posts using independently deployed machine learning models managed via MLflow and served in scalable Kubernetes clusters, and finally order results applying business rules and supporting A/B experimentation across stages. Supporting layers include an experimentation framework for testing model variants, a data store that maintains embeddings and feature stores, and monitoring tools like Grafana and Prometheus ensuring performance and quality observability. This modular, scalable architecture allows continuous optimization through data-driven iterations and targeted improvements to recommendation quality.

Canva addressed the business challenge of creating a personalized, shareable year-in-review experience for millions of engaged users by leveraging generative AI to reflect individual design journeys while respecting strict user privacy policies. Targeting users with significant design activity and marketing consent, they inferred users' top design themes, styles, and emerging design trends from metadata of publicly used templates rather than personal design content, employing keyword-matching and AI-enhanced keyword expansion to predict design trends with 99% coverage. Users were segmented into design personality groups combining trends and audience themes, with generative AI producing tailored poetic content across locales based on top design styles. These personalized data points—including design count, type, personality, poems, and trends—were dynamically embedded into base templates to generate unique, engaging social media stories, resulting in 95 million customized DesignDNA campaigns that strengthened user connection and showcased Canva's AI capabilities.

Canva addressed the business problem of efficiently replacing images in their design templates when third-party media licenses expire, a process formerly requiring extensive manual work by designers. Targeting professional template designers as users, they developed a reverse image search system based on image embeddings extracted from state-of-the-art machine learning models—specifically selecting DINOv2 for its superior similarity matching on photographic content—enabling scalable, IP-safe suggestions from over 150 million indexed images stored in an external vector database optimized for metadata filtering such as image aspect ratio. This solution provides a hierarchical similarity framework prioritizing subject matching and finer details like color, composition, and emotion to ensure seamless template image replacement. The resulting system, integrated into Canva’s Template Assistant with human-in-the-loop quality control, demonstrated a 4.5x speed increase in image replacement tasks, significantly streamlining design maintenance while highlighting weaknesses on non-photographic images due to training data limitations, which are planned to be addressed via additional metadata tagging and filtering in future iterations.

The use case addresses the business problem of a data access gap where non-technical users struggle to query enterprise databases due to the complexity of SQL, causing decision delays and bottlenecks by engineers and data scientists. Intended users include project managers, analysts, and other non-technical staff working within Salesforce, primarily using Slack for collaboration. The proposed solution is Horizon Agent, an internal text-to-SQL AI Slack agent powered by large language models (LLMs) using Retrieval-Augmented Generation to combine natural language queries with enriched business context and dataset metadata from tools like Fack and the Horizon Data Platform. This system generates accurate SQL queries on demand, executes them against a data lake, and returns both answers and transparent explanations directly in Slack’s conversational interface, enabling seamless, instant insights without requiring SQL expertise. Constraints include handling language ambiguity, evolving jargon, and ensuring query accuracy through multiple attempts and validation algorithms. The expected outcome is democratized, real-time data access that accelerates decision-making, reduces reliance on technical gatekeepers, fosters user trust via transparency, improves productivity by freeing engineers for higher-value work, and cultivates a new collaborative workflow integrating AI-powered semantic retrieval in day-to-day operations.

Canva addressed the challenge of improving private design search for over 200 million monthly users without compromising user privacy by creating a synthetic evaluation dataset using generative AI, specifically GPT-4o, to mimic realistic design content and queries without accessing actual user data. The intended users are Canva engineers who need to rapidly and independently test search pipeline changes offline before A/B experiments. The solution involved generating labeled test cases for recall and precision that replicate re-finding tasks, combining synthetic relevant and nonrelevant designs generated based on privacy-preserving aggregate statistics, and running evaluations locally using containerized replicas of the production search environment. This approach overcame limitations of prior manual offline tests and costly online experiments, enabling reproducible, deterministic evaluation on over 1,000 queries in under 10 minutes, correlating well with real-world performance, and supporting detailed debugging with a custom visualization tool. The outcome is a scalable, privacy-preserving framework that accelerates search improvement iterations while safeguarding the confidentiality of user-generated designs.

Criteo addresses the business problem of delivering more personalized ads in real time, which requires fast and efficient image and video generation for ad variations, by improving consistency models (CMs) that promise rapid inference but suffer from unstable training. Intended users include AI researchers and engineers in commerce foundation models focused on real-time personalization. The proposed solution, Generator-Augmented Flows (GC), introduces a self-reinforcement training technique where the model’s own endpoint predictions are fed back into its training loss to reduce discrepancies found when training CMs from scratch versus distillation from pre-trained diffusion models. This approach accelerates convergence, enhances model performance, and lowers stochasticity during training, enabling quicker fine-tuning of high-quality generative models while cutting GPU resource consumption. The expected outcome is more engaging, diverse ad content delivered efficiently at scale, balancing computational cost and real-time requirements.

Meta addresses the challenge of detecting specific, meaningful software faults in large-scale, multi-language codebases by developing Automated Compliance Hardening (ACH), an LLM-powered system that combines mutation testing and test generation. Intended for software engineers across Meta’s platforms like Facebook Feed and WhatsApp, ACH takes plain-text descriptions of fault concerns and leverages large language models to generate realistic mutants (deliberate code faults) and corresponding unit tests guaranteed to catch those faults, overcoming traditional mutation testing limitations of unrealistic mutants and manual test creation. This approach transforms vague or incomplete fault descriptions into verifiable tests targeting regression risks, particularly enhancing privacy-related fault detection, thereby improving code reliability, reducing privacy risks, and optimizing testing processes by automating complex workflows within software development.

Yelp addresses the challenge of accurately understanding user search queries—distinguishing intent, correcting spelling, segmenting semantic components, and highlighting relevant review phrases—by integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT-4 into core search features used daily by millions. Intended for users seeking personalized, context-aware business discovery, the solution leverages LLMs for tasks like query segmentation (labeling parts as topic, location, time, etc.) and generating diverse, semantically enriched review highlight phrases that improve relevance and user trust. Key data considerations include leveraging query-level caching to handle the power-law distribution of search terms, combining spelling correction with segmentation in unified prompts, and augmenting queries via Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) using viewed business names or categories to improve decision-making. A multi-stage approach—from formulation and prototyping with expensive LLM calls, through fine-tuning smaller models for large-scale pre-computation, to deploying fast real-time inference models—enables cost-effective scaling across all traffic, including tail queries. The expected outcome is improved search click-through rates and user satisfaction through more precise intent understanding, implicit location rewriting, and richer, contextually relevant review snippets, ultimately enhancing Yelp’s search experience and business value.

Netflix tackles the challenge of detecting rare, subtle pixel-level artifacts—specifically "hot" pixels caused by sensor glitches that appear as tiny bright spots in individual frames—by developing a bespoke neural network that processes high-resolution video segments at full scale with temporal context from five consecutive frames. Intended for video quality control teams to reduce painstaking, error-prone manual reviews early in production, the solution leverages a synthetic pixel error generator for initial model training due to the rarity of faults, then iteratively refines performance with real-world data to minimize false positives. The model outputs pixel-precise error maps processed in real time on a single GPU, enabling fast, scalable detection of transient pixel errors that, if undetected, could cause costly fixes downstream. This approach accelerates QC workflows, allowing creative teams to focus more on storytelling while maintaining high sensitivity in flagging subtle video sensor artifacts.

The business problem involves selecting and evaluating large language models (LLMs) for integration into GitHub Copilot to provide high-quality, safe, and performant AI-assisted coding tools for developers. Intended users include software engineers relying on Copilot for code generation, codebase modification, and technical Q&A. The proposed solution is a comprehensive, multi-phase evaluation framework combining large-scale automated tests and targeted manual assessments, leveraging over 4,000 offline tests on diverse containerized repositories and a curated technical question set to measure performance, accuracy, and safety across multiple programming languages and frameworks. Constraints include balancing conflicting metrics such as latency versus suggestion acceptance rates, ensuring consistent and scalable evaluation using a proxy-based architecture without product code changes, and maintaining continuous monitoring of production models to detect regressions. The expected outcome is informed model selection and tuning that maximize code completion quality and user satisfaction while safeguarding reliability and responsible AI usage within GitHub Copilot.

Duolingo faced a business problem scaling DuoRadio, an audio feature that improves language learners’ listening comprehension through short, scripted radio shows, due to its labor-intensive production requiring scripting, voice acting, and editing. Intended users are Duolingo learners across many languages and proficiency levels who benefit from immersive listening practice aligned with curriculum goals. The proposed solution leverages generative AI driven by curriculum-based prompts to automatically generate level-appropriate, grammatically sound scripts, combined with AI-powered evaluators crafted by Learning Designers to filter outputs for quality, coherence, and educational alignment. Additionally, automated text-to-speech audio production and end-to-end generation pipelines enable massive scale without manual intervention. Constraints include maintaining Duolingo’s high linguistic and pedagogical quality standards and adapting prompts to each language’s curriculum for accuracy. Expected outcomes are a 10x faster content generation rate, expansion from 2 to 25+ courses, growth of daily sessions from 500K to 5M, and over 15,000 episodes produced in under two quarters, delivering high-quality, curriculum-aligned immersive listening experiences to millions of users while reducing costs by 99%.

The Manus project addresses the business challenge of rapidly deploying effective AI agents that leverage large language models' in-context learning for semantic retrieval and task execution, targeting developers building autonomous multi-tool agents. Instead of training end-to-end models, Manus employs "context engineering" to iteratively refine how the model's input context is structured, focusing on maximizing KV-cache hit rates to reduce latency and inference costs by maintaining stable, append-only prompts and handling dynamic tool selection via masked token logits rather than modifying action spaces. Because LLM context windows are limited and costly, Manus externalizes long-term memory to a file system the agent can read and write, preserving information without inflating the input context. To maintain focus during complex workflows, the system continuously recites task objectives (e.g., updating a todo list) to concentrate model attention on goals. It also embraces failure by retaining error traces in context to aid recovery and learning, while introducing controlled variability into example sequences to prevent overly rigid behavior due to few-shot pattern repetition. This empirical, iterative context engineering approach balances model capabilities, environment interaction, and feedback loops, resulting in an agent architecture that is more efficient, robust, and scalable for real-world multi-step tasks.

Square addressed the challenge of accurately categorizing merchants—critical for personalized product experiences, strategic decision-making, targeted marketing, product eligibility, and compliance with payment processing requirements—by developing a RoBERTa-based large language model (LLM). Unlike prior approaches relying on merchant self-selection and outdated ML methods, this solution integrates high-quality ground truth labels from over 20,000 manually reviewed sellers and a rich set of post-onboarding signals such as business names, self-selected onboarding data, and merchant catalogs ranked by purchase frequency. The workflow includes cleaning auto-created services, prompt engineering for clear context, and GPU-accelerated training and inference using Databricks with optimizations like FP16 and gradient checkpointing. Inference leverages parallel GPUs, PySpark, batch size optimization, and incremental predictions to efficiently handle tens of millions of sellers daily. This approach yielded approximately 30% absolute accuracy improvement over self-selection in identifying merchant categories across major business domains, thereby enhancing Square’s internal business metrics, product strategy, marketing targeting, and future financial operations such as interchange fee management.

Intuit addresses the challenge of discovering precise, up-to-date information within extensive technical documentation by deploying a generative AI-powered dual-loop pipeline designed to continuously improve document quality, structure, and retrieval relevance for engineers and knowledge workers. The inner loop employs specialized GenAI plugins—such as Document Analyzer, Improvement, Style Guide, Discoverability, and Augmentation—to evaluate, refine, standardize, semantically enrich, and update documentation, ensuring consistent and comprehensive knowledge base content. The outer loop enhances semantic retrieval by generating vector embeddings for similarity searches, context-aware search, and answer synthesis from multiple knowledge sources, dynamically adapting search parameters based on user feedback to improve future query responses. This solution overcomes variability in documentation quality, obsolescence, and poor structuring by enabling continuous content enhancement and context-driven retrieval, resulting in faster, more accurate knowledge discovery that can extend beyond software documentation to other domains.

Netflix addresses the complexity and maintenance costs of its personalized recommender system by developing a centralized foundation model that learns member preferences from large-scale, tokenized user interaction data spanning long temporal windows. Targeted at enhancing diverse recommendation tasks across the platform, this model leverages semi-supervised next-token prediction with modifications such as multi-token prediction and auxiliary objectives, while incorporating sparse attention and sliding window sampling to handle extensive sequences efficiently under latency constraints. Unique challenges include cold-start for new titles, addressed via incremental training and metadata-enhanced embeddings combined through age-aware attention, allowing inference on unseen entities. The foundation model supports multiple downstream applications—from direct prediction with multiple heads to generating stabilized embeddings for users and content—enabling fine-tuning for specific use cases. Drawing on insights from large language models, Netflix’s approach emphasizes data-centric, end-to-end training at scale, improving recommendation quality and resource efficiency while accommodating evolving catalogs and member behaviors.

The business problem tackled is the challenge of ensuring compatibility between recommended products in a DIY and home improvement e-commerce platform, where mismatched suggestions—such as a mattress not fitting a bed frame—can frustrate users. Intended for shoppers using the platform, the solution combines semantic retrieval techniques leveraging machine learning: first, harnessing user purchase behavior to identify co-purchased items as proxies for compatibility, though limited by cold start and noisy data; second, mining association rules from standardized product attributes to infer compatibility patterns, hampered by attribute extraction and normalization difficulties; and third, fine-tuning a French-language sentence transformer model using pairs of product textual descriptions labeled as compatible or incompatible, incorporating a custom contrastive loss weighted by purchase confidence. This model computes compatibility scores that filter out incompatible recommendations and enable suggestions for new or rare products lacking purchase history. The approach integrates textual product data including names, category labels, attributes, and descriptions, addressing critical constraints of heterogeneous attribute formats and sparse labeled data. The expected outcome is an enhanced recommendation system providing more accurate, compatibility-aware product suggestions that improve customer satisfaction and reduce incompatible cross-sells, with ongoing challenges in evaluation metrics and negative sample construction guiding future refinements.

Pinterest faced the challenge of improving search relevance so that user queries surface genuinely pertinent Pins rather than relying on superficial engagement metrics, benefiting users seeking inspiring, contextually aligned content. The solution involved fine-tuning a large cross-encoder language model (LLM) as a teacher to classify the relevance of Pins to queries on a 5-level scale, employing enriched Pin text features including user-generated titles/descriptions, synthetic image captions (via BLIP), high-engagement query tokens, board titles, and linked webpage metadata. Due to scalability constraints, knowledge distillation was used to transfer this LLM's knowledge into a lightweight student model combining query-level, Pin-level, and interaction features for online serving. Semi-supervised learning enabled training on billions of logged search impressions labeled by the teacher, facilitating generalization across multiple languages and unseen concepts. Offline experiments validated the benefits of larger, sophisticated multilingual LLMs (e.g., Llama-3–8B) and enriched text features on relevance accuracy, while online A/B tests showed a >2% improvement in nDCG@20 relevance and increased search fulfillment globally. This approach addressed complex semantic matching in multimedia Pins at scale, enhancing Pinterest Search’s ability to meet diverse user information needs efficiently.

Pinterest addressed holiday gift discovery challenges faced by millions of users overwhelmed by disparate wishlists and broad product choices. Targeting consumers at early shopping inspiration stages, especially unbranded searchers, engineers enhanced their existing Homefeed personalization system with gift-specific candidate generation (identifying gift-worthy Pins via purchase intent and seasonal relevance), ranking with real-time user intent and diversity algorithms, and blending filters to curate a balanced, relevant feed. To streamline organizing gift ideas, they built automated wishlist boards triggered by user engagement, supporting seamless saving and complex edge cases like board management across platforms. A new Structured Feed Framework enabled rapid UI iteration with adaptive headers and cross-platform optimization, while a two-phase tab ranking system mitigated cold start issues by balancing fixed exposure and engagement-driven personalization. Comprehensive unified logging extended Homefeed analytics to capture gift discovery behaviors. This integrated solution delivered higher engagement, especially among Gen Z users, simplified holiday shopping journeys, and laid a scalable foundation for continued personalization, UI innovation, and shopping feature expansion within Pinterest’s ecosystem.

Pinterest faced the challenge of enhancing user engagement on its home feed, which previously recommended a grid of Pins but limited contextual richness and exploration of new topics. The intended users are Pinners browsing their home feed for personalized content recommendations. Pinterest introduced heterogeneous modules—such as landing page and carousel modules—that provide varied UI and content formats influenced by topics, boards, and user interests, offering more context and interactive experiences. The proposed solution involves a Module Relevance Platform that dynamically blends these modules with Pins, addressing challenges like module fatigue, ranking, and blending. Key data inputs include historical user-module engagement, cover Pins’ ranker scores, module metadata, and comprehensive user features. The platform uses a dedicated multi-head deep ranking model trained on user engagement signals, supplemented by heuristic fatiguing and a skip-slot blending strategy that compares predicted engagement scores of modules and Pins to optimize feed placement without degrading core metrics. The expected outcome is an improved, personalized home feed that increases user engagement by balancing novel module content with relevant Pins while maintaining feed relevance and responsiveness.

Whatnot, a rapidly scaling live marketplace with over $3 billion GMV in 2024 and extensive livestream hours, faced significant challenges in ranking dynamic shows for its personalized For You Feed, which drives half of its GMV. Initially relying on computationally expensive batch predictions of buyer-seller interaction likelihoods for feed ranking, the approach struggled with scalability (O(nm) growth), stale predictions, inability to incorporate show-level and real-time features, and cold-start problems for new users and sellers. To address this, Whatnot transitioned to an online inference system where real-time retrieval of current shows and dynamic feature values—including request-level, hourly, and session-level data—enable real-time ranking predictions at serving time. This shift allowed integration of more timely signals, immediate accommodation of new marketplace entities, and asynchronous feature logging for training/inference consistency. The move resulted in measurable business improvements such as a 7.5% increase in GMV from the For You Feed, while introducing challenges in latency, system scalability, feature correctness, and monitoring that required new engineering solutions.

Wayfair developed Wilma, a customer service agent copilot that leverages large language models (LLMs) like Gemini and GPT to draft empathetic, policy-compliant responses by dynamically generating prompts based on real-time customer, order, and product data, helping agents resolve issues 12% faster and improve policy adherence by 2-5%. To tackle challenges in conversation control and resolution negotiation, Wilma evolved from using one complex prompt and single LLM call to multiple specialized prompt templates and sequential LLM calls that analyze ongoing conversations, track proposals, and ensure appropriate resolutions. Intended for customer service agents managing complex interactions, especially during peak times, Wilma aims to automate routine dialogue segments, allowing agents to focus on nuanced problems and eventually supervise multiple AI-led chats simultaneously, enhancing operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.

DoorDash addresses the challenge of scaling and enhancing search relevance evaluation—crucial for enabling customers to find desired items quickly—by developing AutoEval, a human-in-the-loop system powered by large language models (LLMs) and the whole-page relevance (WPR) metric. Traditional human annotations were limited by scalability, latency, inconsistency, and coverage, especially given DoorDash’s diverse verticals and complex UIs. AutoEval automates the evaluation of millions of query-result pairs daily by transforming search pages into structured tasks, using task-specific, structured prompts aligned to detailed internal rating rubrics, enriched with contextual metadata, and fine-tuned on expert-labeled data to mirror human reasoning. The WPR metric evaluates the entire spatial search result page—beyond linear lists—measuring relevance across retrieval, ranking, post-processing, and UI layout stages. AutoEval supports offline impact assessment of ranking and UI changes, continuous production monitoring, and leverages human audits for maintaining quality through iterative prompt refinement and fine-tuning. This approach reduces evaluation turnaround time by 98%, increases capacity ninefold, improves consistency and accuracy over crowd raters, and reallocates human expertise to guideline and edge-case focus, thereby transforming DoorDash’s search evaluation into a fast, scalable, and reliable process that helps deliver better, user-aligned search experiences.

eBay addresses the challenge of applying large language models (LLMs) to e-commerce by developing customized Llama-based models, dubbed e-Llama, through continued pretraining on a blend of proprietary e-commerce data and general domain datasets. Targeted users include eBay’s AI teams and ultimately customers engaging in buying and selling across global markets, who benefit from personalized, context-aware interactions. The approach balances maintaining general language understanding while infusing domain-specific knowledge by mixing e-commerce listings, reviews, and curated open-source data with a fraction of non-English content to enhance multilinguality. Training leverages extensive distributed GPU resources and optimized frameworks to efficiently process over one trillion tokens, resulting in 8-billion and 70-billion parameter models that outperform base Llama 3.1 models by roughly 25-30% on e-commerce benchmarks without significant loss in general NLP capabilities. Post-training instruction tuning with human feedback further aligns model outputs with safe, relevant responses, enabling eBay to scale cost-effective, proprietary LLM solutions that meet domain-specific needs while mitigating risks of third-party dependencies.

Shopify addresses the challenge of accurately classifying and describing millions of diverse products sold across its platform to improve search, discovery, and merchant/buyer experiences. Early methods using basic category classification with traditional machine learning evolved into a sophisticated system leveraging a comprehensive Shopify Product Taxonomy—covering over 10,000 categories and 1,000 attributes—and advanced Vision Language Models (VLMs) that integrate multi-modal image and text understanding. This system delivers hierarchical, category-specific attribute extraction and generates consistent product descriptions via zero-shot learning and natural language reasoning, enabling robust semantic retrieval beyond mere categorization. Key constraints include maintaining consistency across a vast, evolving taxonomy and optimizing efficient real-time inference at massive scale (30 million daily predictions) through innovations like FP8 quantization, dynamic request batching, and KV cache optimization within a Kubernetes GPU infrastructure. The system's multi-LLM annotation pipeline with human validation ensures high-quality training data aligned to taxonomy standards. Outcomes include an 85% merchant acceptance rate of predicted categories, improved product discoverability, enhanced search relevance, automated attribute tagging, and reinforced platform trust and safety, demonstrating a scalable, high-precision semantic retrieval solution for complex product understanding in e-commerce.

Lyft addresses the business problem of balancing real-time rideshare supply and demand across hundreds of North American cities by employing real-time spatial temporal forecasting models that predict market signals at fine spatial granularity (geohash-6) and high temporal frequency (every minute). Intended users include dynamic pricing and driver incentive systems that adjust prices and driver earnings based on short-term market forecasts. The solution involves implementing both classical time-series models—like autoregression, ARIMA, spatial-temporal covariance models, and dimension reduction techniques—and deep neural networks such as RNNs, LSTMs, CNNs, with considerations of latency, computational cost, and model retraining frequency. Important constraints include the trade-offs between model accuracy and engineering costs, handling noisy and sparse data with local spikes from irregular events, and the necessity of frequent refitting due to rapidly changing market conditions. The expected outcome is improved real-time marketplace balance through accurate short- and medium-term demand and supply forecasts, enabling responsive pricing and incentive mechanisms with scalability, interpretability, and reliability within Lyft’s machine learning platform and streaming architecture.

Slack addresses the business problem of securely and privately enabling enterprise search across internal Slack content and external applications like Google Drive and GitHub, targeting Slack users and administrators who require seamless access to permissioned, up-to-date knowledge. Their solution builds on Slack AI’s foundation, using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with closed-source large language models hosted in a secure environment, ensuring customer data never leaves Slack’s trust boundary and is only processed if users have permission. Enterprise search employs a federated, real-time approach that queries external data sources via secure OAuth authorization without storing any external content, adhering to the principle of least privilege by requesting only necessary read scopes. Explicit access grants and revocations by users and admins maintain strict control over external data inclusion. This design preserves enterprise-grade compliance, security, and privacy while delivering a powerful, integrated semantic retrieval experience that surfaces relevant, permissioned insights from both Slack and connected third-party tools.

Snap’s advertising platform addresses the challenge of efficiently moderating and ranking vast daily ad creatives by converting multimedia content—videos and images with audio—into rich, structured, human-readable text descriptions using multimodal language models. This method samples key frames, transcribes audio, and generates detailed natural language annotations capturing brands, products, context, and key events, overcoming limitations of traditional embedding approaches that lose context, are uninterpretable, and difficult to annotate. Intended for compliance teams, moderation systems, and relevance ranking models, these textual representations enable precise keyword search, flexible feature expansion without retraining, and improved fraud and brand safety detection through clear, actionable insights. This scalable text-based pipeline enhances transparency, reduces costs, simplifies downstream processing, and boosts the accuracy and efficiency of ad moderation, relevance targeting, and emerging trend detection in Snap’s ecosystem.

Netflix addresses the business challenge of improving content recommendations by predicting user session intent via FM-Intent, a novel hierarchical multi-task learning model designed for the platform's recommender system. Intended users are Netflix members interacting with the service, whose implicit engagement signals—such as action type (e.g., continuing versus discovering content), genre preferences, content type, and time-since-release—serve as critical data inputs. FM-Intent extends the existing foundation model by first predicting user intent through a Transformer encoder that models both short-term and long-term interests, and then hierarchically integrating these intent predictions into next-item recommendations. This structured approach leverages attention-based aggregation to produce comprehensive intent embeddings, enabling more personalized, relevant suggestions. Offline experiments demonstrate FM-Intent’s statistically significant improvements (7.4% uplift over prior state-of-the-art models) in next-item prediction accuracy and generate meaningful user clusters based on intent embeddings. Deployed in production, FM-Intent enhances recommendation precision, informs UI personalization, improves search prioritization, and supports analytics for better user understanding and content strategy.

Expedia Group addresses personalized hotel search by extending their hotel2vec embedding model to include traveler loyalty tier as contextual input, enabling coarse-grained personalization based on user engagement levels. Targeted users are travelers segmented into blue, silver, and gold loyalty tiers, whose preferences influence property embedding representations. The model integrates property features (amenities, ratings, star level, location) with traveler context via early fusion, and is trained on a year's worth of click session data using SGD with negative sampling to minimize co-occurrence loss. Evaluation includes hits@k metrics for embedding quality and incorporation into a downstream search ranking model, which demonstrated improved NDCG@10 and qualitative shifts in recommended properties aligned with loyalty tier—lower-priced but similarly rated options for blue members, and higher-quality, higher-priced choices for silver/gold members. In an online test, dynamically retrieving tier-specific embeddings from a feature store led to significant lift in conversion rates, confirming that contextual property embeddings enhance search relevance by tailoring recommendations to user cohorts.

Stripe Tax addresses the complex business problem of accurately and rapidly determining applicable sales tax jurisdictions for transactions across the US, where intricate and frequently changing geographic tax boundaries create over 16,000 unique tax rate combinations. Its intended users are Stripe’s customers who require precise tax calculations during online purchases. The solution employs a patent-pending jurisdiction resolution system (JRS) with offline and online components: offline, a geographic information system (GIS) cleans, standardizes, and overlays multi-level jurisdictional boundary data to define non-overlapping, time-aware tax regions called Stripe places of taxation (SPOTs); online, it matches geocoded customer addresses to these SPOTs using a multi-level bounding box indexing structure implemented via a balanced R-tree to efficiently narrow down candidate tax zones before applying computationally intensive point-in-polygon algorithms. Constraints include inconsistencies and inaccuracies in public geospatial data, the geometric complexity of tax boundary polygons, and the need for millisecond-level latency to avoid transaction delays. The expected outcome is highly accurate, low-latency tax jurisdiction identification that adapts promptly to changes in tax law, ensuring reliable and scalable tax calculations for businesses using Stripe globally.

Netflix addresses the complexity and high maintenance costs of its personalized recommender system, which relies on multiple specialized models, by developing a centralized foundation model that leverages large-scale member interaction histories and content metadata for unified preference learning. Intended for internal use by recommendation engineers and downstream applications, this data-centric, semi-supervised large-scale model employs interaction tokenization, sparse attention, and sliding window sampling to efficiently process extensive, heterogeneous user event sequences within strict latency constraints, overcoming limitations of short temporal windows in conventional models. The model predicts next interactions using a multi-token objective with auxiliary tasks to capture long-term user preferences and combats cold-start challenges for new titles by combining learnable embeddings from both item IDs and metadata, weighted adaptively via attention mechanisms. It produces stable user and item embeddings for use in various downstream tasks, supports incremental training with warm-start initialization to handle evolving catalogs and user behavior, and can be fine-tuned for application-specific needs. Through careful scaling of data, model size, and context length, the foundation model improves recommendation quality and adaptability compared to fragmented prior approaches, advancing Netflix’s goal of delivering personalized entertainment at scale.

Pinterest addressed limitations in their home feed recommendation system’s pre-ranking stage by modernizing its architecture and training pipeline. The previous two-tower model, deployed separately across retrieval sources, faced deployment complexity, sync challenges, and weak user-item interaction modeling due to late fusion via dot-product. The updated pre-ranking layer jointly trains a request-level sub-component for user representation and an item-level sub-component for online item feature extraction and user-item feature crossing, allowing richer interactions and efficient inference via a root-leaf sharding architecture to handle large item corpora. A novel early funnel logging pipeline capturing both impressed and unimpressed candidates corrects sample selection bias and enables using real negative samples during training, supporting non-two-tower architectures through combined binary cross entropy and distillation losses. Auto-retraining synchronizes models for timely updates, collectively leading to significant engagement improvements and standardized feature handling, with ongoing work focused on further data, model, and serving optimizations.

eBay addresses the challenge of delivering personalized, relevant product recommendations at industrial scale across its dynamic inventory of over two billion listings using Mercury, an agentic AI platform that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and a Listing Matching Engine. Intended for data scientists and engineers within eBay's recommendation teams, Mercury structures LLM-powered processes as modular, reusable "Agents" and "Chains" with defined interfaces that enable scalable, interoperable, and maintainable AI services supporting real-time, low-latency retrieval. Mercury enhances LLM outputs by augmenting them with up-to-date, context-specific data from internal listings, external web crawls, and partner sources, enabling dynamic text-to-listing matching through semantic embeddings and precision filtering (e.g., category and price constraints). This approach bridges the gap between LLM-generated product concepts and live marketplace listings, while ensuring AI safety via integrated content moderation and prompt injection safeguards. The outcome is a robust, scalable AI-driven recommendation system that delivers timely, personalized shopping experiences to hundreds of millions of users, setting a new standard for AI application in large-scale e-commerce environments.

Meta’s Reality Labs addresses the challenge of underutilized, noisy, biased, and unstructured customer feedback data by developing a self-service AI tool powered by their open-source Llama 4 large language models (LLMs) for product analytics. Targeted at product managers and analysts, the solution aggregates a comprehensive repository of immutable and mutable feedback from diverse internal and external sources, applying Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to enhance answer accuracy by retrieving contextually relevant customer inputs via semantic embeddings and cosine similarity searches. Constraints include mitigating hallucination risks through prompt engineering, scope management, and embedding additional context such as bug stack traces. The expected outcome is richer, actionable insights that integrate qualitative feedback with quantitative metrics to improve bug deduplication, internal QA, and strategic product development, demonstrated by applications like extracting sentiment from YouTube reviews for Meta Quest headsets, ultimately enabling nuanced understanding of evolving user preferences and driving innovation.

Facebook uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to analyze unstructured user feedback in the form of bug reports submitted through their apps, addressing the business challenge of efficiently processing and interpreting vast, complex text data to improve product quality. Intended for cross-functional teams such as Engineering, Product Management, and User Experience Research, the solution involves LLM-based classification systems enhanced by iterative prompt engineering and domain expertise to categorize and rationalize user complaints at scale. Important data considerations include privacy-compliant, aggregated long-term retention tables feeding into dashboards that enable real-time monitoring, trend detection, and root cause analysis. This approach facilitates proactive issue identification, guides impactful product fixes, and reduces bug report volume, ultimately enhancing user experience across Meta’s family of apps.

Booking.com's business problem involved improving the complexity, flexibility, and scalability of data enrichments that enhance machine learning-based travel recommendations across diverse customer journeys. Intended users are primarily internal developers who integrate personalized insights—such as accurate pricing, property wishlist counts, recommended images, and user interaction tracking—into recommendations, previously hindered by tightly coupled code and limited reusability. The proposed solution is a new Enrichment System leveraging field masks combined with GraphQL APIs, allowing developers to request specific enrichments on demand without deep code modifications, thus decoupling enrichment from the prediction stage. Key data constraints include handling diverse and dynamic enrichment requests efficiently, achieving high throughput (up to 100,000 enrichments/second) and near-perfect availability (99.99%). This modular, standardized approach enhances developer self-service, reduces errors, promotes reuse, and improves system performance and reliability, ultimately enabling more tailored, robust, and scalable recommendation data enrichments for traveler personalization.

Intuit addressed the challenge of improving engineering productivity with AI-assisted code generation by developing a platform-centric solution tailored to its unique development environment, serving over 8,000 engineers. Recognizing that off-the-shelf AI coding assistants lacked awareness of Intuit-specific APIs, architectural patterns, and compliance standards, they created "golden repositories": curated, high-quality code examples enriched with metadata and validation data to provide real-time context in AI code generation. This context-aware approach enables AI assistants to produce code that aligns with Intuit's design system, best practices, and internal conventions, significantly reducing manual edits, accelerating test generation (58% used without modification), and increasing pull request velocity by 56%. The solution deeply integrates AI capabilities across the Inner and Outer Loops of the software development lifecycle, transforming AI from a simple extension into a collaborative development partner, thereby achieving up to 8× developer velocity improvements and consistent adoption across experience levels.

Wise addresses the challenge of providing instant, convenient, transparent cross-border money transfers to 15.6 million active customers and enterprise clients, including banks, by leveraging a highly scalable and standardized technology platform. Its users encompass internal engineering squads, mobile and web developers, data scientists, and external business clients integrating via their secure, OAuth-backed REST API. The solution includes a distributed microservices architecture built with Java and Kotlin, a Kubernetes-based Compute Runtime Platform for scalable deployments, and advanced observability and CI/CD pipelines using Spinnaker and GitHub Actions. Crucially, Wise employs a sophisticated data infrastructure with Kafka streaming, distributed databases, and a data lake leveraging Apache Iceberg, combined with machine learning pipelines using Amazon SageMaker and in-house ML serving to enhance fraud detection and customer onboarding. Additionally, Wise has integrated multiple large language models through a custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation service to augment internal knowledge retrieval and customer service automation. Data governance and lifecycle management ensure compliance and developer productivity at scale. The expected outcome is a reliable, cost-optimized, and intelligent global payments platform that supports rapid innovation while maintaining security, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency.

Shopify addresses the challenge of heterogeneous, unstructured, and multilingual product data from millions of diverse merchants by building a Global Catalogue powered by multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs) to unify, standardize, and enrich product information across its platform. Intended for Shopify merchants and downstream AI-driven commerce applications such as search, recommendations, and conversational agents, the solution involves a four-layer process: ingesting massive streaming product updates; applying fine-tuned multimodal LLMs for tasks like hierarchical product classification, attribute extraction, image understanding, and text summarization; clustering identical products via graph-based matching with universal product IDs; and reconciling clustered data into canonical, comprehensive product records. Selective field extraction during model fine-tuning improves inference efficiency and generalizability, enabling 40 million daily LLM-powered inferences at reduced latency and GPU cost. Continuous active learning with human-in-the-loop annotation and comprehensive evaluation metrics ensures ongoing model robustness. The outcome is a richly structured, machine-readable product knowledge foundation that enhances semantic search relevance, personalization, and AI-assisted commerce workflows while supporting scalability and evolving taxonomy demands at Shopify’s global scale.

Dropbox Dash addresses the business problem of fragmented and diverse digital workflows that hinder knowledge workers' productivity and collaboration by providing a universal search and knowledge management platform with granular content access control. Targeted at business users managing multi-application, multi-format data environments, Dash leverages retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to combine semantic and lexical information retrieval with large language models (LLMs), ensuring accurate, timely, and context-rich responses under strict latency constraints. To handle complex, multi-step queries requiring domain-specific logic and orchestration, Dash employs AI agents that generate and execute safe, Python-like domain-specific code plans, supported by a custom interpreter with static analysis and runtime type enforcement for security and reliability. This hybrid solution balances data diversity, fragmentation, and modality challenges, delivering a robust, scalable AI-powered search experience that enhances knowledge workers' efficiency while maintaining data security and freshness.

Picnic addresses the blind spots in its fully automated Utrecht warehouse, where tote contents are currently only inspected at picking or delivery stages, risking undetected product errors. Intended for warehouse operators and quality-control teams, the proposed computer vision solution uses cost-effective 2D cameras with controlled lighting to capture sharp, barcode-linked images of moving totes, enabling neural networks to verify correct item counts, detect misplaced or damaged goods, and prevent delivery errors. The system balances hardware choices (2D vs. 3D cameras) and AI inference strategies (edge-based models like YOLO and CountGD versus cloud-hosted Vision Language Models such as Google's Gemini) to optimize accuracy, latency, and scalability. Expected outcomes include reduced manual recounts and stock inaccuracies, earlier fault detection, minimized waste, and improved customer satisfaction, all implemented without disrupting conveyor belt throughput.

Dropbox Dash addresses the business problem of inefficiency faced by knowledge workers who struggle to find multimedia files such as images, videos, and audio across diverse apps and disorganized folders, especially since these files often lack meaningful metadata and have cryptic names. Intended users are professionals needing fast, accurate search of multimedia content within their workflows. The solution reengineers search infrastructure originally built for text by indexing lightweight media metadata (e.g., file paths, EXIF, reverse geocoded locations), extending relevance models for media-specific signals, and implementing just-in-time preview generation to balance high storage and compute costs against latency constraints. This is supported by a scalable previews service and caching to maintain responsiveness. The UI emphasizes fast visual previews with adaptive layouts and on-demand metadata hydration to help users quickly identify relevant files. Expected outcomes include reduced search time and improved retrieval quality for multimedia, enabling a universal search experience with the same intelligence applied to both text and media files, while maintaining cost-performance trade-offs central to scalable multimedia semantic retrieval.

eBay addressed the challenge of manually creating visually engaging category-specific images, which was time-consuming and unscalable, by developing an automated image generation system using multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Vision Models. Targeted at improving shopper engagement and merchandising flexibility across thousands of categories, the system extracts popular item titles weighted by click-through rates, simplifies them to remove non-visual details, and generates detailed image prompts aligned with product photography best practices. A novel feedback loop employs a multimodal LLM-driven evaluation framework that scores images on fidelity, clarity, and stylistic adherence, iteratively refining prompts and regenerating images until predefined quality thresholds are met. This approach ensures high-quality, thematically relevant visuals that replace plain text category representations, enhancing the browsing experience while adhering to eBay’s Responsible AI principles. Human evaluation validated the system’s effectiveness, with 88% of AI-generated images deemed suitable, demonstrating a scalable, resource-efficient solution that elevates eBay’s visual shopping experience.

The business problem addresses complex open-ended research tasks requiring dynamic, multi-step information gathering beyond the capacity of single-agent systems. Intended users include researchers and professionals seeking comprehensive insights from extensive data sources such as the web and Google Workspace.
