This system enables statistically robust, frequent, and cost-effective estimation of prevalence across multiple policy areas, surfaces, and content segments with confidence intervals, facilitating proactive risk detection, rapid root cause analysis, data-driven policy iteration, and strategic enforcement. Constraints include handling rare categories with wide confidence intervals, managing prompt drift, ensuring LLM stability, and controlling operational costs, while future plans focus on expanded segmentation, LLM fine-tuning, human-in-the-loop denoising, and broader application of the pipeline.

Shopify addresses the challenge of maintaining and evolving a complex product taxonomy—comprising over 10,000 categories and 2,000 attributes—amid rapidly changing commerce trends by deploying an AI-driven multi-agent system designed for continuous taxonomy evolution rather than static classification. Intended for taxonomy experts and platform engineers, this solution integrates actual merchant product data with structural taxonomy analysis through specialized AI agents that detect gaps, inconsistencies, and attribute relationships, including sophisticated equivalence between category-attribute combinations, enabling merchant flexibility without sacrificing system intelligence. Automated quality assurance agents act as domain-specific judges to vet proposed taxonomy modifications using advanced reasoning aligned with industry standards, significantly reducing manual bottlenecks. The outcome is a proactive, scalable system that enhances taxonomy consistency, accelerates updates for emerging product categories, improves search and filtering for merchants and customers, and supports ongoing refinement through tighter integration with product classification pipelines.

Doctolib addresses the growing volume of healthcare support requests by developing an agentic AI system composed of specialized Large Language Model-powered agents, orchestrated via LangGraph, to intelligently handle routine queries and free human agents for complex, empathetic cases. The solution targets healthcare professionals using Doctolib’s platform, aiming to sustain support quality while controlling costs. Key features include role-specific agents with constrained API access following least privilege principles, security enforced through dual JWT authentication and user context propagation, and a human-in-the-loop design where AI-generated action requests are fact-checked and confirmed by users to prevent hallucination risks. A practical deployment example automates managing calendar access rights through interactive dialogues, enhancing user experience beyond standard chatbots. The system handles ~1,700 daily support cases with multiple message exchanges, ensuring context maintenance, security compliance, and execution accuracy, evaluated via Literal.ai for task achievement and efficiency, setting a scalable foundation for broader healthcare support automation.

Airbnb addresses the challenge of producing realistic, type-safe GraphQL mock data that is tedious and error-prone to create and maintain manually by engineers, particularly hindering frontend development before backend completion and causing mocks to drift from production data as schemas evolve. Targeting product and client engineers, their solution introduces the @generateMock GraphQL directive, integrated into their existing code generation tool, Niobe, to automatically generate and update context-aware mock data using large language models fine-tuned with schema definitions, product context, UI design snapshots, and domain-specific hints, ensuring mocks are valid via a validation loop. Complemented by @respondWithMock, this approach enables client engineers to unblock UI development by serving mock data for unimplemented fields while mixing real server responses. Niobe tracks hash changes to intelligently update mocks, preserving manual edits and maintaining sync as queries evolve. This results in highly realistic, maintainable mocks conducive to prototyping, testing, and demos, reducing engineering overhead and accelerating feature development across Airbnb’s iOS, Android, and Web platforms.

DoorDash confronts the challenge of moderating millions of daily user-generated chat messages, images, and calls to maintain a safe platform for Dashers and customers. Its SafeChat AI system employs a hybrid semantic retrieval approach: a multi-layered text moderation pipeline evolved from a three-tier model leveraging external moderation APIs and large language models to an efficient, internally trained model complemented by a precise LLM for ambiguous cases, enabling rapid and cost-effective filtering of harmful content like profanity, threats, and sexual language. Image moderation harnesses granular computer vision models fine-tuned to identify diverse safety risks with improved precision and latency, while voice moderation analyzes real-time calls for unsafe language and tone, initially under human review before enabling automated interventions. SafeChat applies measured responses—blocking or censoring content, canceling or reassigning deliveries, restricting communication, and escalating severe cases to human agents—to prevent escalation and protect users. This semantically aware system has halved medium and low-severity safety incidents, enhancing trust, operational efficiency, and platform reliability by proactively and scalably safeguarding communication across modalities.

The business problem addresses the low recall and relevance limitations of traditional keyword-based search in a large-scale, multilingual e-commerce platform with visually rich content; the intended users are online shoppers seeking more accurate and comprehensive search results. The proposed solution integrates dense retrieval via a Two-Tower model architecture, where a query tower encodes user queries into 256-dimensional embeddings based on a fine-tuned multilingual CLIP model, and an item tower generates embeddings by fusing image features and categorical metadata from catalog items. The model is trained using contrastive learning over hundreds of millions of positive pairs, optimized with techniques such as learnable temperature and cosine annealing, and deployed within a Vespa application managing approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) searches using multiple HNSW indices partitioned by market. Significant engineering effort addresses scalability, latency constraints (500ms query budgets), and consistency requirements, employing dynamic threshold tuning, retry strategies between approximate and exact nearest neighbor searches, and complex ranking phase filtering with reciprocal rank fusion to limit poor-quality nearest neighbor matches. Performance optimizations include JVM upgrades and garbage collection tuning, resulting in improved search metrics, reduced tail latencies, and extremely low error rates (<0.02%). The outcome is a dense retrieval-enhanced search system that demonstrably improves recall and relevance at billion-scale datasets, while establishing a flexible architecture that supports future advancements like image search and personalized ranking.

Wayfair automates its supplier-facing ticket triage process, assisting supplier associates who manually classify unstructured ticket data by question type, supplier ID, and preferred language in SupportHub, a JIRA-based system. To reduce manual effort, error, and response times, they developed Wilma, an LLM-powered automation framework orchestrated via LangGraph that integrates LLMs for intent classification, language detection, and a ReAct LLM agent with BigQuery access to identify supplier IDs by dynamically querying structured data. By combining a deterministic workflow with agent-based querying, Wilma improves accuracy—achieving 93% for question type, 98% for language, and 88% for supplier ID—surpassing human performance while enabling associates to focus on complex tasks. Observability is enhanced through Arize, and lessons highlight the trade-offs between agentic and workflow approaches, favoring a hybrid model for reliability and adaptive error handling in a complex event-driven architecture. This system exemplifies LLM-based semantic retrieval and reasoning to extract and structure insights from semi-structured supplier ticket text, with plans to extend LLM automation to other repetitive business processes.

Pinterest addresses the challenge of understanding users’ long-term intentions rather than only immediate interests by identifying personalized user journeys—defined as sequences of user-item interactions reflecting evolving interests, intents, and contexts across sessions. Targeting users engaged in multi-stage activities like wedding planning or home renovation, Pinterest employs a dynamic keyword extraction approach, clustering keywords from search queries, pin interactions, and boards using pretrained embeddings to form journey candidates. The system names journeys via ranking models and explores LLM-based improvements for naming and recommendations, while journey ranking, diversification, and stage prediction models ensure relevance, variety, and lifecycle awareness. This architecture supports journey-aware notifications that significantly increase user engagement metrics. Constraints include limited initial annotated data, prompting a lean, extensible design leveraging foundation models and streaming inference pipelines, with ongoing efforts to consolidate components and boost accuracy using large language models, validated through LLM-based relevance evaluation correlated with human judgments.

Grab addressed the challenge of accurately extracting information from diverse Southeast Asian (SEA) documents for eKYC by developing a custom lightweight Vision Large Language Model (LLM). Traditional OCR struggled with SEA languages and varied formats, while existing Vision LLMs lacked sufficient SEA visual-text training and had high latency. They chose Qwen2-VL 2B as a base due to its support for SEA languages, dynamic image resolution, and size amenable to GPU fine-tuning. Using synthetic OCR datasets from SEA languages and their in-house auto-labeling framework Documint for high-quality training data, they first attempted low-rank adaptation fine-tuning, which improved Latin script accuracy but faltered on Thai and Vietnamese. Subsequently, full-parameter fine-tuning using a two-stage process (continual pre-training on synthetic data, then task-specific fine-tuning) significantly boosted accuracy (+70pp Thai, +40pp Vietnamese). To optimize deployment efficiency, Grab built a novel ~1B-parameter Vision LLM combining Qwen2-VL’s encoder and a compact language decoder, trained through projector alignment, vision tower enhancement, language-specific visual training, and task-centric fine-tuning. This custom model matched the larger model’s accuracy within 3 percentage points but outperformed it and traditional OCR in latency, critical for scalable operations. Their approach highlights the importance of full fine-tuning, native-language support, meticulous data augmentation, and dynamic resolution handling in specialized Vision LLMs for semantic retrieval of document information in multilingual SEA contexts.

BlaBlaCar addresses the inefficiency and friction between Software Engineers (SWE) and Data Analysts (DA) in accessing and analyzing production data by shifting data analysis left—enabling engineers to validate and query data during feature development rather than relying on downstream analysts. Their solution, BlaBlaCar Data Copilot, is an AI-powered extension integrated into the engineers' IDE that uses curated business-specific semantic retrieval from BigQuery, combining existing code and documentation to provide context-aware Text-to-SQL assistance tailored to BlaBlaCar’s domain logic. It generates transparent, test-covered Python scripts as artifacts subject to pull-request review by analysts, fostering collaboration and maintaining rigorous analytical standards. This approach replaces ad-hoc queries and opaque dashboards with reproducible, version-controlled analyses, operationalizes data quality as an upstream engineering task, and enhances data culture by making insights accessible and maintainable. The system leverages large language models for synthesis without complex new infrastructure, employs heuristic linting for data health warnings, and transforms the data repository into an indexed memory for reusable knowledge, resulting in faster engineer autonomy, scalable analyst focus on complex tasks, and improved trust in data-driven decisions.

DoorDash addresses the challenge of dispersed, complex organizational knowledge by developing an internal agentic AI platform that unifies distributed data and operations into a collaborative ecosystem, targeting business users across Finance, Strategy, Analytics, and Operations. The platform evolves from deterministic workflows—reliable, sequence-driven pipelines optimized for high-stakes reporting and operational tasks—toward dynamic agents powered by large language models using ReAct architecture for adaptive, multi-step reasoning. It advances further into deep agents that decompose hierarchical tasks through specialized, coordinated subagents with shared persistent memory, ultimately exploring asynchronous agent swarms that distribute control across peer agents for resilient, emergent solutions to complex, real-time logistics problems. Key technical enablers include a vector-based multistage semantic retrieval system integrating reciprocal rank fusion, schema-aware SQL generation with zero-data statistical validation to ensure accuracy and guardrails, and LLM-based automated evaluation frameworks for continuous reliability assessment. The platform emphasizes trust through provenance and auditability, user accessibility via integrations with Slack and development environments, and open standards like model context protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication protocols to scale multi-agent collaboration. This layered, scalable approach enables business stakeholders to get trustworthy, timely insights without requiring technical query skills, improving operational agility and decision-making efficiency.

The ART·E project addresses the business problem of efficiently answering users' natural-language questions by searching their email inboxes, targeting everyday users who want quick, accurate responses without manual keyword searches. Leveraging publicly available Enron email data, the team generated a synthetic dataset of realistic question-answer pairs using GPT-4, structuring the environment with tools for keyword-based email search and email reading via a local sqlite database with full-text search. They implemented a simple agentic loop guided by reinforcement learning, using the ART training library and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to optimize a reward function balancing answer correctness, minimal interaction turns to reduce latency, and penalization of hallucinations. Benchmarking against existing models like o3, ART·E demonstrated faster, cheaper training (~$80 on a single H100 GPU) and achieved higher accuracy with fewer hallucinations, highlighting the effectiveness of RL-based semantic retrieval for email question-answering agents.

Leboncoin addressed the business challenge of providing secure, efficient internal access to diverse company knowledge amid GenAI adoption risks by developing Ada, an internal chatbot leveraging large language models (LLMs) while ensuring strict data privacy and residency compliance under EU law. Targeted at data scientists, machine learning engineers, and employees across departments, Ada initially used hosted Anthropic Claude models via AWS Bedrock for trust and privacy, later evolving to specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistants connected to internal data sources like Confluence, Lumapps, and Backstage, employing vector databases, OpenSearch, rerankers, and query rephrasers to enable precise semantic retrieval across multilingual corpora and structured organizational data. Integration into workflows such as Slack enhanced usability, while custom evaluation metrics and datasets ensured answer correctness and source relevance. Despite Ada’s operational success and valuable learnings in deploying LLM-based retrieval systems with tailored architectures and strict governance, rising maintenance costs and emerging enterprise solutions with data residency guarantees prompted a strategic transition towards ChatGPT Enterprise, leveraging its EU-compliant infrastructure and richer integration capabilities, thereby marking Ada’s sunset as a foundational but complex step in scalable, secure semantic retrieval deployment within an enterprise context.

Wayfair addresses the challenge of identifying style compatibility across its extensive catalog of tens of millions of SKUs to improve search and recommendations beyond popularity biases by developing an LLM-powered binary classification pipeline using Gemini 2.5 Pro on Google Cloud. Intended for catalog curators and recommendation engineers, the multimodal model processes product images and metadata with carefully engineered, interior-design-informed prompts and few-shot examples to label pairs of products as stylistically compatible or not, encapsulating nuanced design principles like shape, material, and color harmony. This scalable, automated labeling replaces slow, costly human annotation and yields an 11% accuracy gain over initial prompts, enabling consistent style-aware evaluation of recommendation algorithms aligned with expert judgments. The outcome is improved search relevance and customer experience via style-coherent product pairings, with future plans to incorporate active learning, monitor evolving style trends, and extend compatibility judgments to entire room sets for enhanced personalization at scale.

The Reinforcement Infused Agentic RAG framework addresses the challenge of automating the authoring of software test cases from business requirements in Quality Engineering (QE) by integrating reinforcement learning with autonomous AI agents and a hybrid vector-graph knowledge base, enabling continuous improvement beyond static LLM-generated testing artifacts. Targeting QE professionals, the system leverages expert feedback, defect detection outcomes, and workflow metrics to optimize test case generation strategies using RL algorithms like PPO and DQN, thus establishing a dynamic knowledge refinement loop that enhances test accuracy and defect detection rates. Validated through enterprise Apple projects, this approach demonstrated a 2.4% increase in test generation accuracy and a 10.8% boost in defect identification, ultimately augmenting human testers’ effectiveness within QE workflows rather than replacing them.

Meta addresses the challenges of scaling mutation testing for software compliance by developing Automated Compliance Hardening (ACH), an LLM-powered tool that generates realistic, domain-specific code mutants and corresponding tests through simple textual prompts. Mutation testing, traditionally hindered by high computational costs, unrealistic or equivalent mutants, and scalability issues, is transformed by leveraging Meta’s extensive bug data to train LLMs that focus on relevant fault classes such as privacy risks. ACH's LLM-guided mutation and test generation reduces cognitive load for developers, ensures continuous compliance, and improves risk resilience across large codebases in platforms like Facebook and Instagram. Additionally, the platform incorporates an LLM-based equivalence detector to filter out semantically equivalent mutants, optimizing test quality and resource use. Meta's ongoing initiatives, including the Catching Just-in-Time Test (JiTTest) Challenge, seek to further harness LLMs to generate precise, human-reviewed tests that catch faults pre-production, addressing open challenges such as the Test Oracle Problem while enhancing developer workflow and global regulatory adherence.

Pinterest Search addresses the challenge of evaluating search relevance—a measure of how well search results align with user queries—by fine-tuning open-source multilingual large language models (LLMs) on human-annotated relevance labels spanning five levels from Highly Relevant to Highly Irrelevant. This LLM-based relevance model ingests rich textual features from Pins, including titles, descriptions, BLIP image captions, linked page info, and user-curated board titles, enabling accurate semantic relevance prediction across languages. The solution reduces reliance on costly human labeling, permitting a stratified sampling design that improves experimental sensitivity, lowers minimum detectable effects (MDEs) from around 1.3-1.5% to ≤0.25%, and supports measurement of heterogeneous treatment effects in A/B tests. Using models like XLM-RoBERTa-large balances prediction accuracy and inference efficiency, allowing labeling of large query-Pin pairs fast enough for practical deployment. Validation demonstrates strong alignment between LLM-generated and human labels at both Pin and query levels, including for non-English queries, ensuring reliable relevance metrics for online experiments, improved metric quality, and reduced annotation costs. The approach empowers Pinterest to track whole-page relevance more effectively, optimize personalized search rankings, and facilitate rapid iteration on search features.

trivago addressed the business challenge of enhancing productivity and innovation across its 700 employees by transitioning from isolated AI experiments to comprehensive company-wide integration between 2023 and 2025. The intended users are broadly the entire workforce, with particular benefits in technical, product, marketing, finance, legal, and research teams. The proposed solution centers on embedding AI tools like trivago Copilot for tasks including data analysis, content drafting, technical support, and workflow automation, supported by the AI Ambassadors group that fosters cross-functional knowledge sharing, governance via Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), and strategic tool adoption processes. Constraints include maintaining data safety and reliability amid rising user expectations, managed through a categorized AI tool dashboard and procurement protocols. The expected outcome is significant productivity gains—averaging 16 workdays saved per employee annually—enhanced decision-making, creativity scaling, and a culture of AI-driven innovation and ethical governance that continuously evolves to unlock new business value.

Gradient Labs addresses the business problem of ensuring high-reliability AI agents for financial services customers, where failures in response to critical money-related queries are unacceptable. Intended for financial service providers and their customers, the solution employs a resilient agentic system integrating multiple large language models (LLMs) from providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with orchestration via Temporal for durable checkpointing. Key constraints include managing latency, rate limits, error handling, and state persistence across potentially long LLM call chains, while intelligently failing over across API providers and models to mitigate 5XX errors, rate-limiting, and latency spikes. Tailored prompts are developed for primary and backup models to maintain response quality during failovers. The expected outcome is a robust, fault-tolerant AI agent that reliably serves accurate financial assistance with minimal disruptions, even under adverse conditions or provider outages.

Instacart faced challenges in accurately understanding diverse and often imprecise user search queries, especially long-tail and broad queries, due to noisy labels, sparse data, and a complex legacy of multiple disconnected models for query understanding tasks like classification and rewrites. To address this, they leveraged Large Language Models (LLMs), enhancing them with domain-specific context through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), post-processing guardrails, and fine-tuning using proprietary data, creating a unified, specialist intent engine. This hybrid approach integrates an offline "teacher" pipeline that generates high-quality semantic role labels and cached results for common queries with a fine-tuned, lightweight real-time "student" model handling long-tail queries, optimizing for cost, latency, and accuracy. Their solution yields improved precision, recall, and semantic tagging, reduces system complexity, delivers significant enhancements in search quality (e.g., lowering average scroll depth by 6%), and enables a scalable, efficient semantic retrieval system that better interprets nuanced user intent, ultimately transforming Instacart’s eCommerce search experience.

The Deep Research AI assistant addresses the business problem of automating complex, multi-faceted information gathering and synthesis tasks that traditionally require extensive manual effort and expertise, targeting researchers, knowledge workers, and professionals needing comprehensive, curated insights on diverse topics. The solution employs agentic large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned with custom-tuned frontier models like Gemini 1.5 Flash, executing iterative, asynchronous workflows that autonomously plan, search 100+ web sources, extract, verify, and synthesize findings into editable research reports over several minutes, with UX features allowing users to steer research plans and pose follow-up queries. Key constraints include managing long research session latencies (around five minutes), handling noisy and fragmented web data, and maintaining deep contextual memory of up to millions of tokens, with ongoing challenges related to effective orchestration, source grounding, and evaluation metrics. The expected outcome is a superhuman digital research assistant capable of producing nuanced, thoroughly sourced reports and second-order insights with PhD-level quality and efficiency, revolutionizing knowledge work by replacing manual browsing with a transparent, iterative AI-driven research process.

The Digits Machine Learning Team addresses the business problem of deploying reliable AI agents—redefined as process daemons—in production for accounting workflows, targeting internal engineering teams managing AI system operations. Their solution involves building lightweight, transparent background processes that combine a clear objective, a large language model (LLM), curated tool invocation via API introspection, and observable responses, emphasizing control and production readiness over dependence on complex open-source frameworks. Key constraints include maintaining thorough observability with OpenTelemetry, ensuring memory through semantic search integrated with databases, implementing guardrails with secondary LLM assessment to avoid model self-trust, and reusing existing APIs to preserve security. Expected outcomes are faster, more accurate task completion in use cases such as vendor data enrichment, client onboarding simplification, and multi-source complex query handling, alongside continuous improvement through feedback loops, ultimately delivering robust, transparent, and responsible AI processes rather than hype-driven autonomous agents.

The use case addresses the challenge of performing sophisticated legal research traditionally requiring expert attorneys to navigate complex, jurisdiction-sensitive questions and nuanced legal authority. The intended users are practicing lawyers who need to efficiently identify and assess relevant case law, statutes, and secondary sources while understanding the strength of legal inferences and emerging statutory changes. The proposed solution, Deep Research, is an agentic AI system integrated into Westlaw Advantage and CoCounsel that autonomously plans multi-step research strategies, executes parallel document analysis, employs specialized tools and real-time content evaluation (including KeyCite warnings), and maintains session memory to orchestrate findings coherently. Constraints include ensuring high accuracy and trustworthiness through rigorous model selection, human verification loops, compliance with enterprise privacy and security, and managing the tradeoff between comprehensive retrieval and noise minimization within limited model context windows. The expected outcome is a transformative, reliable legal research assistant that elevates research depth, quality, and efficiency by replicating the iterative, reasoning-driven workflows of skilled attorneys, thereby enhancing legal professionals’ ability to build well-supported cases in high-stakes environments.

Meta addresses the business problem of repetitive and overwhelming notifications on Instagram by introducing a diversity-aware notification ranking framework aimed at improving user experience and engagement quality for Instagram users. The challenge is balancing personalization, which optimizes for click-through rates and time spent by prioritizing familiar content and authors, against the risk of overexposure to the same creators or notification types leading to user fatigue and notification disablement. The proposed solution layers a multiplicative diversity penalty on machine-learned relevance scores to downrank notifications similar to recently sent ones across semantic dimensions such as content type, author, and product surface. This re-ranking reduces the volume of redundant notifications while maintaining high engagement potential, enabling a more varied and satisfying notification mix. Constraints include tuning penalty strengths to balance diversity and relevance dynamically, with future plans to incorporate adaptive strategies based on delivery timing and volume, as well as leveraging large language models to semantically enrich notifications. The expected outcome is decreased redundant notification delivery, higher user engagement rates, and a more balanced, personalized, and less spammy notification experience.

This use case addresses the challenge in e-commerce of accurately describing product attributes across massive catalogs, where manual labeling is costly and error-prone, and large vision-language models (VLMs) are expensive to fine-tune at scale. Intended for e-commerce platform engineers and AI researchers, the proposed solution employs compact VLMs (2–3 billion parameters) and a label-efficient, semi-supervised fine-tuning method combining Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) on a small labeled dataset with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) on much larger unlabeled datasets. This approach involves generating multiple reasoning chains per product, applying self-consistency to identify preferred attribute predictions, and fine-tuning models to prefer these outputs, enabling iterative self-improvement without reinforcing biases seen in simpler self-learning. Tested across twelve e-commerce verticals, this method significantly boosts attribute prediction accuracy (e.g., lifting Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct model accuracy from 75.1% to 85.7%) while reducing labeling costs and accelerating cataloging, thereby enhancing product listings, search relevance, and recommendation quality.

LinkedIn addresses the business problem of scaling and enhancing personalized, adaptive AI-powered recruitment and member support by developing generative AI agents—autonomous or semi-autonomous systems leveraging large language models (LLMs) that reason, plan, and interact dynamically with users and systems under a human-in-the-loop (HITL) framework for control and trust. Intended users include recruiters and members engaging in complex workflows across LinkedIn’s platform. The solution involves a modular multi-agent architecture defined and registered via gRPC schemas and orchestrated through LinkedIn’s messaging infrastructure to ensure scalability, resilience, and flexible parallel task execution while supporting asynchronous, synchronous, and incremental communication streams. Critical data considerations include context engineering with memory and knowledge graphs for personalized responsiveness, strict privacy and security controls with compartmentalized experiential memory, and observability implemented through tools like LangSmith in pre-production and OpenTelemetry in production for continuous monitoring and improvement. Developer tooling such as a Playground enables rapid prototyping and testing, while adopting open protocols like MCP and A2A fosters interoperability in diverse agent ecosystems. The expected outcome is a robust, scalable, and extensible AI agent platform that delivers proactive, personalized, and trustworthy experiences at scale across LinkedIn’s services.

LinkedIn’s Hiring Assistant addresses the challenge recruiters face in managing high-volume, pattern-intensive sourcing, evaluation, and engagement tasks by offering an AI agent that combines large-scale asynchronous execution, real-time conversational interfaces, and continuous learning from recruiter behavior to automate and scale recruiting workflows across over 1.2 billion candidate profiles. Targeted at professional recruiters, the solution uses a plan-and-execute architecture featuring a central supervisor agent and specialized sub-agents for intake, sourcing, evaluation, outreach, screening, learning, and cognitive memory, all integrated via LinkedIn’s agent platform, SDK, and GraphQL APIs to provide a dynamic, transparent, and trustworthy agentic user experience blending interactive dialogue with autonomous background task execution. Leveraging LinkedIn’s Economic Graph and fine-tuned LLMs, Hiring Assistant continuously refines sourcing queries and candidate evaluations, adapts to recruiter preferences through explicit feedback and implicit activity signals, and maintains strict product policies and human alignment to ensure reliable, compliant, and high-quality hiring recommendations, ultimately freeing recruiters to focus on high-value human interactions while improving candidate discovery and hiring outcomes at enterprise scale.

The business problem addressed by AUSPEX is the complex, time-consuming, and resource-intensive nature of threat modeling for cybersecurity, especially within critical infrastructures such as banking systems, where expertise requirements and lack of standardization hinder efficiency and scalability. Intended for cybersecurity practitioners and threat modelers, AUSPEX offers a generative AI-based copilot that uses a novel "tradecraft prompting" technique to encode expert threat modeling knowledge into prompt chains, enabling a lightweight, modular, and extensible system. It ingests multimodal system representations (architecture diagrams, textual descriptions, or system records) and produces detailed threat matrices that classify threat scenarios by frameworks like STRIDE and CIA Triad, with mappings to mitigations, all generated rapidly without fine-tuning or agents. AUSPEX’s design accommodates various cybersecurity frameworks and roles, fostering early and continual threat modeling integration within development lifecycles. Evaluated on real banking systems with expert feedback, AUSPEX generated clear, realistic, and useful threat models, substantially enhancing the threat modeling experience, reducing manual effort from weeks to minutes, and addressing key limitations such as complexity, expertise shortage, standardization gaps, updating challenges, integration deficits, and limited scope.

DoorDash addressed the challenge of scaling and updating its support chatbot’s knowledge base amid growing marketplace complexity by developing a semantic retrieval system that leverages clustering algorithms and large language models (LLMs) on user-generated content (UGC). Intended for customer support agents and content specialists, the solution involves embedding and clustering thousands of anonymized escalated chat transcripts to identify high-impact knowledge gaps, which are then classified and drafted into knowledge base articles automatically by LLMs. Human reviewers validate and refine these drafts to capture policy nuances and edge cases, ensuring quality and compliance. The finalized articles feed a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) layer integrated with the chatbot, enabling precise matching of user issues to relevant content, significantly reducing escalation rates and improving response accuracy. Consistency in embedding models and prompt design between pipeline stages maintains retrieval reliability, while ongoing offline and online testing guides iterative improvements, thus enhancing customer satisfaction and operational efficiency in support at scale.

Salesforce’s use case with Agentforce addresses the business problem of improving sales productivity and customer service by augmenting human agents with AI agents capable of handling routine and volume-intensive tasks such as lead qualification and support requests. Intended users include sales development representatives, customer service agents, and employees across the organization who interact with AI agents integrated into familiar tools like Slack and CRM systems. The proposed solution involves deploying AI agents that are goal-driven—told what to achieve rather than how to achieve it—and continuously refined through real user feedback, rigorous data governance, and consolidation to ensure data fidelity, avoiding contradictions that could degrade agent performance. Constraints include balancing human-AI collaboration by allowing agents to handle repetitive inquiries while humans manage complex, relationship-driven interactions, and designing consumer-grade, seamless experiences embedded within workflows. Expected outcomes are substantial gains in efficiency and ROI, such as freeing 500,000 work hours, generating $1.7 million in new sales pipeline from dormant leads, and handling the majority of 1.5 million support cases autonomously, ultimately enabling Salesforce to serve as “Customer Zero” for AI agent deployment and guide others in agentic enterprise transformation.

Duolingo addressed the challenge of extensive manual regression testing required to ensure quality in their rapidly iterating language-learning app by deploying AI-driven automation using MobileBoost's GPT Driver, a tool that executes natural language test instructions on virtual devices. Intended for the QA team, the solution enables non-coding members to define test goals like progressing through screens until a condition is met, allowing GPT to creatively navigate UI variants and A/B test branches inherent to Duolingo's complex user flows. This semantic, goal-oriented prompting overcomes the brittleness of scripted tests under frequent UI changes, though it may miss subtle bugs that do not impede flow. Recorded AI-driven test executions allow quick review, transforming hours of manual regression testing into minutes and reducing effort by 70%. Constraints include GPT's occasional misinterpretations, complex interactions with nuanced content, and the need for human-in-the-loop validation, but overall the approach enhances QA productivity, freeing the team to focus on high-value tasks like bug fixing and feature testing.

Cubic faced a business problem where their AI code review agent produced excessive low-value, noisy comments, causing developers to lose trust and overlook important feedback. Intended users were software developers relying on AI-assisted pull request (PR) reviews. Their solution involved architectural redesign featuring explicit reasoning logs that made the AI's decision process transparent and debuggable, reducing arbitrary suggestions; a streamlined set of essential tooling minimizing confusion from overly complex analyses; and a modular system of specialized micro-agents each focused on distinct review tasks such as security, duplication, or editorial checks, enhancing precision and context efficiency. The approach was validated on hundreds of real PRs, achieving a 51% reduction in false positives and halving the number of comments per PR, which improved developer trust, engagement, and review effectiveness by emphasizing genuinely critical issues.

HubSpot faced the business challenge of scaling AI coding tool adoption across its diverse engineering teams to improve software development productivity while managing risk and skepticism. The intended users were engineers at all experience levels within HubSpot's product, UX, and engineering groups. The proposed solution involved a strategic rollout starting with a pilot of GitHub Copilot supported by executive buy-in, extensive enablement, and quantitative measurement of performance impacts; followed by the creation of a central Developer Experience AI team to drive adoption, customize AI tool integration for HubSpot’s specific technology stack, advocate internally, streamline procurement, and develop evaluation capabilities. Important constraints included managing cost, security compliance, and cautious incremental rollout with guardrails to monitor production incidents and code quality. The expected outcomes included substantive productivity gains, broad organizational adoption surpassing 90%, normalized AI fluency as a job requisite, and a foundation for more advanced AI-driven development workflows and tools, ultimately embedding AI deeply into HubSpot’s engineering culture and processes.

Pinterest faces a business problem of fragmented observability (o11y) data—logs, metrics, traces, and change events are siloed across separate systems developed before OpenTelemetry (OTel) standards, causing inefficiencies and steep learning curves for engineers conducting root cause analysis. The intended users are Pinterest engineers who need unified, contextual insights to quickly diagnose system anomalies and alerts. The proposed solution leverages AI agents integrated via a centralized Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which unifies disparate observability signals into a cohesive, context-rich stream accessible under fine-grained control; this MCP server enables plug-and-play tooling for AI agents to query logs, metrics, traces, changefeed events, alerts, and dependency graphs without requiring a costly infrastructure overhaul. Key data constraints include the massive volume of observability data—billions of data points and terabytes daily—necessitating context window management strategies such as link generation for dashboards and stepwise querying guided by detailed tool metadata. The expected outcome is accelerated, clearer root-cause analysis and actionable recommendations delivered through an AI-powered agent called Tricorder, which streamlines the troubleshooting process, reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR), and opens new avenues for autonomous observability and agentic tooling across Pinterest teams.

Amazon and Audible addressed the challenge of simplifying book discovery for millions of customers searching across multiple book formats by developing a low-latency, ML-powered visual autocomplete system that provides instant, personalized search suggestions with book cover previews and direct navigation to relevant product or author pages. Leveraging historical search data and real-time intent detection, Audible uses a deep pairwise-learning-to-rank (DeepPLTR) model with specialized towers capturing contextual features, user engagement, and customer preferences to rank books, while Amazon employs a two-stage approach combining a probabilistic information-retrieval model and a format-personalization model to recommend the most relevant book title and format. This semantic retrieval solution minimizes search steps by displaying visual widgets tailored to detected user intent, offering connections to related series and author collections, ultimately enhancing the speed and relevance of book discovery within Amazon’s ecosystem.

Shopify built a high-performance, scalable product search engine to balance rapid machine learning innovation with millisecond latency at global commerce scale, addressing the challenge of serving billions of queries during peak events like Black Friday. Intended for data scientists and engineers managing millions of merchants, the solution integrates classical IR techniques with advanced ML models—including transformers, neural rankers, and gradient boosting—running atop RankFlow, a domain-specific language that offers Python-like ease with C++ execution speed. This architecture supports real-time indexing, multi-language, privacy, and merchant-specific relevance customization, enabling fast ranking experimentation and deployment on billions of historical queries while maintaining predictable latency and memory efficiency crucial for a massive multi-tenant environment. Automated performance analytics ensure continuous improvements without production regressions, ultimately optimizing search results for purchase intent, brand trust, and conversion within Shopify’s complex commerce ecosystem.

Ramp developed a suite of large language model (LLM)-backed agents to automate expense management by handling tasks like expense approvals, traditionally managed by human finance managers. Targeting finance teams who face tedious, low-risk decision-making processes, the solution employs a "policy agent" that matches or exceeds human judgment while building trust through transparent reasoning, direct citations of relevant expense policies, and deferring to human review when uncertain. Key constraints include preventing hallucinations by grounding outputs in verifiable input data, avoiding forced answers via explicit uncertainty categories, and offering customizable autonomy levels through a workflow builder that enforces guardrails like dollar limits and vendor blocks. The collaborative context refinement and progressive autonomy—from suggesting actions to fully autonomous decisions—help establish confidence and improve policy accuracy over time. Evaluations against expert-defined golden datasets ensure objective quality control beyond user feedback, aiming to create economically valuable, trustworthy AI agents that transform finance team operations.

The use case addresses the challenge of integrating large language model (LLM)-driven "vibe coding"—where developers use natural language prompts to generate code—with quality engineering practices in enterprise software development. Intended users are software engineers and product teams at ASOS experimenting with AI-enhanced development. The proposed solution, Test-Driven Vibe Development (TDVD), restructures traditional vibe coding by embedding mature test-first methodologies such as architecture-driven testing, ATDD, BDD, and TDD into the AI coding workflow, prompting clear, testable requirements before code generation. This approach counters LLM limitations like hallucinations and attention diffusion by breaking development into smaller atomic tasks aligned with expected behavior defined upfront, enabling continuous validation and early defect detection. In a real-world trial developing a stock discrepancy reporting tool under resource constraints, TDVD accelerated MVP delivery by 7–10 times compared to conventional estimates while improving quality and enabling rapid upskilling in unfamiliar tech stacks. The expected outcome is a disciplined yet flexible AI-augmented software development lifecycle that enhances code quality, reduces costly late defect fixes, and supports rapid, iterative product delivery despite inherent LLM constraints and infrastructure challenges.

DoorDash addresses the cold start problem of recommending grocery and convenience items to consumers new to those verticals by inferring preferences from their restaurant order histories using large language models (LLMs). The solution targets active DoorDash users and employs a scalable, multi-step pipeline that first compresses user restaurant data into cleaned and normalized tagsets representing dishes, cuisines, and dietary attributes. Offline, LLMs map these tagsets to grocery taxonomies using retrieval augmented generation (RAG) to reduce context size and hallucinations, creating reusable mappings efficiently at scale. Online, personalized scoring combines frequency and recency of tagsets with LLM relevance scores to generate grocery taxonomy preferences, which are then integrated with multi-stage retrieval and deep learning ranking models (including two-tower embeddings and multi-task MMoE) to deliver timely, relevant grocery recommendations. Continuous validation incorporates LLM-based judging of mappings and evaluation via key business metrics like conversion and order rates, demonstrating significant improvements in cross-vertical recommendation quality while controlling inference costs and maintaining high signal quality.

Grab faced the business problem of overwhelmed ML Platform team support channels inundated with repetitive queries, leading to inefficient use of on-call engineers' time. The intended users were Grab employees ("Grabbers") needing quick, secure, and accessible AI-assisted answers. The initial solution of building a chatbot leveraging GPT-3.5-turbo for semantic retrieval of platform documentation was limited by token constraints and insufficient embedding search quality, resulting in failure. Pivoting, an internal ChatGPT-like tool named GrabGPT was developed rapidly using Grab’s own model-serving platform, supporting multiple LLM providers and integrated with Google authentication to ensure secure, auditable, and globally accessible interactions within Grab’s private infrastructure. The expected outcome was a widely adopted AI assistant that reduced support burdens, enhanced productivity, and fostered company-wide LLM adoption, culminating in thousands of active daily users and catalyzing Grab’s broader LLM strategy.

IBM Research addressed the challenge that non-expert users struggle to realize productivity gains from generative AI by developing AI agents capable of complex problem-solving through Retrieval-Augmented Generation and dynamic tool interaction using open-source Llama 3–70B-Chat. Targeting everyday builders, particularly TypeScript developers, they created the BeeAI Framework—a flexible, open-source agent development library with innovative features like trajectory exploration to enhance transparency and trust. Key insights included the importance of explainable reasoning aligned with user expectations, security challenges from agent-environment interactions, enforceable business rules beyond prompting, and the need to tailor multi-agent architectures to specific use cases via orchestration workflows. The solution emphasized a clean developer experience, iterative community-driven refinement, and rigorous custom evaluation methods analyzing both outputs and reasoning processes, with aims to expand usability (including Python support) and interaction paradigms to accelerate adoption and production readiness in the evolving AI agent space.

Harvey addresses the complex, iterative nature of legal research—characterized by multi-source queries requiring back-and-forth reasoning—by implementing an agentic search system that goes beyond conventional one-shot retrieval. Intended for legal professionals conducting nuanced due diligence and jurisdiction-specific analyses, this system dynamically plans search strategies, selects relevant knowledge sources, evaluates information sufficiency, and iteratively refines queries while synthesizing findings with precise citations to statutes, case law, and internal documents. Leveraging Retrieval Augmented Generation enhanced with reasoning, the agent overcomes challenges such as implicit source selection, scaling retrieval efforts to query complexity, and multi-source citation integration. Continuous improvements are driven by privacy-preserving evaluation workflows involving expert legal researchers who generate realistic evaluation queries and feedback, enabling the system to improve tool selection precision from near zero to 0.8-0.9 and dynamically adjust retrieval complexity. The expected outcome is a more accurate, context-aware legal research assistant that produces citation-backed, comprehensive answers reflecting up-to-date and jurisdiction-specific legal standards, ultimately enhancing efficiency and reliability in legal intelligence.

DoorDash’s fraud team developed a scalable anomaly detection platform to proactively identify emerging fraud trends by analyzing daily aggregated metrics—such as refund claims and chargeback scores—across millions of multi-dimensional user segments defined by combinations of dimensions like customer country and business name. Employing a moving-window z-score algorithm on 28-day time series data, the system flags statistically and business-significantly anomalous segments that indicate growing fraudulent behavior before it impacts top-line metrics. Hierarchical clustering groups overlapping anomalous segments into clusters, reducing investigation volume, while operations teams use a workflow tool to review representative segments and sample transactions for early root-cause analysis and containment. This platform, running daily batch jobs coordinated by Airflow and leveraging fast in-memory DBMS like DuckDB for efficient aggregation, has reduced fraud detection time from over 100 to under 3 days, saving DoorDash tens of millions annually by catching subtle but growing fraud patterns early. Future enhancements include cross-day clustering to avoid redundant investigations and AI-assisted automation of investigations, expanding anomaly detection beyond fraud to other business areas such as growth and payments.

SpellVault addresses the business problem of democratizing AI by enabling non-technical users at Grab to build, manage, and evolve AI-powered applications seamlessly integrated with diverse internal and external data sources. Initially a no-code platform leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and basic plugins for LLM app creation, it evolved to support advanced agentic capabilities by incorporating dynamic tool invocation, a graph-based executor for complex reasoning and action, and extensive plugin ecosystems including Native and Community Built Tools. Essential data inputs include real-time knowledge vaults, external APIs, and internal systems like Slack and Kibana, with constraints focusing on trustworthiness, up-to-date data, and user customization without coding requirements. Users access SpellVault apps via web, Slack, and APIs, facilitating millions of productivity and automation use cases internally, with the platform’s transition to an MCP-compliant service enabling interoperability within the broader agentic AI ecosystem. The expected outcome is an accessible, adaptable AI platform transforming from static LLM app generation towards intelligent AI agents capable of autonomous reasoning and dynamic interaction across organizational workflows.

DoorDash addresses the challenge of delivering highly personalized homepage store recommendations for millions of users by replacing a heuristic food knowledge graph-based system with a generative AI-powered pipeline that leverages large language models (LLMs) to create unique carousel titles and associated metadata based on detailed consumer profiles, including cuisine and dish preferences contextualized by time of day. This solution overcomes limitations of static, overly broad carousels and inaccurate tagging by dynamically generating diverse, relevant, and moderated content, embedding carousel queries and merchant profiles into a shared vector space for exact k-nearest neighbors retrieval of relevant stores and dishes within delivery areas, followed by a ranking approach combining engagement signals and embedding similarity to optimize presentation. The system, designed for scalability and cost-effectiveness with batch LLM calls and GPU-accelerated retrieval, is evaluated both offline by user panels and labelers and validated via A/B testing, yielding significant improvements in click-through, conversion, and exploration of merchants, thereby enhancing user engagement and SMB merchant exposure on the DoorDash platform.

The business problem addressed by OLX is improving search relevance and recall in a multilingual, user-generated classifieds marketplace, where traditional keyword matching often yielded low recall and zero-results pages due to query vagueness, misspellings, and inconsistent listing descriptions. Intended users include marketplace buyers searching across languages and sellers seeking visibility. The proposed solution is a Hybrid Search combining keyword-based retrieval (using SOLR/BM25) with semantic vector search via embeddings generated by multilingual models (mCLIP and multilingual-e5-small), integrating results into a unified recall set capped at 1,000 ads and re-ranked using a Learning to Rank (LTR) model enhanced to incorporate vector similarity features. Initial experiments inserting semantic search into fallback chains showed doubling of user-seller contacts, and subsequent A/B testing of full Hybrid Search flows demonstrated consistent improvements in successful user interactions and ad engagement across mobile and web platforms, thereby reducing zero-results pages and increasing recall. Constraints included multilingual support with a single model across markets, limited embedding context lengths, and balancing ranking for paid ads (VAS). Expected outcomes were increased recall, reduced ZRPs, improved user engagement metrics, and a scalable search solution refined by ongoing embedding and ranking model enhancements.

The New York Times addressed the business challenge of optimizing its digital subscription funnel, which involves decisions about showing registration walls, paywalls, or granting content access to unregistered and registered users, balancing multiple competing KPIs such as subscription rate, registration rate, engagement, bounce rate, and SEO impact. Intended users include non-subscribers and registered users navigating their content access experience. The proposed solution leverages real-time causal machine learning models trained on continuously collected randomized control trial data to predict the outcomes of different access-control actions and select the optimal one through multi-objective optimization subject to business constraints. These models use an S-Learner framework to estimate causal effects of actions with respect to user and content features and adjust weights daily to dynamically tune the tradeoff between KPIs in real time, enabling millisecond decision-making on content gating. Expected outcomes include increased subscription and registration rates while maintaining target rates for showing paywalls or registration walls, improved user engagement, and adherence to business rules, all supported by ongoing performance monitoring against randomized baselines and A/B testing.

Ramp Research addresses the data bottleneck at Ramp by serving as an AI-powered agentic data analyst accessible via Slack, designed to answer thousands of data-related questions in minutes rather than hours, thus accelerating decision-making and reducing reliance on overburdened human analysts. Intended for Ramp’s internal teams across business domains, the solution integrates and indexes contextual metadata from sources like dbt, Looker, and Snowflake, combining this with domain experts' technical documentation to ensure expert-level understanding. Employing a sophisticated agentic approach that inspects data at the column and row levels while enabling reasoning similar to human analysts, Ramp Research supports stateful, threaded Slack interactions with features such as CSV previews for non-technical users and seamless workflow integration. A Python mini-framework for automated end-to-end testing of queries and intermediate reasoning steps enables continuous improvement of the agent’s context and accuracy. The outcome is a 10-20x increase in question volume, faster hypothesis validation, improved decision quality across many business functions, and empowered teams that can now automate workflows like fraud detection and case study generation, thus enhancing operational efficiency and customer value.

This use case addresses the problem of SNAP benefit interruptions or "program churn," which affects around 200,000 monthly users due to eligibility renewal issues like missed periodic reports or recertifications, causing food insecurity and increasing state agency workload. Propel leverages AI semantic retrieval and generation capabilities to help SNAP recipients self-diagnose the cause of missing electronic benefit transfers, understand complex agency notices, and receive targeted guidance on corrective actions—such as submitting a late report rather than reapplying—thus reducing recovery time and unnecessary agency calls. Two AI-driven solutions were tested: a multi-step triage flow code-generated via AI to identify likely issues and streamline user navigation (piloted in California), and a nationwide AI chat assistant that provides state-specific, context-aware, and multilingual support using generative AI integrated with a knowledge base. These pilots demonstrated strong user engagement, quicker benefit restoration, and reduced program churn, showcasing AI's potential to improve benefits navigation by dynamically interpreting user input, adapting to language shifts, and personalizing support, thereby easing digital access challenges and administrative burden for both recipients and agencies.

The use case addresses the challenge faced by Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams in diagnosing production incidents in cloud-native applications by developing an autonomous SRE agent leveraging Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) with FastMCP. Intended for SRE teams, the agent integrates a layered architecture consisting of a Large Language Model (LLM) as the reasoning brain, an MCP client for executing commands, and MCP servers interfacing with Kubernetes, GitHub, and Slack to automate diagnosis workflows. The system detects errors like HTTP 500 crashes via AWS CloudWatch, retrieves relevant Kubernetes pod logs and source files from GitHub, and posts diagnostic summaries and remediation recommendations in Slack. Constraints involve managing token usage and costs through caching and tool filtering, enforcing timeouts, and ensuring autonomous yet controlled agent operation. Expected outcomes include faster, more accurate incident triage with reduced manual effort, improved infrastructure monitoring, and a framework for further research on effectiveness, security, and cost-efficiency in deploying agentic AI for real-world cloud operations.

Booking.com addresses the challenge of slow, manual partner responses to guest inquiries, which can delay communication and risk cancellations, by developing a scalable Generative AI agent integrated into their messaging platform. Intended for accommodation partners, this system uses semantic retrieval via MiniLM embeddings stored in a Weaviate vector database to select relevant response templates, augmented by tools querying property and reservation data with GraphQL, enabling the agent to autonomously decide whether to suggest predefined templates, generate custom replies using GPT-4 Mini, or abstain for sensitive topics under strict guardrails that redact PII and enforce safety policies. The solution emphasizes multi-language support, real-time template updates via Kafka, and human-in-the-loop oversight to balance accuracy and trust. Continuous evaluation through manual review, LLM-based automated judgments, and operational monitoring with Arize ensures high-quality, context-aware, and timely responses, resulting in significant increases in user satisfaction, consistency, and efficiency in partner-guest communication while preparing for future enhancements like deeper operational assistance and personalized tone adaptation.

This use case addresses the challenge of managing nondeterministic outputs from large language models (LLMs) when building an AI agent for DevOps tasks, specifically root cause analysis (RCA) of flaky test failures in continuous integration (CI). Intended users include software engineers and developers working on CI/DevOps workflows who require reliable, actionable summaries of test failures to improve developer experience. The proposed solution emphasizes starting with a narrow, well-defined use case supported by rich historical failure data, applying adapted software engineering principles to create tight feedback loops, and incrementally improving the agent through rigorous input/output validation, mocking, and user feedback integration. Constraints include handling the context window limits of LLMs, the inherent black-box and inconsistent behavior of models, and the need for deterministic, concise outputs that facilitate automation without overwhelming verbosity. Expected outcomes are more dependable agent outputs that reduce manual triage effort, produce measurable incremental improvements over time, support internal dogfooding for rapid iteration, and ultimately enhance productivity by enabling partial automation in CI failure diagnosis.

Zalando faced inefficiencies and inconsistencies stemming from two distinct in-house UI component libraries used across partner-facing B2B applications, leading to increased maintenance overhead and developer onboarding challenges. To address this, their engineering team aimed to migrate all applications from one UI library to the other, tackling the complex code transformation required for 15 sophisticated applications. They explored using Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly GPT-4o, to automate code migration by iteratively refining prompts that combined source code, detailed component interfaces, explicit transformation mappings, and carefully verified examples. Their Python-based migration tool, enhanced by system prompts and prompt engineering best practices, processed source files while managing token limits, output formatting, and caching to optimize accuracy and cost (under $40 per repo). The LLM-powered approach achieved approximately 90% accuracy, significantly accelerating development compared to traditional codemods, although human oversight was essential due to LLM limitations like occasional unreliable outputs, lack of visual layout understanding, and complex manual adjustments for test suites and design differences. This iterative, example-driven semantic retrieval and transformation process improved code comprehension and contextual awareness, demonstrating a viable, cost-effective AI solution for large-scale UI component migration while providing insights for future applications.

Coinbase addresses the business problem of improving decision quality and speed within its RAPID framework by developing RAPID-D, an AI-powered decision support system used by internal stakeholders involved in critical decisions. RAPID-D leverages specialized multi-agent architectures—including an Analyst agent for baseline recommendations, a Seeker agent that retrieves context from enterprise knowledge bases, a Devil's Advocate agent to identify risks and biases, and a Synthesizer agent to integrate findings into comprehensive, explainable recommendations—all designed to systematically uncover unseen risks, mitigate cognitive biases, and enhance transparency and auditability. The system processes structured RAPID documents containing roles, recommendations, and stakeholder inputs, continuously adapting through real-time user feedback to improve accuracy and relevance. The outcome is a transparent, reproducible, and AI-augmented decision-making process that supports human Deciders in making smarter, faster business decisions aligned with Coinbase’s mission to innovate operational excellence.

Amazon addresses the escalating sophistication of cyber threats by deploying Autonomous Threat Analysis (ATA), an AI-driven security system designed for cybersecurity professionals to anticipate and counteract adversarial tactics. ATA employs agentic AI with red-team agents simulating attacker methods and blue-team agents validating and improving detection rules through adversarial multiagent reinforcement learning. Operating in isolated environments mimicking real infrastructure, ATA executes and tests real commands, generating verifiable telemetry to eliminate AI hallucinations. Notably, in tackling Python-based reverse shell threats, ATA autonomously generated diverse technique variants, producing detection rules with perfect precision and recall validated against production audit data. This approach reduces manual testing cycles from weeks to hours, scales across concurrent tests, and balances automation with human oversight, enhancing proactive threat detection, reducing false positives, and fortifying Amazon’s cybersecurity posture against evolving attack vectors.

Coinbase addresses product quality assurance challenges faced by manual and flaky test automation by deploying a Quality Assurance AI agent (qa-ai-agent) that processes natural language test requests to autonomously perform and validate tests using visual and textual web data, eliminating the need for code-based test scripts. Intended for developers and QA teams, this solution leverages an open-source LLM browser agent, gRPC/WebSocket connectivity, MongoDB for persistence, and BrowserStack for cross-environment automation. Benchmarked against human testers via A/B testing, qa-ai-agent achieves 75% accuracy—slightly below human level—while detecting thrice as many bugs, enabling rapid test creation (minutes to 1.5 hours), and reducing costs by 86%. LLMs are also deployed to judge bug validity via confidence scoring to filter false positives. Currently running 40 test scenarios integrated with developer workflows (Slack, JIRA), the AI agent identifies roughly 10 issues weekly and is on track to replace 75% of manual tests, greatly enhancing scalability, cost-effectiveness, and reliability in functional, localization, compliance, and UI/UX testing domains.

Dash addresses the challenge of evolving from traditional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) search to an agentic AI capable of interpreting, summarizing, and acting on information by employing context engineering to optimize the model’s reasoning and decision-making. Intended for knowledge workers who require precise, actionable insights across enterprise data sources, Dash consolidates multiple retrieval tools into a single universal search index augmented by a knowledge graph that filters and ranks only relevant context, reducing noise and token usage within the model’s context window. To mitigate complexity and analysis paralysis caused by numerous capabilities, Dash implements specialized agents for complex tasks like query construction, allowing the main planning agent to focus on task execution with minimal but highly pertinent context. This approach enhances accuracy, efficiency, and scalability in workspace AI applications by balancing context richness with resource constraints, ultimately enabling smarter, faster, and cost-effective agentic workflows.

Orbital Copilot addresses the real estate legal sector’s need to efficiently analyze and interpret complex, voluminous legal documents by providing an AI Agent that mimics a lawyer’s reasoning process for due diligence tasks. Designed for legal professionals at prestigious law firms, this solution leverages advanced Large Language Models combined with autonomous agent capabilities—planning, memory, and tool use—to parse multiple documents, track definitions, cross-reference data, and transparently explain its conclusions while supporting queries ranging from simple facts to complex lease variations. Operating under constraints such as high computational costs, limited token throughput, and service reliability challenges, Orbital Copilot achieves up to 70% time savings on lease reporting, dramatically enhancing productivity and precision in real estate legal workflows, and is expanding from the UK into US and global markets.

Netflix addresses the complexity and resource intensity of maintaining multiple personalized recommendation models by developing a centralized Foundation Model trained on extensive user interaction and content data to learn member preferences at scale. Intended for Netflix application teams with diverse latency, technology, and adaptation needs, the integration strategies include generating user and item embeddings updated daily and served via an Embedding Store for low-latency feature consumption; embedding the Foundation Model as a subgraph within downstream models to enable end-to-end fine-tuning and avoid staleness at the expense of increased inference cost and complexity; and fine-tuning the entire Foundation Model directly on product-specific data to optimize for particular recommendations. These approaches balance trade-offs among computational cost, latency, freshness, and customization, with infrastructure built to stabilize embeddings across retraining and support near-real-time updates, ultimately enhancing personalization effectiveness and adaptability across Netflix’s recommendation systems.

Harvey faced the business problem of scaling development for its AI Assistant, which integrates multiple specialized capabilities like tax law retrieval, document drafting, and external tools (e.g., LexisNexis) to perform complex, open-ended tasks for users such as legal professionals. The intended users were engineering teams needing to build and integrate diverse features without bottlenecks. The proposed solution was adopting a unified agent framework that modularizes capabilities into "Tool Bundles," each packaging multiple related tools with instructions, enabling decentralized development while maintaining interoperability through a common system prompt. Critical constraints included avoiding bespoke orchestration to prevent maintenance complexity, managing conflicts between system prompts and Tool Bundles, and preventing context degradation. To ensure reliability, Harvey implemented eval gates requiring leave-one-out testing of any prompt or Tool Bundle changes against benchmark datasets to detect regressions. The expected outcome was accelerated, scalable feature development across multiple teams, emergent integrations of capabilities, and maintained or improved AI output quality within a centralized yet collaboratively owned agent system.

Stack Overflow addressed the challenge of improving new user question quality and reducing repetitive reviewer feedback by developing Question Assistant, a semantic retrieval solution combining traditional machine learning with generative AI. Targeting question askers, especially novices, the system uses logistic regression models trained on labeled feedback indicators—such as problem definition and error details—derived from clustering reviewer comments to detect specific quality issues in question drafts. When a model flags a deficiency, the flagged question and relevant prompts are fed to an LLM (Google’s Gemini) to generate tailored, actionable feedback rather than generic quality scores, overcoming limitations of direct LLM quality rating due to subjectivity and poor inter-rater consistency. Deployed initially in staged A/B testing, the solution delivered a significant +12% success rate increase in questions staying open and receiving positive engagement, demonstrating value in enhancing question clarity and usefulness rather than reducing review time or approval rates. Hosted in Azure with integrated telemetry for iterative improvement, this hybrid ML-AI approach advances Stack Overflow’s core Q&A workflows by systematically guiding askers to better-formulated questions that facilitate knowledge discovery.

Amazon improves the completeness, accuracy, and appeal of its massive online product catalogue by using large language models (LLMs) for quality control of product listings, complementing traditional category-specific machine learning models. Targeting product data such as images, titles, descriptions, and attributes, the adaptable LLM approach addresses challenges of nuanced or granular attribute values across millions of diverse products and multiple languages. The solution involves prompt tuning, where LLMs are systematically exposed to organized catalogue attribute schemas and value distributions to capture correct attribute usage and maintain granularity without losing specificity. This process also enhances representation consistency and error detection, enabling faster incorporation of seller updates and broadening multilingual coverage while significantly reducing manual review effort. The outcome is scalable, generalizable semantic retrieval and correction of product attributes that improve shopper experience and catalogue quality at Amazon’s global scale.

LinkedIn addressed the bottleneck where data experts spent excessive time assisting colleagues in accessing enterprise data by developing SQL Bot, an AI-powered text-to-SQL assistant integrated into their DARWIN data science platform, enabling employees across functions to independently retrieve insights with proper access control. The solution leverages embedding-based semantic retrieval enhanced by certified table metadata and user-personalized dataset inference, coupled with a knowledge graph to inform LLM-based ranking, query generation, and self-correction agents that iteratively construct and validate SQL queries. User experience improvements include chat-based interaction with intent classification, conversational follow-ups, rich visual elements, and seamless integration facilitating adoption, while customization options allow users to tailor dataset scopes, supply custom instructions, and add example queries. The system is continuously benchmarked using a comprehensive, multi-answer dataset with human and LLM evaluation to optimize recall, accuracy, and efficiency, resulting in high user satisfaction and significant time savings in query debugging.

GitLab addresses the challenge of reliably integrating large language models (LLMs) into its DevSecOps platform by developing GitLab Duo, an AI suite requiring rigorous validation and testing at scale to ensure quality and robustness. Targeting DevSecOps teams and software developers as end users, GitLab’s solution includes a Centralized Evaluation Framework (CEF) that utilizes a comprehensive, custom-designed prompt library tailored to GitLab-specific use cases, simulating diverse, production-relevant queries with ground truth answers to benchmark multiple foundational models from providers like Google and Anthropic. This large-scale evaluation employs metrics such as Cosine Similarity and LLM Judge scoring to compare outputs and select the best models, while iterative experiments guided by performance patterns refine prompts and features, validated daily to avoid unintended regressions. The approach emphasizes transparency, non-reliance on customer data for training, and ongoing adaptation to optimize AI-powered code suggestions, chatbots, and vulnerability analysis within GitLab Duo, ultimately delivering trustworthy, continuously improving AI capabilities that accelerate software development workflows.

GitLab developed GitLab Duo, an AI-powered suite integrated into their DevSecOps workflows to address inefficiencies and manual effort in software development, targeting a wide range of users from engineers to technical writers and product managers.
