By embedding features like Code Suggestions, Chat for code explanations, and automated Merge Request Summaries directly into their daily routines, GitLab Duo enhances productivity and streamlines complex tasks such as understanding external projects and generating boilerplate code. The solution leverages continuous feedback and usage metrics via an AI Impact analytics dashboard to iteratively refine these capabilities, aiming to transform internal engineering workflows and demonstrate the potential of generative AI in enterprise software development.

This use case addresses the challenge faced by developers and product teams in rapidly building and deploying generative AI applications using large language models (LLMs) to solve user problems involving large-scale analysis and interpretation of unstructured text where traditional ML is insufficient. Intended users include product managers, AI engineers, and cross-functional teams aiming to innovate with generative AI. The proposed solution outlines a structured process: identifying suitable use cases through empathy and task analysis, defining detailed product requirements balancing latency, complexity, quality, and safety, prototyping with advanced off-the-shelf LLMs (e.g., GPT-4) to validate ideas and refine prompts using AI-assisted evaluation, followed by iterative limited releases focusing on user satisfaction and system health metrics. For scale deployment, the architecture integrates inference servers, safety filters, and monitoring, while considering trade-offs between commercial LLM APIs and self-hosted open-source models (such as Llama and Mistral) to optimize cost, performance, privacy, and engineering effort. The expected outcome is an efficient and user-centric generative AI product that delivers high-quality, safe outputs while balancing operational costs and scalability challenges.

The use case addresses improving multilingual semantic search for deliveryhero.jobs, targeting users seeking job listings across different languages. The business problem is bridging language barriers to enhance search relevance without extensive labeled data. The proposed solution employs few-shot large language model (LLM) translations to semantically align queries and job postings in multiple languages, leveraging LLMs' natural language understanding capabilities with minimal training examples. Important constraints include maintaining translation accuracy and scalability across languages with limited resources. The expected outcome is higher recall and precision in cross-lingual job search, resulting in better user experience and increased engagement from a diverse multilingual audience.

Replit addresses the problem of inefficient bug fixing faced by developers within its IDE by building a specialized large language model (LLM) for code repair that directly integrates with the development environment. Targeting Python projects with Language Server Protocol (LSP) diagnostics—which frequently identify errors but provide fixes in only about 10% of cases—the solution reconstructs project files from logs of operational transformations and session events to create a large training dataset of (code, diagnostic) pairs. Using few-shot prompting and synthetically generated, verified line diffs as training targets, Replit finetunes a 7-billion-parameter code LLM to output precise, line-numbered code edits conforming to a structured schema that enhances response consistency and parseability. The model is trained and evaluated on both public benchmarks (like DebugBench) and a novel dataset of real user errors verified by human annotators, with metrics including exact and functional correctness. Compared to larger, generalist LLMs accessed via APIs, this Replit-native model shows competitive repair capabilities at lower latency and cost, demonstrating promising results in real-world IDE integration and highlighting future directions such as multi-file edits, support for more languages, and user-feedback-driven continual learning.

Coinbase addresses the business challenge of scaling customer support amid surging, diverse inquiries—ranging from account restrictions to product-specific questions—using the Conversational Coinbase Chatbot (CBCB), an LLM-powered semantic retrieval system designed for customer support agents and users alike. The CBCB integrates multi-stage pipelines that semantically retrieve and rank relevant knowledge base articles, utilize real-time account and transaction APIs, apply domain-specific rules, and enforce strict legal, privacy, and compliance guardrails to deliver personalized, accurate, and compliant responses. It processes queries sequentially through components like a query rephraser, article retriever with ML ranking models, response stylizer, and compliance guardrails, ensuring scalability via multi-cloud and multi-LLM strategies to handle high concurrency. The expected outcome is faster, context-aware customer interactions with reduced back-and-forth, enabling human agents to focus on complex issues while maintaining transparency, controllability, and continuous evaluation through A/B testing and manual reviews within Coinbase’s ecosystem.

Twilio Segment addresses the complexity marketers face when building sophisticated customer audiences using an advanced UI that compiles queries into abstract syntax trees (ASTs), which can be represented in multiple equivalent forms. To simplify audience creation via natural language prompts and ensure robust evaluation of generative AI outputs despite the unbounded set of valid answers, they developed an LLM-as-Judge system: leveraging large language models both to generate synthetic prompts from ground truth ASTs and to assess the alignment of generated ASTs against these references. This multi-agent architecture includes a Question Generator to create evaluative prompts, an AST Generator to produce candidate ASTs, and an LLM Judge that scores outputs on a discrete 1–5 scale using chain-of-thought explanations to enhance interpretability and closely mimic human evaluations, achieving over 90% alignment. This approach supports model selection, prompt optimization, and system architecture decisions while ensuring transparent, responsible, and accountable AI use, resulting in a threefold reduction in median audience creation time and high feature retention, thereby empowering marketers to efficiently construct accurate customer segments without dealing with UI or data complexity.

Canva addresses the challenge of preserving semantic meaning in user designs by detecting implicit groups—collections of elements like tables, charts, and diagrams that form cohesive visual units despite varying construction methods—using computer vision. Intended for Canva users who benefit from features such as Magic Layouts and Magic Switch that transform and inspire designs without breaking these semantic units, the solution involves rasterizing design pages and applying a Vision Transformer-based object detection model to identify these immutable implicit groups within sparse, multimodal design images. The approach includes an element-level decoder that maps detected bounding boxes back to design elements using polygon-based overlap for precise assignment. Key constraints include maintaining low latency for real-time user interactions, handling large design dimensions, and optimizing raster image size through JPEG compression and resizing to balance payload size and detection accuracy. Robustness is enhanced through data augmentation techniques, including template-fusion augmentation, ensuring reliable detection across diverse and creative designs. The expected outcome is a seamless, AI-powered design editing experience that respects the integrity of complex design components, enabling intuitive and meaningful design transformations while maintaining performance and global accessibility.

Lyft addresses the business problem of accurately predicting Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) reliability to reduce rider cancellations and improve user experience by providing trustworthy pickup times before a ride is requested. Intended for riders and internal downstream services, the solution employs a tree-based gradient boosting classification model that predicts the probability a driver arrives within a reasonable timeframe around a given ETA estimate. The model ingests diverse data including historical ride events, real-time supply and demand metrics, driver status, geographic features, and ETA brackets, accommodating marketplace dynamics and uncertainties like driver availability, traffic, and GPS volatility. Training involves duplicating rides across all possible ETA values to prevent bias and enable the model to learn complex interactions influencing reliability. Model outputs guide selection of ETA estimates meeting strict reliability SLAs, enhancing ETA accuracy and reducing cancellations. Continuous model monitoring and retraining via Lyft’s ML platform ensure robustness against temporal shifts in patterns, with ongoing efforts to integrate nuanced, market-specific real-time signals for sustained performance improvement.

Tubi, an advertiser-based video-on-demand streaming service, faces the business problem of ensuring the quality and reliability of its recommender system, which is critical for helping viewers discover suitable content. Intended users of the monitoring system include the Machine Learning and Data teams, as well as domain owners responsible for various stages of recommendation delivery. The proposed solution involves comprehensive monitoring of three key data types: input data passed to the model for inference, final recommendation results displayed to users, and the asynchronous model training data that impacts model quality. Key constraints include the need for real-time monitoring of user requests and responses, batch processing for training data, scalability to handle growing data volume and types, and the management of alert precision to avoid alert fatigue. Tubi’s approach leverages flexible, explicit metric definitions via proto structures, user-configurable metric extraction using Scala, Python, or a JSON-path-based DSL, and configuration-driven updates for real-time monitoring jobs without redeployment. This data-centric monitoring pipeline enables timely detection of anomalies caused by upstream data issues, model changes, or feature errors, ultimately ensuring stable recommendation quality and improving operational response through domain ownership and monthly performance summaries.

Binance’s P2P platform addresses the business problem of fraudulent proof of payment (POP) manipulation, which threatens user asset security during peer-to-peer crypto transactions. Intended users are Binance P2P traders who submit payment verification images. The proposed solution leverages AI-based computer vision (CV) models incorporating optical character recognition (OCR), image classification, object detection, and error-level analysis (ELA) to detect subtle visual anomalies—such as altered transaction details, misaligned text, and pixel-level distortions—in POP images in real time. These models cross-verify extracted textual content, image metadata, and trading patterns, while an image encoder supports a vector database for rapid detection of reused or modified POPs through near real-time similar image searches. Despite the complexity posed by over 250,000 daily diverse-format images, this approach aims to safeguard transaction authenticity with minimal disruption to user experience, ultimately reducing fraud risk and enhancing trust in the P2P marketplace.

The AI Data Analyst "QueryAnswerBird" addresses the business problem of enabling non-technical users to perform complex data queries and analysis efficiently. Intended for business analysts and decision-makers, the solution leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combined with Text-to-SQL techniques to interpret natural language questions and convert them into precise SQL queries against structured databases. By integrating semantic retrieval with language models, the system can access relevant data sources dynamically, respecting security constraints and data governance policies. The expected outcome is to democratize data access, improve query accuracy, and accelerate insights generation without requiring deep technical expertise in SQL or data engineering.

LinkedIn addressed the business challenge of delivering personalized, cost-effective AI-driven professional services for its over 1 billion members and 69 million companies by developing domain-adapted foundation models called EON, built upon open-source and third-party language models fine-tuned with LinkedIn Economic Graph data. Intended for recruiters and platform users, EON models use multi-task instruction tuning with reasoning traces and safety alignment techniques such as RLHF to ensure responsible, context-aware generation tailored to professional tasks like candidate-job matching. These models are trained and evaluated via an integrated pipeline supporting modular experimentation and cost-efficiency, with the EON-8B model achieving significant accuracy improvements and cost reductions compared to state-of-the-art models like GPT-4. Deployment in products like the Hiring Assistant automates recruiter workflows by accurately evaluating candidate suitability from diverse data inputs while adhering to LinkedIn's Responsible AI governance, with ongoing enhancements planned to expand multi-turn interactions and agentic capabilities.

ASOS addresses the challenge of personalizing product recommendations from a vast and constantly updating catalog of nearly 50,000 fashion items by leveraging transformer-based machine learning models for semantic retrieval. Intended for fashion-forward customers shopping via app and web, the solution uses self-attention mechanisms to capture nuanced customer style preferences from sequences of past interactions and employs positional awareness to weigh the temporal relevance of these interactions, enabling it to discern evolving tastes and context-specific shopping intents. By replacing traditional models that treat all interactions equally, this transformer-driven recommender enhances product ranking and relevance, resulting in over a 20% improvement in offline evaluation metrics, thereby boosting customer engagement through more precise, contextually aware fashion recommendations.

Data Analysts at Grab face inefficiency from repeatedly running similar data queries to respond to stakeholder requests. To address this, the Integrity Analytics team developed an integrated Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-powered Large Language Model (LLM) solution that leverages Data-Arks, a Python-based API platform hosting frequently used SQL queries and scripts, enabling self-service data retrieval via standardized APIs. Combined with Spellvault, an internal low/no-code platform managing LLM prompts, a scheduling system, and Slack as a messaging interface, the system automates tasks such as generating regular metric reports and conducting fraud investigations by retrieving updated, relevant data and summarizing insights in natural language. This architecture eliminates costly model fine-tuning by dynamically pulling current data, enhancing scalability and responsiveness while saving analysts several hours per report and reducing fraud investigation time from hours to minutes. The solution supports real-time or near-real-time data formatted for accuracy and integrates multiple tools to empower analysts across teams to focus on higher-value activities.

The AI Data Analyst "QueryAnswerBird" addresses the business problem of efficient data discovery for delivery service analysts who need to extract insights rapidly from complex datasets. Intended for data analysts and business intelligence users at Delivery Hero, the solution leverages semantic retrieval powered by AI and machine learning to interpret natural language queries, enabling users to explore data without deep technical expertise. It relies on integrating domain-specific delivery data with secure access constraints, ensuring data privacy and compliance. The expected outcome is improved speed and accuracy in data-driven decision-making by transforming unstructured queries into relevant, context-aware data retrieval, enhancing operational insights across the delivery platform.

Salesforce's Marketing Event Tech team rapidly transformed their homegrown AI assistant for the Salesforce Events app into Ask Astro Agent, an AI-driven event concierge, leveraging Agentforce and Data Cloud's retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) features to enhance semantic retrieval and schedule management for Dreamforce attendees. The solution ingested structured and unstructured event session data via CSV and API pipelines using Mulesoft and Data Cloud, indexing it through hybrid vector and keyword search enriched with augmented indexing for precise domain-specific queries such as speaker names. Configured through Apex code and Salesforce's native tools, the agent managed FAQs, personalized session recommendations, and real-time schedule updates, supported by continuous feedback via Einstein. This allowed rapid iteration and scalable, trusted retrieval grounded in proprietary corporate data, resulting in a feature-rich MVP operational within five days that integrated automated data streaming, knowledge article management, and seamless app embedding aimed at improving user engagement and event experience.

LinkedIn addressed the business challenge of maintaining high-quality, personalized typeahead search suggestions for over a billion members by replacing labor-intensive human evaluations with an automated GenAI-driven quality assessment using an OpenAI GPT model via Azure. Targeted at search engineers and platform quality teams, the solution involved developing precise, unified quality guidelines to handle diverse suggestion types (People, Company, Job, etc.) and personalization effects, constructing a comprehensive golden test set reflecting varied user intents and session behaviors, and engineering specialized prompt templates for the GPT model to score suggestions binary (high or low quality) with reasoning. This semantic retrieval-focused framework enabled rapid, consistent, and scalable evaluation of ranked typeahead suggestions, producing metrics that track suggestion quality over the top ranks and across user sessions. The outcome was a significant improvement in suggestion quality scores (e.g., a 6.8% absolute increase at top 10 suggestions), faster iteration on search relevance experiments, and enhanced user experience through more relevant and actionable search completions.

Pinterest addressed the challenge faced by their data analysts in translating analytical questions into efficient SQL queries across a vast, multi-domain data warehouse by developing a Text-to-SQL feature integrated into their Querybook tool. Initially leveraging large language models (LLMs) with metadata-enriched table schemas—including low-cardinality column values—to generate SQL code from user questions, they enhanced responsiveness via streaming JSON over WebSocket. Recognizing difficulties users had in identifying relevant tables from hundreds of thousands available, they incorporated Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) by creating vector embeddings of table and query summaries stored in OpenSearch to suggest appropriate tables through similarity search, followed by LLM-based re-ranking for user validation before SQL generation. Evaluation highlighted the importance of rich table metadata for search accuracy, achieving a substantial increase in query acceptance rates and a 35% improvement in query writing speed, though initial benchmarks proved less representative than real-world complexity. Ongoing improvements include metadata enrichment, real-time index updates, refined similarity scoring, query validation, and user feedback mechanisms to further optimize semantic retrieval and SQL generation in a large-scale, heterogeneous data environment.

Meta addresses the complex business problem of swiftly identifying root causes during system reliability investigations within their web monorepo, aimed at internal engineers responsible for incident response. The proposed AI-assisted solution combines heuristic-based retrieval to narrow thousands of potential code changes to a few hundred by leveraging code ownership and runtime dependency graphs, followed by a large language model (LLaMA 2, 7B) ranker that iteratively refines this to the top five candidate changes. Training involves supervised fine-tuning on a curated dataset of historical investigations and root cause annotations to guide the model in reasoning with limited initial context. This system achieves 42% accuracy in root cause identification at investigation onset, enhancing investigation efficiency and decision-making. To address risks of misidentification, the solution incorporates explainability, confidence thresholds, and feedback loops, enabling engineers to validate AI outputs. Future expansions include autonomous workflow execution and proactive incident detection to further mitigate reliability risks before deployment.

The coches.net team addressed the complexity and unintuitive user experience of their vehicle marketplace’s filter-based search by developing an AI-powered natural language interface that translates user phrases like “family-friendly SUV for mountain trips” into existing filter parameters, enhancing search convenience. Intended for car buyers seeking a more intuitive, phrase-based search method without manually applying multiple filters, the solution uses Amazon Bedrock’s Claude model with Few-shot prompting to moderate queries and convert them into filter codes within 15 days. This approach balances cost and speed, processing millions of tokens daily at a manageable expense, while ensuring ethical compliance through moderation. The expected outcome is improved user satisfaction and search efficiency, demonstrated by favorable user feedback and increased value generation, although adoption remains limited and ongoing iterations aim to boost usability and impact.

The meal generator application from Cherrypick addresses the business problem of creating personalized, nutritionally balanced meal plans that reduce customer plan changes and increase shopping basket usage, targeting end users seeking tailored dietary solutions. The solution leverages large language models (LLMs) for their strength in complex natural language understanding, creative generation, and contextual reasoning, enabling personalized recipe selection and natural language explanations for choices, which simpler ML or rule-based methods cannot achieve. Key constraints include controlling LLM costs by minimizing API calls, avoiding chat-based interfaces due to interaction inefficiency and expense, and managing LLM randomness through careful prompt design that limits recipe input to relevant options. The system incorporates a multi-layered evaluation framework combining automated data validation and expert human review to ensure output quality and facilitate continuous model improvement. As a result, the product achieves a scalable, robust LLM-powered meal planning experience that balances personalization, cost, and user engagement without succumbing to common pitfalls like excessive model unpredictability or unwieldy interaction models.

Malt addressed the challenge of slow, inflexible freelancer-to-project matching by developing a scalable retriever-ranker architecture leveraging a vector database, primarily to optimize their freelancer recommendation system for both speed and precision. Intended for platform users seeking project-freelancer matches, the solution encodes freelancers and projects separately via transformer-based bi-encoders to generate semantic embeddings stored in a vector database enabling fast Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) searches for an initial candidate retrieval; subsequently, a cross-encoder ranker refines results for exact matching. Key data considerations included handling over 700,000 freelancer profiles with filtering requirements like geo-spatial constraints, managed by choosing Qdrant after benchmarking against alternatives for superior query speed, ANN precision, and filtering support. The outcome was a significant reduction in response latency from minutes to about three seconds, enhanced recommendation quality demonstrated by higher conversion rates, and architecture extensibility for future ranker improvements and new use cases.

Pinterest addresses the business challenge of enhancing product visualization on its platform for users such as shoppers and merchants by developing Pinterest Canvas, a text-to-image latent diffusion foundation model trained on over 1.5 billion high-quality captioned image pairs filtered for trust and relevance. The model supports conditioning on product masks and images to perform inpainting, enabling it to fill missing background regions around product images rather than generating entirely new content. Fine-tuning in stages—with initial random mask inpainting, then product-specific mask conditioning using segmentation and enriched captions from visual large language models—ensures coherent background completions preserving object boundaries. Additional personalization is achieved by conditioning generation on style-providing example images via an IP-Adapter, leveraging Pinterest's Unified Visual Embeddings for strong visual guidance. The outcome is a system capable of real-time generation of photorealistic, stylistically coherent backgrounds for products, boosting aesthetics and engagement while maintaining product integrity through strict masking constraints.

Walmart addressed the challenge of retrieving relevant candidate products for complex and specific tail queries in e-commerce search by developing a hybrid semantic retrieval system that combines traditional inverted index methods with embedding-based neural retrieval models. Targeting users seeking niche or less common products, the solution leverages a scalable neural training technique to enhance the relevance of search results, validated through both offline and online evaluations, while maintaining low response times suitable for production deployment. This approach improves the initial candidate selection stage crucial for downstream re-ranking, thereby enhancing search experience and accuracy in handling intricate user intents within a large product catalog.

Meta’s business problem involves improving the relevance and effectiveness of personalized ads recommendations, traditionally limited by deep learning recommendation models (DLRMs) that rely on human-engineered sparse features, which lose sequential and granular event information and rely heavily on manual intuition. Intended users include advertisers and people interacting with ads across Meta’s apps. The proposed solution replaces handcrafted feature aggregations with event-based features (EBFs) that capture detailed, timestamped sequences of user interactions, enabling new sequence learning architectures powered by transformer models and optimized infrastructure supporting jagged tensor operations. Important data dimensions include event streams, sequence length, and semantic event attributes across millions of heterogeneous entities, requiring scaling solutions like kernel-level GPU optimizations and quantization. The expected outcome is a more nuanced understanding of user behavior over time, resulting in improved ad prediction accuracy, higher conversion rates by 2-4% on select segments, enhanced ad relevance and infrastructure efficiency, and accelerated innovation in recommendation system research.

Dropbox addresses knowledge workers’ information overload by enabling AI-powered semantic retrieval within web file previews, allowing users to generate concise summaries and ask questions about various file types—including documents, videos, and CAD drawings—without manual searching. Using their Riviera framework, Dropbox converts diverse file formats into text and further into embeddings, numerical representations capturing semantic content. These embeddings are chunked and clustered via k-means to identify key concepts for summarization or ranked by similarity to user queries for targeted Q&A, with follow-up questions generated to enhance user understanding. The system supports real-time processing and multi-file queries, dynamically selecting relevant content based on power law distributions of embedding relevance scores, balancing response breadth and focus. Caching intermediate conversions and embeddings optimizes latency and cost, reducing summary costs by 93% and query costs by 64%, while significantly improving response times. This large-scale, embedding-driven architecture leverages LLMs to semantically interpret and consolidate multi-format content securely and efficiently, enhancing user access to complex, lengthy information directly in file previews on the web.

Booking.com addresses the business problem of delivering personalized, high-performance search rankings for millions of accommodation properties by building a sophisticated Ranking platform powered by machine learning models. Intended for end users searching for accommodations and flights, the system integrates diverse data sources, including static features like property attributes and dynamic real-time data such as pricing and availability, aggregated and processed via a sharded Availability Search Engine. Machine learning scientists develop, train, and deploy models using features stored and updated in dedicated feature stores, with inference served through a specialized ML platform cluster to ensure reliable, low-latency predictions under high request volumes—scaling with numerous worker shards handling parallel scoring requests. The system handles challenges like variable payload sizes via chunking and multi-stage ranking, incorporates extensive experimentation via A/B testing, and employs fallback mechanisms to static scores to maintain robustness. The expected outcome is an efficient, scalable, and continuously optimized ranking service that personalizes search results in milliseconds, enhancing user relevance and satisfaction across Booking.com’s travel verticals.

Airbnb addressed the challenge of ranking search results on their map interface, which differs fundamentally from list-based results because user attention does not decay by position but is spread across geographically scattered listings shown as pins. The intended users are guests searching for listings on maps, where traditional ranking by booking probability is ineffective since maps lack a ranked order. Airbnb proposed a semantic retrieval solution modeling user attention flow across pins, initially assuming uniform attention and controlling the diversity of booking probabilities of shown listings via a bounded parameter, improving discovery efficiency and increasing high-quality bookings evidenced by enhanced 5-star stays. They further refined this by tiering pins into regular pins with prices and mini-pins without prices to prioritize attention on higher booking probability listings, especially in fixed-grid desktop interfaces. Finally, they introduced a repositioning algorithm that recenters maps so high-probability listings cluster near the center, reducing searcher effort and improving booking rates. The approach relies on booking probability data, user interaction metrics like click-through rates by location, and constraints on pin quantity and visibility, delivering a more effective semantic ranking of spatial listings that boost both guest discovery and booking quality on map-based search.

Instacart enhances its Order Management System, FoodStorm, used by grocers to sell customizable food products, by integrating generative AI for image generation to solve the challenge of sourcing high-quality photos for diverse product configurations, such as sandwiches with various fillings or personalized cakes. Intended for grocers who require versatile food imagery to improve online customer experience, the solution leverages Instacart’s in-house Pixel text-to-image service and models like Google Imagen, allowing users to generate detailed AI images with fine-tuned prompts specifying specific food details (e.g., "sliced monterey jack cheese on a white background"). The AI-generated images are previewed and optimized for web delivery, supplementing but not replacing authentic professional photography. This capability extends beyond product images to promotional content and category thumbnails, facilitating dynamic visual content creation while addressing technical, legal, and UI design challenges to empower retailers with scalable, customizable visuals across Instacart’s platforms, ultimately saving time and enhancing grocery digital merchandising.

Walmart addresses the challenge of accurately categorizing over 400 million SKUs on its digital storefront to enhance customer navigation akin to their physical stores by deploying Ghotok, an AI system combining predictive and generative models. This system maps complex many-to-many relationships between product categories and product types—distinct hierarchical taxonomies essential for precise item placement and relevance filtering during searches. Using an ensemble approach, Ghotok first employs predictive AI trained on domain-specific, human-labeled features to prune candidate <Category, ProductType> pairs based on confidence thresholds, then applies generative AI with chain-of-thought prompting for refined semantic filtering, balancing effectiveness and inference cost. The backend manages millions of such mappings via a two-tier LRU caching system to meet millisecond-level retrieval SLAs. This hybrid AI framework reduces false positives, handles domain-specific terminology, and improves categorization accuracy, resulting in faster, more relevant search outcomes and a streamlined, intuitive shopping experience on Walmart.com.

Instacart’s Economics Team addresses the challenging problem of efficiently allocating vast paid marketing budgets by developing an adaptive experimentation system for optimizing marketing actions like target cost per action (CPA). Traditional observational data is heavily confounded due to non-random marketing actions influenced by events, holidays, or competitor behavior, making it unreliable for inferring performance curves that relate marketing spend to returns. Their solution introduces controlled random perturbations in marketing actions to generate exogenous variation, enabling credible estimation of performance curves via inverse-propensity-weighted Bayesian regression models constrained by domain knowledge. Leveraging a Thompson Sampling-based explore-exploit algorithm, the system continuously updates a posterior distribution over performance curves to intelligently balance exploration of uncertain strategies and exploitation of known effective ones, thus progressively maximizing marketing return minus cost. This fully automated adaptive experimentation framework is iterated in a loop of performance modeling and action selection, yielding significantly improved marketing efficiency demonstrated in controlled A/B tests.

The use case addresses the business problem of efficiently extracting detailed product attributes from unstructured PDF reports containing both text and images, crucial for assortment planning in fashion retail to meet customer demands and optimize inventory. Intended users include assortment planners, suppliers, and designers who rely on enriched product metadata for catalog mapping and improved search filtering. The proposed solution, the Product Attribute Extraction (PAE) framework, employs a multi-step process involving text and image extraction from PDFs using OCR and computer vision, followed by attribute extraction through large language models (LLMs) applied to both textual and visual data, and consolidates extracted attributes to match them with existing catalog items using BERT-based embeddings and cosine similarity. Key challenges addressed include handling complex PDF layouts, noisy and missing labels, and variant attribute representations, while leveraging image encoding to enable LLM processing of visual content. The outcome is a high-accuracy, scalable method yielding an average F1 score of 92.5% for text and perfect for images, enhancing catalog quality, facilitating seamless product comparison, and supporting future assortment decisions in e-commerce fashion.

Pinterest addresses the challenge of user retention through an advanced Notification Event Processor (NEP) system that replaces a daily budget allocation model with a near real-time, machine-learning-powered pipeline to optimize notifications. NEP targets multiple user segments and notification types by generating daily candidates in an event pool, ranking these with a multi-head model that predicts engagement metrics (e.g., push open, email click, unsubscribe), and applying a policy layer that determines the channel and timing for delivery. The system integrates rich content and user behavioral features, employs sequence transformers for temporal representation learning, and adjusts notification volumes dynamically using a PID controller to balance engagement with user fatigue. Operating in a streaming fashion with real-time inference, NEP substantially improves email and push engagement metrics and weekly active user growth, though it also necessitates managing increased unsubscribe rates primarily among new users.

LinkedIn addressed the challenge of improving content search quality for complex, natural language queries by introducing a semantic retrieval capability in their content search engine, targeting LinkedIn members seeking professional content. The solution combines a token-based retriever (TBR) that uses keyword matching and an embedding-based retriever (EBR) leveraging a two-tower model with multilingual-e5 text embeddings to semantically match queries to posts, enabling retrieval of relevant content even when exact keywords are missing. Candidate posts from both retrievers undergo a two-stage multi-ranking process using models that predict on-topicness and long-dwell engagement scores from query, post, author, and searcher features, optimizing for relevance and user engagement metrics. Precomputation of post embeddings ensures efficient retrieval at scale over billions of posts, while approximate nearest neighbor search and careful latency budgeting support high-query throughput. This design resulted in over 10% improvements in on-topic rate and long-dwell metrics, enhancing user satisfaction and site engagement by better answering complex professional content queries.

Grammarly’s Strategic Research team developed mEdIT, a multilingual fine-tuned large language model (LLM) designed for intelligent writing assistance across seven languages and three editing tasks—grammatical error correction, text simplification, and paraphrasing—addressing the business challenge of enabling high-quality, cross-lingual text editing with instructions in mismatched languages; leveraging over 200,000 human-annotated instruction-output pairs fine-tuned on diverse multilingual Seq2Seq and causal LLM architectures, mEdIT outperforms prior models, generalizes well to unseen languages and tasks, and delivers consistent performance regardless of instruction language, with model efficacy correlated to training data quality and size, ultimately enhancing scalable, multilingual writing support for users while providing publicly available datasets and models to foster further research.

Airbnb addresses the critical business problem of securing personal data by developing a comprehensive in-house data classification system that supports Security, Privacy, and Compliance requirements. The intended users include data owners, developers, and governance teams who need to identify, annotate, and enforce policies on personal data across diverse data ecosystems comprising production and analytical databases and cloud storage. The solution involves a three-pillar workflow: dynamic cataloging of data inventories, automated detection using classifiers that leverage regex and machine learning models, and human-in-the-loop reconciliation where data owners confirm annotations. Key data constraints include handling complex, variable data schemas and achieving high precision, recall, and processing speed to minimize false positives and compliance risks. A novel aspect is the "shift left" approach, embedding schema annotations during data creation enforced via CI/CD pipelines, which shifts stewardship to data producers and reduces downstream classification inconsistencies and costs. Expected outcomes are improved accuracy, scalability, and timeliness of personal data classification, fostering trust and enabling robust policy enforcement with measurable quality through recall, precision, and speed metrics.

Instacart addresses the business problem of optimizing search relevance on its large, multi-retailer e-commerce platform by improving the recall layer that retrieves relevant products for user queries; intended users include shoppers seeking specific or broad grocery items across diverse retailers. Their proposed solution is a hybrid retrieval architecture that adaptively combines text-based search via Postgres and semantic embedding search using FAISS, dynamically tuning recall set sizes guided by a query entropy model that measures query specificity and guides how many and which documents to fetch from each retrieval method. Key data include over 1.4 billion product documents across 1500+ retailers, with challenges stemming from varying query distributions and retailer-specific inventories. By adaptively adjusting recall thresholds and exploring fusion techniques like Reciprocal Rank Fusion and convex score combinations, they improve search relevance and reduce over-fetching, leading to measurable improvements in mean converting position (+1.7%) and latency reduction (1.5%). Ongoing infrastructure work includes migrating from FAISS to pgvector to unify retrieval mechanisms and enhance performance.

DoorDash enhances support for its independent delivery contractors, "Dashers," by implementing a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system leveraging large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 to address delivery issues more efficiently than traditional flow-based automation. The system condenses multi-turn conversations to accurately summarize Dasher issues, retrieves relevant knowledge base (KB) articles using optimized embeddings, and generates tailored responses. Key challenges include ensuring groundedness to prevent LLM hallucinations, maintaining language consistency especially for non-English users, coherence between actions and responses, and minimizing latency. To mitigate these, DoorDash developed LLM Guardrail for online response validation, LLM Judge for continuous quality evaluation across retrieval correctness and response accuracy, and a human-in-the-loop process for KB refinement and handling complex cases. This combination improves automated support speed and accuracy, reducing reliance on human agents for routine queries while enabling them to focus on complex problems, thereby creating a scalable, robust semantic retrieval solution that adapts through ongoing monitoring and iterative enhancement.

Thomson Reuters addressed the challenge of providing timely, accurate customer support in complex legal and tax domains by empowering support agents burdened by information overload from vast CRM systems and knowledge bases. Their solution targeted customer support executives who require fast access to precise domain-specific resolutions, using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)—a hybrid approach combining dense vector retrieval from curated document embeddings (via tools like Milvus and sentence transformers) with GPT-4-based seq-to-seq generation to produce context-aware, factually grounded answers with provenance. This architecture mitigates language model hallucinations and enables updates without retraining, crucial for evolving regulatory content. The expected outcome is reduced case resolution times and improved support accuracy, enhancing customer satisfaction and maintaining competitiveness as user service expectations rise.

Instacart enhanced grocery ecommerce search by integrating large language models (LLMs) to generate discovery-oriented content that complements traditional intent-matching results, addressing users’ desire for inspirational product suggestions alongside precise matches. Intended for shoppers using Instacart’s platform, the solution fuses LLMs’ vast world knowledge with domain-specific signals like query annotations, user purchase history, and sequential search behaviors to generate relevant substitute and complementary product lists, such as pairing ingredients or suggesting alternative items when no exact matches exist. The system employs a two-phase content generation approach—basic LLM prompting and advanced augmented prompting with contextual user engagement data—followed by mapping generated terms to catalog products, offline batch processing for scalability, and specialized ranking to align with revenue goals while maintaining interface clarity. This approach improves recommendation relevance, overcomes limitations of previous keyword- and category-based retrieval methods, and has led to significant uplifts in user engagement and revenue, demonstrating LLMs’ effectiveness in enriching ecommerce semantic retrieval beyond straightforward intent matching.

Grab faced a major business problem where employees struggled to find relevant datasets amid over 200,000 tables and numerous data sources, resulting in inefficient data discovery that often took days and relied heavily on tribal knowledge shared via Slack. The intended users were Grab’s data consumers and analysts who needed faster, more accurate access to data for various use cases. The proposed solution combined enhancing Elasticsearch search capabilities with semantic search through an LLM-powered chatbot, HubbleIQ, integrated into both the internal Hubble data discovery tool and Slack for conversational query handling. Key data constraints included sparse documentation coverage (only 20% initially on critical tables) and Elasticsearch's lack of semantic understanding for contextual queries. The team improved documentation coverage to 90% on high-priority tables using GPT-4–generated docs, tuned Elasticsearch to boost relevant and certified datasets, and deployed HubbleIQ to automate semantic data discovery using LLMs. The expected outcome was a dramatic reduction in data discovery time from days to seconds, evidenced by a 12-point rise in click-through rates (to 94%), 17-point improvement in user satisfaction, and record platform engagement, ultimately positioning Grab to fully automate data discovery while continuously refining the AI-powered system.

GitHub addresses the business challenge of efficiently extracting actionable insights from vast volumes of customer feedback submitted via support tickets, aimed at its internal product and engineering teams seeking to identify recurring pain points and prioritize feature improvements. To overcome the manual, error-prone nature of traditional text analysis, GitHub developed a proprietary AI-driven semantic retrieval solution leveraging open-source models like BERTopic—which uses BERT embeddings and HDBSCAN clustering for multilingual topic modeling—and GPT-4 to generate human-readable summaries of clustered feedback. The solution respects privacy by applying pre-trained models without retraining on customer data and incorporates customized visual analytics through an internal web application, enabling context-aware filtering and focused presentation of the most relevant insights. This AI-powered approach automates trend identification, accelerates recognition of common issues, improves feature prioritization, supports data-driven decision-making, and reveals self-serve support opportunities, thereby enhancing responsiveness to developer needs and fostering continuous product evolution aligned with GitHub’s commitment to innovation and user trust.

Roblox addressed the business challenge of scaling immersive, real-time voice communication safety in its 3D worlds by developing an end-to-end machine learning system that detects policy violations in millions of daily voice chat minutes more accurately than human moderators. Targeting users across multiple languages, the solution includes a multilingual Transformer-based voice classifier operating on raw audio within 15-second windows to identify multilabel categories of abuse (e.g., profanity, bullying, discrimination) with low latency suitable for production deployment. To overcome scarce high-quality labeled data, Roblox devised a scalable machine labeling pipeline combining audio chunking, open-source ASR transcription, and an in-house text classification filter, generating large weakly supervised datasets for training while reserving human-labeled data for model evaluation. The system’s architecture supports massive parallelism and 24/7 uptime at scale, enabling a compact and efficient model via student-teacher distillation and latency optimizations like quantization and voice activity detection. Evaluations on human-labeled datasets yielded a PR-AUC above 0.95, and live deployment reduced severe voice abuse reports by over 15%, demonstrating effective real-time moderation that maintains community safety and civility at scale within Roblox immersive worlds.

The New York Times addresses the business problem of efficiently curating a relevant, engaging, and fresh home page from over 250 daily stories by integrating editorial judgment into algorithmic content curation for its online and app home pages. Intended users are news editors and readers, with editorial input shaping three algorithmic programming steps: pooling eligible stories, ranking via a contextual bandit reinforcement learning method that personalizes content using reader context, and finishing with editorial guardrails such as pinning, filters for previously seen content, and exposure minimums to guarantee diverse story prominence. The solution includes features like Exposure Boosting for dynamic story positioning, Smart Refreshing to balance content novelty and reader experience, and Algo Visibility tools enabling editors to monitor algorithmic decisions and story performance. This hybrid human-AI approach enhances editorial workflow efficiency, increases user engagement, ensures editorial priorities are maintained in ranking and display, and supports scalability, especially during major news events where additional automated modules supplement coverage.

Roblox tackled the challenge of enabling seamless communication among its global user base by developing a fast, unified multilingual translation large language model (LLM) that supports real-time text chat translation between any of 16 supported languages, including slang and platform-specific jargon. Intended for over 70 million daily active users who interact in immersive 3D experiences, the solution replaces the impracticality of 256 separate models with a transformer-based unified architecture that leverages linguistic similarities and expert specialization for efficiency and accuracy, achieving latency around 100 milliseconds to maintain natural conversation flow. The model was trained on a combination of open-source, proprietary chat translation data, and human-labeled errors, with innovative evaluation metrics enabling quality assessment without ground-truth references, and iterative back-translation to augment data for rare language pairs. To scale for millions of simultaneous chats, a smaller distilled model (<650 million parameters) was derived from a larger one (~1 billion parameters), optimized for low-latency serving and integrated with Roblox's trust and safety systems to moderate content. This approach not only improved engagement but outperformed commercial APIs on Roblox-specific content by better capturing gaming slang and conversational nuance. Ongoing efforts include incorporating user feedback to continually refine the model, expanding language support, updating slang translations, and exploring future multimodal and voice chat translation capabilities to further break down language barriers across the platform.

Shopify addressed the business problem of improving consumer search intent on merchant storefronts by developing a real-time semantic search solution powered by AI, aimed at merchants and their customers seeking relevant product discovery. The solution leverages embeddings—numerical vector representations of text and images—generated and updated in near real time through a streaming ML inference pipeline built on Google Cloud Dataflow and BigQuery, enabling contextual similarity comparisons beyond keyword matching. Key constraints include managing high throughput (around 2,500 embeddings per second), balancing latency, memory usage, and cost, as well as overcoming GPU memory and concurrency challenges in a distributed environment. The expected outcome is an enhanced, intuitive search experience that boosts merchant sales and customer satisfaction by instantly reflecting product updates and delivering highly relevant search results through shared foundational ML assets.

This use case addresses the challenge of retrieving relevant information for complex, nuanced queries where traditional vector similarity search alone may produce inaccurate results due to its limited contextual understanding, such as confusing negations or conceptual subtleties. Intended for users of semantic search systems dealing with structured relational data, the solution combines efficient initial shortlisting of candidate entries via vector similarity search using FAISS and OpenAI embeddings, followed by re-ranking these candidates with a large language model (LLM), specifically GPT-4o, that leverages natural language understanding to improve relevance and accuracy. Experiments on synthetic datasets of food dishes and tourist spots demonstrated that while raw vector search performs adequately on simple keyword-based queries, the LLM-assisted approach excels in handling queries with additional constraints and context, filtering out irrelevant results and better capturing user intent. This hybrid method aims to enhance search precision for domain-specific applications, balancing efficiency and contextual comprehension, though it introduces additional latency due to the LLM processing step and may vary in effectiveness depending on data complexity and volume.

Figma addressed the complex business problem of users struggling to locate specific designs or components within large organizations by developing AI-powered semantic search features accessible via screenshots, layer selections, or text descriptions. Targeted at designers working with extensive and intricate design systems, the solution leverages multimodal embedding models (not trained on private data) to convert images and text into comparable numerical embeddings, which are indexed alongside metadata in OpenSearch, enabling nearest neighbor vector searches combined with traditional lexical queries. The infrastructure involves enumerating and thumbnailing all frames in files using a server-side C++ renderer, storing metadata in DynamoDB, generating embeddings in AWS SageMaker with batch inference, and optimizing indexing and search performance and cost through engineering improvements such as software rendering, batch update throttling, cluster autoscaling, filtering of non-essential files, and vector quantization. The expected outcome is a scalable, cost-efficient, and robust AI search system improving findability of relevant UI designs and components, currently in early beta and gradually rolling out to users.

Airbnb’s Automation Platform v2 addresses the inflexibility and scalability challenges of traditional conversational AI, which relied on rigid, manually created workflows, by integrating large language models (LLMs) to enable more natural, context-aware dialogues that better interpret nuanced customer queries. Targeted at customer support agents and AI developers, the platform combines LLM-driven workflows with existing rule-based processes to balance innovation with reliability, employing components like a Chain of Thought workflow to sequentially execute tools (actions and workflows) based on LLM reasoning, context management systems that dynamically fetch relevant historical and situational data, and guardrails frameworks to prevent hallucinations and unethical outputs. The solution incorporates developer tools such as a playground for prompt iteration and observability features for monitoring LLM interactions, enabling scalable, efficient creation and production deployment of LLM applications that enhance response accuracy and speed. This hybrid architecture aims to improve customer support experiences while maintaining safety and operational rigor across millions of Airbnb users.

Expedia addresses the challenge of providing highly relevant lodging rankings tailored to different user search contexts and acquisition channels, such as organic destination searches versus external property-focused referrals. For millions of travelers, the platform uses machine learning to adapt its property ranking algorithm by leveraging a rich set of features—including search context parameters, property attributes, and embedding-based representations inspired by Word2vec—to capture both utility and similarity signals. This involves training deep neural network models on converted search logs with booking and click feedback to learn to rank properties by relevance, adjusting rankings for marketplace considerations and channel-specific business logic. In particular, when users come from external channels targeting specific properties (property search), Expedia blends rankings based on contextual relevance and similarity to the targeted property, overcoming issues like full bookings by offering well-ranked alternatives. This dual adaptation enhances user experience by aligning rankings with user intent and channel source, validated through feature ablation studies and A/B testing, ultimately improving booking conversion and traveler satisfaction.

Netflix addresses the challenge of recommending content that fosters long-term member satisfaction rather than merely optimizing short-term engagement metrics like click-through rates. Their personalization system models recommendations as a contextual bandit problem, using a proxy reward function derived from diverse user interactions—including plays, completions, and thumbs-up/down—to better reflect enduring satisfaction. Directly optimizing retention is impractical due to noise, delayed signals, and attribution difficulties, so Netflix engineers the proxy reward function iteratively, incorporating both immediate and delayed feedback. To handle delayed or missing feedback, they predict final user responses based on observed interactions, enabling timely bandit policy updates that reflect long-term preferences. The system relies on two ML models: one predicts delayed feedback offline to define rewards, and the other generates real-time recommendations online. This approach confronts the online-offline metric disparity by refining proxy rewards to align predictive improvements with actual user satisfaction, aiming to enhance both member enjoyment and retention over time.

Spotify addressed the challenge of training machine learning models on their massive and diverse content catalogs by developing a scalable annotation platform to generate millions of high-quality content annotations efficiently. Intended for domain expert annotators, quality analysts, project managers, and ML engineers, the solution automates and streamlines the annotation workflow with integrated tooling for varied tasks (e.g., audio/video segment labeling, NLP classification) and incorporates configurable large language models to augment human expertise. Key components include centralized expert workforces with multi-level review, custom annotation interfaces, metrics for tracking annotator agreement and project progress, and flexible APIs enabling end-to-end integration with ML training and evaluation pipelines. This comprehensive platform reduced annotation time, boosted annotator productivity threefold, and increased annotation volume tenfold, accelerating model iteration and improving model quality for content relation detection, policy violation identification, and related tasks at Spotify’s scale.

DoorDash addresses the challenge of personalized restaurant recommendations and user engagement through an innovative notification system powered by Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), targeting users seeking relevant local cuisine suggestions. By modeling users, restaurants, and their interactions as graph nodes and edges, DoorDash utilizes GNNs to capture complex, heterogeneous relationships within a rich, interconnected data structure spanning orders, views, and user behavior over a year. The system employs message passing, aggregation, and stacked GNN layers to generate latent embeddings for users and restaurants, enabling link prediction of likely user-restaurant orders within a week. The model incorporates geolocation constraints to ensure recommendations are delivery-feasible, followed by filtering for freshness and quality. Offline evaluations show significant performance gains over traditional models, and production deployment via daily notifications results in measurable increases in user engagement and monthly active users across cohorts. This GNN-driven approach effectively addresses fragmented data and inactive users, enhancing personalized discovery and loyalty through contextual, data-driven culinary exploration.

Revolut addresses the challenge of fragmented, siloed risk management in financial services by developing an integrated, scientific Enterprise Risk Management Framework (ERMF) that models risks as chains of events within a Markov chain structure, enabling consistent measurement, comparison, and hypothetical scenario analysis across financial and operational risks. Intended for risk managers and regulators, the solution uses semantic reasoning via the Prometheux platform to encode states, events, and risks into a knowledge graph linked to live data sources for continuous monitoring and learning, supporting both ex-ante expected loss calculations and ex-post observed metrics. Explainability and auditability are ensured through AI-powered proof trees and natural language interactions via large language models, providing transparent, compliant insights and documentation automation. This approach enables unified risk assessment, dynamic updating of risk hypotheses, and AI-assisted natural language risk generation and explanation, overcoming legacy methodological silos and enhancing regulatory compliance and decision-making in the fintech domain.

Instacart addressed the challenge of delivering relevant product recommendations across multiple shopping surfaces by developing a unified contextual retrieval system based on transformer sequence models, primarily a BERT-like Masked Language Model trained on user interaction sequences of product IDs. Targeted at shoppers placing large basket orders, the solution predicts the next product a user may add by leveraging the sequential context of viewed and added items within a session, thereby enabling dynamic, real-time recommendations on search, item detail, cart, and checkout pages. Handling a massive catalog spanning millions of products from thousands of retailers, the model employs a fixed vocabulary of popular product IDs and yields top-K product predictions for downstream ranking, achieving significant improvements in relevance metrics and a 30% increase in cart additions. The approach replaces disparate legacy retrieval systems and proves the importance of precise sequence information, while ongoing work aims to scale vocabulary, incorporate canonical product identities, mitigate popularity bias, and enrich context features to enhance recommendation accuracy.

LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant addresses the challenge recruiters face with repetitive and complex hiring workflows by leveraging large language models (LLMs) to automate deeply personalized tasks such as crafting and refining job descriptions, translating recruiter requirements into nuanced search queries, ranking candidate matches against qualifications, and managing interview coordination. Intended primarily for recruiters, the solution incorporates an experiential memory that personalizes interactions by learning from individual recruiter preferences and feedback, enabling iterative refinement of candidate lists. It also integrates an agent orchestration layer facilitating asynchronous, collaborative workflows across sourcing, messaging, and hiring manager communications, enhanced by LinkedIn's semantic search and Economic Graph data to transparently infer candidate fit. Prioritizing responsible AI use, the system maintains recruiter control with editable, auditable actions and safeguards against content hallucination, ensuring trust, fairness, and transparency in the AI-assisted hiring process, ultimately streamlining recruiters’ workflows to focus on strategic, interpersonal hiring activities.

Meta AI addressed the challenge of scaling their generative AI-based image animation feature to serve billions efficiently by optimizing latency and resource use for their diffusion models. Targeting users across Meta’s apps, the solution involved converting models to bfloat16 precision to halve memory use and speed inference, enhancing temporal-attention computation to reduce redundant tensor expansions, applying DPM-Solver to cut sampling steps, and combining guidance with step distillation to collapse multiple forward passes, all accelerating generation times. Additional PyTorch-based compiler optimizations further boosted deployment efficiency. To manage global traffic and maintain low latency despite network overhead, Meta implemented a dynamic traffic routing system that keeps requests region-local when possible and redistributes load to avoid GPU saturation, coupled with tailored retry strategies incorporating delays and exponential backoff to prevent cascading failures. Together, these techniques enabled robust, low-latency, large-scale production animation generation with minimal errors and sustainable GPU usage.

Klaviyo's Segments AI addresses the challenge of customer segmentation for its 130,000 users by automating the creation of intelligent, dynamic customer segments that update as new data arrives, enabling both inexperienced users to simplify interaction and experts to save time on repetitive tasks. The solution employs advanced prompt chaining and few-shot learning techniques with large language models (LLMs), particularly leveraging OpenAI, to generate segmented outputs adhering to Klaviyo’s JSON schema, while mitigating error propagation through asynchronous, parallelized subtasks. Validation poses significant challenges due to the non-deterministic and creative nature of LLM-generated segments, leading the team to combine LLM self-evaluation with hand-crafted test cases for scalable feedback, acknowledging the ongoing necessity for maintenance and iterative development inherent in generative AI features deployed in customer-facing environments.

The Grammarly Keyboard on iOS addresses the business problem of improving personalized typing experiences by enabling the keyboard to learn users' unique vocabularies, including non-standard words like pet names or project titles, without compromising privacy. Targeted at mobile users, the proposed solution involves an on-device personal language model (PLM) that operates entirely locally to ensure sensitive data never leaves the device, supporting offline personalization. Given mobile constraints—limited RAM (under 5 MB for new features) and the need for responsive typing—the model efficiently manages custom vocabulary using memory-mapped key-value stores, caching, and a time-based decay function to discard obsolete words. To improve accuracy, it filters out noisy inputs (casual variants or typos) with regex and timing-based thresholds before incorporating words into suggestions. An offline evaluation framework validates these mechanisms, ensuring robust handling of edge cases. Deployed to over 5 million devices, this approach reduces irrelevant suggestion reversions and increases accepted corrections, delivering privacy-preserving, performant, and accurate personalized language modeling for enhanced user communication.

This use case addresses the business challenge of optimizing marketing channel allocation (SMS vs. Email) to maximize customer engagement for Klaviyo customers, who are marketers sending campaigns. Intended users are marketers seeking personalized messaging strategies. The proposed solution employs counterfactual learning and uplift modeling within a contextual bandit framework, using randomized A/B test data to estimate the individual treatment effect (ITE) of each channel on engagement without requiring numerous separate experiments. Key data components include customer context features, assigned treatment, observed rewards, and logged assignment probabilities, enabling unbiased inverse propensity weighting estimators to evaluate and optimize policies post hoc. Expected outcomes are improved targeted personalization through automated uplift-model-based personalization tests that dynamically select the best channel per recipient, enhancing engagement and providing interpretability on segment-level treatment effects.

Discord addresses the challenge of efficiently modeling complex relationships among users, guilds (servers), games, and other entities within its platform by developing DERE (Discord's Entity-Relationship Embeddings), which produces vector embeddings derived from social graph-based features using unsupervised contrastive learning on billions of (head, relation, tail) triplets representing entity interactions. Intended for ML engineers and data scientists, DERE pre-trains embeddings that capture multifaceted entity relationships by optimizing a triplet margin loss to place related entities close in embedding space and unrelated ones far apart, enabling applications such as classification, recommendation, ranking, and discovery (e.g., game similarity and player quest targeting). The embeddings are made accessible via BigQuery, cloud storage, and live serving, accelerating model development by providing reusable, expressive representations that reflect the entire relationship graph, with ongoing enhancements focused on stability monitoring and visualization to improve downstream model retraining and interpretability.

Booking.com addresses complex fraud detection challenges by leveraging graph technology to represent and analyze interconnected transaction identifiers such as accounts and credit cards in real time. Fraud detection experts and machine learning models use a graph database (JanusGraph with Cassandra) to build dynamic graphs from historical and incoming reservation request data, enabling the system to detect suspicious patterns based on node connections and proximity to flagged fraudulent identifiers. The graph service enriches fraud risk estimation with features like node counts and shortest hops to fraud notices, which are computed within stringent low-latency constraints (p99 ~300ms) to support synchronous real-time evaluation during request processing. This solution allows detection of evolving fraudulent schemes by revealing subtle relational structures in transaction data that traditional systems might miss, thereby enhancing Booking.com's platform security and trustworthiness for customers and partners.

Picnic addresses the common challenge of weekly meal planning by offering in-app personalized recipe recommendations to enhance customer inspiration and ease menu selection, leveraging implicit collaborative filtering based on customers' past recipe orders as feedback. Targeting end users of the Picnic supermarket app, their solution constructs a customer-recipe interaction matrix representing purchase behavior and applies a CosineRecommender model to find recipe similarities and generate tailored suggestions. To mitigate noise from outliers and popularity bias, they implement BM25 weighting to properly balance interaction significance. Deployed in A/B testing, this straightforward machine learning approach proved as effective as manual curation, saving effort while providing scalable, personalized recommendations. Future plans include hybrid models incorporating recipe content features and explicit dietary preferences, aiming to improve recommendation relevance and sophistication beyond the current collaborative filtering framework.

Upwork addresses the business problem of efficiently connecting clients and freelancers to solve complex work challenges by deploying Uma, a multi-model AI system designed for semantic retrieval and tailored workflows within its marketplace. Intended for hiring managers and freelancers, Uma leverages decades of rich platform data, proprietary synthetic data generation, and human-curated conversational scripts to train both large pretrained models and custom use case-specific language models fine-tuned for precision in tasks like job post creation, proposal writing, and candidate matching. Constrained by the need for high-quality, relevant, and privacy-compliant training data, Upwork’s AI team combines general LLMs with bespoke models to enhance conversational coherence, contextual understanding, and outcome accuracy. The expected outcome is a mindful, responsible AI companion that accelerates hiring processes, improves freelancer productivity, and delivers high-quality work outcomes by facilitating deeply contextual and intelligent interactions across the platform.

Coinbase faced the enterprise challenge of deploying generative AI solutions that balance accuracy, cost, latency, availability, and trust-safety constraints, targeting both customer-facing and internal users such as non-ML staff and engineers. To address this, they developed CB-GPT, a multi-cloud, multi-LLM platform integrating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques to ground responses in authoritative enterprise data and external sources, ensuring honest, helpful, and harmless outputs via custom guardrails against hallucinations and jailbreaking. CB-GPT supports semantic caching to reduce costs, offers no-code and API access for diverse user proficiency levels, and leverages self-hosted open-source models for fine-tuned crypto-specific tasks and cost control. Additionally, the platform enables agentified LLM solutions that autonomously reason, plan, and act to automate complex workflows, enhancing operational scalability and reliability amidst dynamic model leaderboards and constrained GPU resources expected in production-scale crypto enterprise environments.

Adyen addresses the challenge of augmenting unit test generation in large, complex codebases by integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) enhanced through Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parsing and Knowledge Graphs (KGs), overcoming limitations of conventional Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems and vector embeddings which struggle with code's contextual and logical complexities. The intended users are Adyen’s software developers who require more efficient, consistent, and high-quality test creation to maintain codebase standards while focusing on complex development tasks. The solution involves a code-context-aware system that structurally represents code syntax and semantics within graph databases, enabling sophisticated retrieval and precise test generation aligned with code dependencies and interactions. Although fine-tuning LLMs is resource-intensive and challenged by rapid codebase evolution, combining it with RAG techniques and AST-KG integrations enhances context sensitivity and logic-driven code understanding. Expected outcomes include improved developer productivity, elevated code quality, automated and optimized software lifecycle processes, and a reliable internal tool tailored for Adyen’s evolving development environment.

Trivago addressed the challenge of enabling travelers to find hotels that precisely match complex, natural language preferences by developing Smart AI Search, an AI-powered semantic retrieval system integrated deeply into their core hotel search platform. Aimed at end users seeking intuitive and accurate hotel discovery, the solution leverages recent advances in Large Language Models combined with traditional keyword matching, filtering, and data preprocessing to interpret free-text queries like "a quiet boutique hotel near the old town with a rooftop pool and good workspace," delivering highly relevant results. The development involved a cross-functional team in close partnership with Google to tailor and scale the AI technology while ensuring seamless integration without disrupting existing search functionalities. Constraints included user difficulty in articulating preferences upfront and balancing innovation with a refined user experience, prompting the design of supportive interaction models. Ultimately, Smart AI Search provides a smarter, faster, more intuitive travel planning experience, positioning trivago uniquely in a competitive, rapidly evolving AI space.

The MongoDB Documentation AI Chatbot addresses the business problem of enabling users to perform semantic search and question answering on their own unstructured textual data without requiring a full database setup or Atlas account, targeting developers and data practitioners exploring Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with vector search. The solution uses the Chatbot Demo Builder within the MongoDB Search Playground, allowing users to import PDFs or text up to 100,000 characters, generate embeddings via built-in Voyage AI models, and apply configurable chunking strategies to create a pre-configured, non-editable vector search index. Constraints include data size limits, exclusion of image content, and ephemeral session persistence (30-day snapshot sharing). The chatbot executes semantic vector searches using MongoDB's $vectorSearch aggregation and independently answers each query with generated responses based on retrieved document chunks, while offering transparency into search queries, retrieved documents, and model settings. Expected outcomes include rapid prototyping and evaluation of RAG workflows on custom textual datasets with scalable vector retrieval that supports experimentation with embedding and chunking parameters without requiring sensitive data uploads or permanent infrastructure.

The Reforge Extension addresses the challenge of applying Reforge's expert course content to users' everyday workflow by integrating AI-powered semantic retrieval and generation directly into popular productivity tools like Google Docs, Notion, Confluence, and Coda.
