Targeted at product managers and knowledge workers drafting documents such as Product Requirements Documents (PRDs), the solution uses large language models (LLMs) augmented with embeddings stored in a Pinecone vector database to retrieve relevant expert artifacts, classify document types, and provide tailored suggestions grounded in vetted Reforge content. The development involved iterative prototyping from simple Retrieve-and-Generate (RAG) setups to more sophisticated chain-of-thought (CoT) approaches that improved the relevance and accuracy of semantic search and prompts. Constraints such as latency, cost, model quality, and limited data availability shaped the technology stack and testing strategies, while user feedback guided continual refinements. Expected outcomes include enhanced productivity, more contextually appropriate document drafting assistance, and increased trust due to transparent referencing of authoritative Reforge materials, all seamlessly embedded into users’ existing tools without workflow disruption.

The New York Times Games team addresses the user experience challenge of handwriting input for their Crossword app by developing an on-device handwriting recognition system enabled through a custom ‘SketchBox’ component that captures stylus or finger-drawn strokes per crossword square. Targeting iOS and Android users of the app, they designed a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) leveraging augmented datasets—including an expanded EMNIST set for letters and digits—with careful preprocessing, normalization, and timing logic to accurately segment user input strokes. By deploying a compact TensorFlow Lite model optimized via hyperparameter tuning and stratified cross-validation, the solution achieves about 91% validation accuracy in recognizing 62 alphanumeric characters, improving robustness against handwriting variability and off-center inputs inherent in crossword puzzle entry. This semantic retrieval system aims to enhance interactivity and accessibility in puzzle-solving while laying groundwork for future features like erase gestures and self-training, ultimately enriching the gaming experience for subscribers.

Incident.io addressed the challenge of keeping incident summaries current amid active incident resolution, targeting incident responders who struggle to update summaries while mitigating issues. They developed a semantic retrieval solution using OpenAI’s large language models via API to suggest dynamic, context-aware summary updates by analyzing incident updates, Slack conversations, and prior summaries. Key constraints included accuracy, user control over accepting or modifying AI-generated summaries to prevent user frustration, prompt engineering complexity addressed through iterative testing with real incident fixtures, and data privacy concerns managed via strict zero-data retention agreements with OpenAI and careful customer communication. The outcome was improved summary freshness and efficiency, with half of all updates AI-generated, enhancing user experience and establishing reusable AI infrastructure for future features.

Careem addressed the business problem of reducing payment fraud in its ride-hailing service by transitioning from a rules-based pre-authorisation system—which places temporary holds on customer credit cards to mitigate fraud risks but can degrade user experience—to a machine learning (ML) model-based approach. Intended for the fraud prevention and integrity teams, the solution employs a Catboost gradient boosting model trained on recent, relevant transaction data with time-based rolling validation to optimize real-time predictions, balancing high Recall (>0.9) to catch fraud with precision to minimize false positives and customer complaints. The system relies on engineered features aggregated daily for efficient prediction through an internal platform (YODA) allowing near real-time scoring via endpoints while maintaining model and production data alignment. Deployment includes shadow mode testing to assess performance without impacting live transactions. The ML-driven approach improved precision by 60%, reduced losses and customer complaints, and enhanced adaptability against evolving fraudulent behaviors compared to static, reverse-engineered rules, demonstrating significant gains in fraud detection efficacy and user experience preservation.

The business problem addressed is reducing user friction and context switching when seeking help with complex retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines by integrating a context-sensitive AI assistant directly into the Vectorize user interface, intended for platform users configuring integrations and workflows. The solution involves building a RAG pipeline that ingests unstructured documentation and approved support answers from multiple dynamic sources (like documentation, Discord, and Intercom) into a vector database, enabling semantic similarity search enhanced by appending page-specific contextual topics to user queries. To improve relevance, the system employs a reranking model to filter out low-relevance retrievals before passing data to a large language model (LLM), combined with prompt engineering that instructs the LLM not to hallucinate answers and restrict responses to retrieved content. The assistant is embedded as a React component with initial seed questions to encourage use and context-aware retrieval, thus minimizing irrelevant results and optimizing user assistance in real-time. Monitoring user feedback via ratings and plans for relevance tracking aim to continuously assess and improve retrieval quality. This approach enables fast, accurate, context-sensitive support that evolves automatically as documentation and support data update, enhancing user experience and reducing support bottlenecks.

DoorDash addresses the business challenge of delivering accurate and reliable estimated times of arrival (ETAs) across diverse delivery scenarios to enhance customer trust and experience at scale by developing a NextGen ETA system based on a novel two-layer multi-task deep learning model. Intended for various business stakeholders and delivery situations—from home page browsing to checkout and multiple delivery types—the solution combines a probabilistic base layer providing unbiased, uncertainty-quantified ETA distributions with a decision layer optimizing multi-objective business goals. Using multi-task modeling enables unified predictions across numerous ETA use cases, leveraging transfer learning to improve performance on infrequent tasks, while advanced feature embedding and flexible deep learning optimizations overcome limitations of prior tree-based models. Probabilistic forecasts deliver calibrated uncertainty estimates using metrics like continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), allowing the system to communicate not only expected ETAs but also delivery variances, improving on-time accuracy and consistency. This architecture supports rapid onboarding of new prediction tasks, manages data imbalance, and incorporates real-world uncertainties such as food preparation delays and Dasher availability, ultimately producing more transparent, robust, and trustworthy ETA predictions that scale reliably with DoorDash’s complex ecosystem.

This use case addresses the challenge of text classification across imbalanced and evolving datasets, primarily targeting data scientists and machine learning engineers working with large-scale document categorization, such as news articles spanning diverse categories like space, medicine, and graphics. The proposed solution employs semantic search via the Faiss library, which enables efficient vector-based nearest neighbor retrieval to classify documents without the need for retraining conventional supervised models when new categories emerge or data scales up. Key constraints include managing data imbalance and optimizing search speed-accuracy trade-offs through different Faiss indexing strategies—flat, partitioning, and product quantization—while leveraging embeddings generated by transformer-based models (e.g., MiniLM). Expected outcomes include scalable, flexible classification that mitigates the computational cost and complexity of retraining while maintaining robust accuracy across heterogeneous datasets, demonstrated through practical experiments on a multi-category news dataset.

This use case addresses the challenge in customer service technical support of rapidly and accurately retrieving relevant past issue tickets to resolve inquiries efficiently. Intended for customer service teams, the proposed solution integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a knowledge graph (KG) constructed from historical issue tickets, preserving both intra-issue hierarchical structures and inter-issue relationships such as explicit and semantic links. The KG nodes, enriched with embeddings from models like BERT and E5, enable precise semantic retrieval of subgraphs relevant to user queries, while query parsing extracts named entities and intents to guide retrieval. Generated answers leverage large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4 to synthesize information from the KG. This approach overcomes limitations of conventional text chunking methods, improving retrieval metrics substantially (e.g., 77.6% gain in mean reciprocal rank) and enhancing answer quality, as evidenced by BLEU score improvements and a 28.6% reduction in median issue resolution times in LinkedIn’s deployment. Constraints include managing text length for embedding and maintaining graph coherence, with future work focusing on automation and adaptability of graph templates and dynamic updates.

LinkedIn addressed the business problem of data experts' time being consumed by helping colleagues find data by creating SQL Bot, an AI-powered assistant integrated into their DARWIN data science platform that transforms natural language questions into SQL queries, enabling employees to access data insights independently with proper permissions. The solution tackles challenges such as navigating vast, complex enterprise data warehouses with millions of tables by leveraging embedding-based retrieval enhanced with certified metadata, personalized dataset inference via organizational context, and continuous updating through usage signals and deprecations. A knowledge graph enriched with domain knowledge, example queries, and query logs supports LLM-based re-ranking for precise table and field selection, iterative query generation with validation and self-correction, and a rich conversational UX that guides users through query construction and permits customization via dataset selection, custom instructions, and example queries. The system incorporates rigorous benchmarking with expert human and LLM evaluation to ensure query accuracy and user satisfaction, ultimately democratizing data access across LinkedIn’s business verticals while improving efficiency and reducing bottlenecks in data analytics workflows.

Netflix addresses the operational burden of diagnosing and remediating failed big data jobs, particularly Spark jobs, by evolving from a rule-based error classifier (Pensive) to an integrated Auto Remediation system that combines rule-based classification with a machine learning (ML) service (Nightingale). The business problem involves handling errors like memory misconfigurations and unclassified errors at scale without excessive manual intervention, where memory errors require tuning multiple Spark configuration parameters and unclassified errors cause unnecessary retries and costs. The solution automates error classification using predefined rules, then applies an ML model predicting retry success probability and associated compute costs, optimizing Spark configurations via Bayesian optimization to recommend or disable retries, with recommendations automatically applied through an online configuration service (ConfigService). Key data inputs include logs, Spark execution parameters, and job metadata processed via feature embeddings, while constraints involve maintaining user experience and balancing retry success against cost efficiency. Production deployment has demonstrated that Auto Remediation remediates approximately 56% of memory configuration errors and reduces compute costs by about 50%, significantly lowering human intervention and operational expenses while enabling continued scaling and potential future enhancements such as Right Sizing for resource optimization.

Instacart addresses the critical business problem of detecting and preventing diverse fraudulent activities such as fake accounts, payment fraud, and collusion between customers and shoppers with its real-time Fraud Platform, Yoda, intended for fraud analysts and operations teams. The solution leverages ClickHouse, a fast columnar analytical database, as the primary real-time datastore to support low-latency, real-time decisioning by ingesting data streams from PostgreSQL and Instacart event sources via Kafka and Flink ingestion pipelines configured with YAML. Analysts define dynamic, SQL-based feature definitions and create configurable rules through a self-serve UI, enabling real-time evaluation of aggregated features for prompt actions like transaction blocking or account suspension. This architecture improves fraud detection speed and accuracy, enhances engineering productivity by shifting workflow ownership to analysts, and secures sensitive data through strict access controls, ultimately resulting in significant financial savings and platform trustworthiness.

DoorDash addresses the challenge of inconsistent and incomplete product attribute data in its retail catalog, which aggregates SKUs from diverse merchants across new verticals like grocery and liquor stores, by deploying large language models (LLMs) for semantic attribute extraction and enrichment. Intended for internal teams managing product data and ultimately benefiting customers and delivery personnel (Dashers), the solution automates named-entity recognition tasks such as brand identification, organic labeling, and generalized attribute extraction, overcoming the cold-start problem inherent in traditional NLP methods requiring extensive labeled data. Leveraging techniques like retrieval augmented generation and embedding-based example retrieval, the approach generates accurate, scalable annotations and updates a hierarchical brand knowledge graph, significantly improving catalog quality, personalized recommendation accuracy, fulfillment reliability, and customer engagement metrics. Constraints include handling diverse, unstructured SKU descriptions and the need to incorporate multimodal data (text and images) to address abbreviation and abstraction issues; ongoing work explores multimodal LLMs and centralized platforms for democratized model deployment. The expected outcome is a high-quality, comprehensive, and dynamically enriched product knowledge graph enabling superior shopping experiences across DoorDash’s expanding retail verticals.

Airbnb developed Brandometer, an advanced natural language understanding system using deep learning word embeddings from social media data across 19 platforms to quantitatively measure and track brand perception, which traditionally relied on limited and biased customer surveys. Targeting brand analysts and marketers, the solution processes noisy, sparse user-generated content monthly, employing models like Word2Vec, FastText, and DeBERTa to embed Airbnb-related concepts and compute Perception Scores via cosine similarity and rank-based metrics for stability over time. By addressing variability through score averaging and calibration, Brandometer enables stable, real-time monitoring of brand sentiments (e.g., "belonging," "host," "stay") and emerging trends linked to campaigns or events, facilitating data-driven insights to enhance brand strategy and customer experience.

DoorDash addresses the challenge of accurately interpreting complex, multi-attribute user food and retail item queries—such as specifying dietary restrictions like "vegan chicken sandwich"—by integrating large language models (LLMs) with knowledge graph-based semantic retrieval to enhance query and document understanding. The system segments queries into meaningful, taxonomy-aligned components (e.g., dietary preference, flavor, product category) and links them to rich metadata in knowledge graphs, enabling precise retrieval that respects crucial constraints like dietary restrictions as mandatory while allowing flexibility for other attributes. To mitigate LLM hallucinations, DoorDash employs controlled vocabularies and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that constrains the model to candidate concepts identified via approximate nearest neighbor search, improving entity linking accuracy. This hybrid approach balances memorization and generalization by combining LLM-driven contextual understanding with scalable methods like embedding retrieval, leading to improved search recall and precision. Post-processing and manual audits ensure high precision, especially for sensitive attributes. The enhanced query understanding signals are integrated into ranking components, resulting in a nearly 30% increase in popular dish carousel triggers and over 2% uplift in whole page relevance for dish-intent queries, which correlate with higher user engagement and order conversions. This framework enables DoorDash to better accommodate nuanced consumer intents and offers future opportunities for query rewriting, personalized recommendations, and expanded catalog attribute coverage.

LinkedIn developed a generative AI product aimed at enhancing job search and professional content engagement by enabling users to quickly extract insights, evaluate job fit, and receive personalized career advice via a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline involving specialized AI agents. The system routes user queries to domain-specific AI agents which retrieve relevant internal and external data through API calls—including LinkedIn’s unique datasets and Bing—and then synthesize responses using large language models (LLMs) augmented by embedding-based retrieval. The development prioritized modular agent design for rapid parallel development but faced challenges in maintaining consistent user experience, scaling high-quality evaluation with human annotation and automatic methods, and managing error-prone structured API calls from LLM outputs. Key constraints involved balancing response quality, latency, and GPU resource usage, while ongoing efforts focus on improving fine-tuning of LLMs, automated evaluation, API invocation robustness via a unified skill registry, and optimizing system throughput with async, streaming pipelines. The expected outcome is a scalable, interactive assistant that delivers accurate, grounded, and contextually relevant career and content guidance to LinkedIn members.

This use case addresses the challenge security professionals face in efficiently summarizing complex security and privacy incidents for diverse audiences like executives and partner teams. Intended users include incident response teams and incident commanders who must communicate incident details clearly and swiftly while maintaining regulatory compliance. The proposed solution leverages large language models (LLMs) to generate concise, structured incident summaries and executive updates by processing unstructured, sensitive data tagged with self-explanatory markers to guide the model. Human oversight ensures accuracy and mitigates risks such as hallucinations, with infrastructure designed to avoid data retention or unauthorized training. Prompt engineering evolved through iterative refinements and example-driven instruction to produce high-quality summaries aligned with internal communication standards. The outcome is a 51% reduction in summary drafting time and improved content quality, enabling faster, more consistent incident response communications at scale without compromising privacy or compliance.

Picnic addresses the business challenge of enabling fast, accurate product and recipe search for millions of diverse customers across multiple countries and languages on a limited mobile interface by enhancing search retrieval with Large Language Models (LLMs). Their primary users are online grocery shoppers who frequently create varied and sometimes error-prone queries. The proposed solution leverages OpenAI’s GPT-3.5-turbo to convert search terms into detailed product descriptions, which are then transformed into embeddings for efficient matching against a precomputed and cached index of product and recipe data using OpenSearch, enabling millisecond latency critical for a seamless user experience. This system accounts for linguistic nuances, typos, contextual intent, and location-specific expectations, supporting multi-language and culturally distinct preferences, while balancing the computational cost of API calls with caching strategies. The expected outcome is improved search accuracy, faster response times, higher conversion and click-through rates, and increased customer satisfaction achieved through offline tuning, extensive A/B testing, and continuous iterative refinements, ultimately maintaining Picnic’s competitive edge in online grocery retail.

GoDaddy faces the business problem of providing scalable, accurate customer support through conversational AI given over 60,000 daily customer contacts across messaging channels. Their Digital Care team, intended for customer support agents and end users, implements large language models (LLMs) to classify inquiries, prompt topic-specific questions, offer self-help, and route conversations efficiently. Key constraints include managing large, costly prompts, model output reliability, latency issues, token limits, and the probabilistic nature of LLMs requiring guardrails to prevent adverse outcomes. Solutions evolved from mega-prompts to a multi-agent architecture combining controller and task-oriented prompts, integrated Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with optimized, compressed knowledge representations, model-specific prompt tuning, structured output validation, and deterministic human handoff mechanisms. They also address operational challenges like model outages via adaptive model selection and mitigate latency with streaming APIs. Expected outcomes include improved chatbot accuracy, enhanced user experience, and maintainable, cost-effective AI deployment, emphasizing continuous fine-tuning, memory management, thorough multi-disciplinary testing, and monitoring to ensure reliable semantic retrieval in customer support.

Microsoft’s Skilling organization developed “Ask Learn,” a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based knowledge service integrated into Microsoft Q&A and powering Microsoft Copilot for Azure, to address the challenge of delivering accurate, relevant, and verifiable AI-generated answers from vast, continuously updated Microsoft Learn documentation. Intended for Azure users and developers, the solution employs advanced RAG techniques—embedding document chunks into a vector database, sophisticated pre- and post-processing for query refinement and answer validation, and orchestration through modular microservices—to ensure high-quality results despite the non-deterministic nature of generative AI. Key constraints include maintaining up-to-date indexing amid frequent documentation changes, rigorous evaluation via a curated golden dataset, safeguarding privacy and ethical standards, and capturing user feedback while respecting data ownership. The expected outcome is a chat experience embedded within the Azure portal that reduces users’ context switching by providing grounded, actionable knowledge and serving both as a direct answer source and a fallback mechanism, ultimately enhancing user productivity and trust in AI responses at massive scale.

Airtable addressed the business challenge of enabling rich semantic search over complex customer data, intended for users like marketing, product, and support teams seeking rapid insights from related past records. The proposed solution involved building a resilient embedding system wherein data is asynchronously converted into numerical vectors (embeddings) stored in a separate vector database, distinct from the main in-memory database (MemApp), to balance costs and performance through eventual consistency rather than costly strong consistency. The system manages embeddings lifecycle with careful tracking of embedding states via transaction IDs to maintain ordering and freshness, supports flexible configuration through embedding configs that define data subscriptions and embedding strategies, and handles operational complexities such as migrations, disaster recovery, permission enforcement, and multi-provider AI model support. This architecture results in a robust, adaptable platform that gracefully copes with failures, evolving AI models, data privacy needs, and scaling, enabling fast, semantically rich queries while controlling costs and downtime to acceptable levels.

This use case addresses the business problem of identifying AI-generated (deepfake) faces used in fake online profiles that facilitate spam, fraud, and disinformation campaigns, targeting users such as social media platforms and cybersecurity teams. The proposed solution focuses on detecting AI-generated facial images by exploiting resilient, general-purpose artifacts present across various generative models, including GANs and diffusion-based engines, regardless of image resolution or quality (as low as 128 x 128 pixels). Key data constraints include the need to handle diverse synthesis engines and image qualities commonly found "in the wild." The expected outcome is a robust, scalable system capable of distinguishing real faces from AI-generated ones, thereby improving the integrity of online identity verification and curbing malicious activities associated with synthetic media.

The business problem addressed is generating personalized, relevant connection recommendations for LinkedIn’s over one billion members in the “People You May Know” (PYMK) feature within the My Network tab, balancing scalability and relevance. Intended users are LinkedIn members seeking to grow or reconnect with their professional networks. The proposed solution involves a multi-stage Candidate Generation (CG) system combining three main techniques: graph-based CG using deterministic N-hop and personalized PageRank walks over the member connection graph to explore network vicinity; similarity-based CG leveraging learned member embeddings from profile, education, and skill data via a Two Tower Neural Network and nearest neighbor search; and heuristics-based CG applying simple interaction-based filters. Constraints include handling extremely large-scale data, avoiding computationally prohibitive scoring over the entire member base, and mitigating biases in embedding learning by using impressed candidates as positives and employing diverse negative sampling strategies. The CG stage produces a scored, aggregated candidate pool for ranking, optimizing diverse yet relevant candidate retrieval; offline metrics like recall@k and entropy guide evaluation, while A/B testing confirms gains in member engagement and retention, establishing candidate generation as critical for high-quality large-scale graph recommendation systems.

LinkedIn addresses the large-scale semantic retrieval challenge of recommending relevant connection candidates ("People You May Know") among over a billion members by employing a multi-stage ranking system tailored for efficient candidate selection and scoring. Intended users are LinkedIn members seeking valuable professional connections, with the business problem being the impossibility of exhaustively scoring hundreds of billions of pairwise invitations in real time. The solution involves an initial candidate generation stage that selects thousands of potential candidates from billions using graph and embedding-based retrieval, followed by lightweight and then deep neural ranking stages to calibrate and predict engagement likelihoods, and a final re-ranking stage optimizing fairness, diversity, and multi-objective parameters through Bayesian optimization. Important constraints include latency requirements and the necessity to aggregate diverse candidate sources, with metrics shifting from recall-focused early stages to precision and calibration in the final stages, validated through online A/B testing to capture real-world engagement improvements and guide continuous system enhancements.

Brief Me addresses the business challenge of rapidly extracting and synthesizing key information from large, diverse enterprise data sources—such as PDFs, Word documents, presentations, URLs, and intranet links—to enhance employee productivity by enabling conversational, real-time access to complex content. Intended for knowledge workers like sales reps overwhelmed by voluminous documents, the solution employs an agentic AI architecture featuring a two-stage system: low-latency online ingestion (fetching, chunking, embedding, indexing content) and conversational content generation using an operation planner that dynamically decides whether to search or read documents. It leverages hybrid semantic and keyword search via fine-tuned enterprise embedding models, contextual window expansions, and a map-reduce based generation algorithm to produce grounded, concise, multi-turn query responses along with paragraph-level citations. Evaluated on thousands of real-world enterprise queries for action accuracy, relevance, completeness, and groundedness, Brief Me streamlines knowledge discovery, reduces manual effort, and delivers trustworthy, verifiable insights across diverse business domains.

Expedia Group addresses the complexity of group travel planning and real-time trip management by introducing Romie™, an AI-driven travel assistant designed for travelers and groups seeking personalized, dynamic support. Romie leverages semantic retrieval by monitoring group chat conversations across platforms like SMS and WhatsApp to extract preferences and coordinate travel plans, integrating booking data and contextual information such as weather disruptions to provide proactive itinerary updates and alternatives. Key constraints include handling multifaceted user preferences and real-time event changes, while respecting user engagement levels by being assistive but non-intrusive. The solution aims to streamline the discovery, planning, booking, and in-trip assistance phases, enhancing traveler experience through intelligent summarization, personalized recommendations, and proactive disruption management, ultimately reducing planning effort and increasing trip satisfaction.

The Expedia Group lodging ranking system addresses the business challenge of efficiently selecting relevant lodging candidates for ranking under strict latency and data freshness constraints across multiple brands, targeting customers searching for accommodations within specific destinations. To achieve this, a two-stage recommendation approach is employed, where candidate generation narrows down properties before an expensive ranking phase that accounts for live availability and pricing data. The system uses machine-learning models trained on historical shopping logs to predict property relevance, incorporating static features (e.g., reviews, location), dynamic features (e.g., query parameters, non-live pricing signals), and user interaction history; when such data is unavailable, heuristic methods leveraging historical booking and click metrics normalized by visibility scores offer an alternative. Addressing the cold start problem for new listings, the solution applies mechanisms like interleaving new and established property selections and spatial indexing via H3 hexagons to ensure fair exposure. This pipeline balances predictive accuracy and efficiency, enabling improved recall of relevant properties, and is actively deployed across Expedia Group brands to optimize lodging recommendations.

OLX faced the challenge of unstructured job roles buried within job ad titles and descriptions, impairing efficient search and organization for job seekers. To address this, their intended users—job seekers and search platform teams—benefited from a solution leveraging the Prosus AI Assistant, a generative AI Large Language Model (LLM), to extract and normalize job roles into a hierarchical job taxonomy. This pipeline involved sampling and preprocessing 2,000 job ads, creating role taxonomies guided by high-frequency job-related keywords, and continuously extracting roles from new and updated ads through API calls integrated into their infrastructure. Key constraints included maintaining privacy with a zero-day data retention policy, the evolving nature of job categories requiring taxonomy updates, and managing approximately 4,000 daily API requests. Initial deployment improved retrieval precision in search results, enhancing user interaction metrics, though full impacts on ranking awaited further integration and data. Cost considerations, around $15K monthly for the AI service, prompted evaluation of future paths, potentially adopting self-hosted models for broader and cost-efficient extraction capabilities while maintaining rapid deployment advantages offered by the Prosus AI Assistant.

Mozilla addresses the accessibility problem where nearly half of web images lack alt text, impairing users relying on screen readers. Intended for Firefox users, especially those using assistive technologies, their solution employs compact Transformer-based models—combining Vision Transformers (ViT) and a distilled GPT-2 decoder—running entirely on-device to generate automatic alt text without sending images to external servers, thereby preserving user privacy. The approach integrates ONNX and Transformers.js within Firefox Nightly, initially targeting PDF editing via pdf.js to generate and validate alt descriptions, with models cached locally for efficiency and user control. Trained on datasets like COCO with iterative fine-tuning, this on-device semantic retrieval system balances brevity and accuracy in image captioning, offering improved transparency, environmental benefits, and the groundwork for future broad deployment in general web browsing.

GitHub addresses the business problem of securing codebases against vulnerabilities by providing developers with AI-powered semantic retrieval and automated fixing of security issues detected via CodeQL static analysis, particularly targeting JavaScript and TypeScript in pull requests. Intended for software developers and security teams, the solution leverages code scanning alerts enriched with context-aware snippets and vulnerability descriptions to generate precise LLM prompts that produce detailed natural language explanations and code edits, including dependency modifications, delivered as suggested fixes within pull request interfaces for review and direct committing. This approach relies on compact, context-sensitive code snippets, post-processing heuristics to correct model output, a rigorous automated test harness validating fixes against security alerts and test suites, and integration with existing code scanning workflows, all while maintaining privacy by collecting anonymized telemetry and implementing security guardrails against AI-specific risks. The expected outcome is a streamlined developer experience that improves remediation rates of security vulnerabilities with minimal manual effort, reducing turnaround time and enhancing overall code security.

Grammarly addresses the challenge of protecting users from sensitive or "delicate" text—emotionally charged, potentially triggering content that may not be overtly toxic but still poses a risk—by developing DeTexD, a benchmark dataset of labeled delicate texts sourced from controversial forums and news sites using keyword-based domain specification and expert annotation that includes risk-level ratings. Their approach fine-tunes a RoBERTa-based classifier to differentiate delicate text from toxic text, demonstrating that traditional toxic language detection models underperform on delicate topics such as mental health, violence, race, and sexuality, resulting in poor coverage or precision. The intended users are content moderation systems and AI agents requiring nuanced detection of emotionally sensitive text beyond overt toxicity, with the goal of safer AI and more comprehensive harmful content identification. The DeTexD dataset, annotation guidelines, and baseline model have been publicly released with caveats on privacy and ethics due to the inclusion of uncensored sensitive material.

Instacart’s Economics Team addressed the business challenge of optimizing authorization buffer amounts placed on customers’ credit cards at checkout—buffers that balance reducing unpaid amounts with minimizing customer friction from confusing holds—by employing regression discontinuity designs (RDD), a quasi-experimental econometric method leveraging natural breakpoints in buffer rounding. They analyzed local average treatment effects (LATE) at $5 rounding thresholds, comparing card decline rates and other metrics for orders just below and just above these cutoffs, under the assumption that customers near thresholds are statistically similar. This causal inference enabled the team to quantify the trade-offs between buffer size and decline rates, informing a revised policy that reduced upward rounding, validated by subsequent A/B tests which showed increased order volume via fewer card declines. The approach exemplifies using discontinuous thresholds common in consumer-facing products to improve decisions without initial randomized experiments, intending to evolve toward personalized authorization rules based on order context and customer history.

The business problem addressed is the difficulty of training machine learning classifiers on imbalanced text datasets, specifically within the context of legal invoice review for inconsistencies where minority class examples are scarce. Intended users are data scientists and ML practitioners seeking flexible, classifier-agnostic methods to improve minority class detection. The proposed solution focuses on data-level augmentation techniques rather than algorithmic modifications, employing multiple text augmentation methods including character-level (keyboard and OCR error simulation), word-level (contextual embedding and back-translation), sentence-level (contextual embeddings), and a novel keyword-to-sentence approach combining YAKE keyword extraction with GPT Neo sentence generation. Important data considerations include automated imbalance detection, train-test splitting to prevent leakage, and an inbuilt fine-tuned BERT classifier evaluated with metrics like Precision, Recall, Balanced Accuracy, and F-Beta. The expected outcome is enhanced minority class detection performance, with contextual word embedding augmentation yielding the best F1 score improvement (0.35 from baseline 0) and the keyword-to-sentence technique showing competitive gains, thereby providing a versatile, effective augmentation framework for imbalanced text classification in industrial legal audit contexts.

eBay addresses the complex business problem of enhancing developer productivity amidst rapid innovation by targeting three complementary AI-driven semantic retrieval and code assistance solutions for their developer community. The intended users are eBay software engineers who face challenges in managing a massive, multifaceted codebase and distributed internal knowledge scattered across platforms like GitHub, Jira, Slack, and Wikis. The first proposed solution involves expanding usage of commercial Large Language Models (LLMs) like GitHub Copilot to assist with code generation and testing, resulting in measurable improvements in coding efficiency and lead times but constrained by prompt size limits. The second solution fine-tunes open-source LLMs such as Code Llama by training on eBay’s proprietary code and documentation, enabling deeper context-aware tasks like complex software upkeep and reducing code duplication by encompassing broader internal knowledge beyond immediate dependencies. The third solution constructs an internal GPT-based knowledge base employing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with vector embeddings to semantically retrieve relevant documentation and API guidance from diverse data sources, thereby reducing investigation time and reliance on expert consultations. Together, these tracks utilize quantitative metrics (e.g., code acceptance rates, pull request times) and qualitative developer surveys under the constraint of handling vast, evolving internal data, with early outcomes showing increased productivity, improved context relevance, and ongoing refinement through user feedback and reinforcement learning to minimize erroneous outputs.

LinkedIn addresses the challenge of optimizing feed content relevance for diverse member engagement behaviors, including passive consumption, by leveraging dwell time—the duration users spend on posts—as a critical implicit feedback signal in its Feed ranking system. Intended for LinkedIn members who consume content variably across posts, articles, images, and videos, the solution uses a multi-objective, multi-task deep learning framework that integrates both active signals (likes, comments, reshares) and passive signals such as clicks and dwell time. To overcome challenges of noisy dwell time signals, static thresholds that introduce content-type biases, and evolving user behavior patterns, LinkedIn developed an auto-normalized long dwell model that dynamically computes dwell time percentiles conditioned on key attributes like content and creator types, enabling adaptive binary classification of long dwell engagement. This model's output is incorporated as a positive engagement signal with adjustable weight into the ranking multi-objective optimization, improving the relevance and quality of feed content while attenuating clickbait. Online A/B testing validated significant gains in session frequency, overall time spent, and passive user retention, demonstrating a more personalized, high-quality member experience on the LinkedIn Feed.

Coinbase addresses the challenge of unpredictable, volatile user traffic driven by crypto market fluctuations by deploying a machine learning classification model that predicts traffic spikes with a 60-minute lead time, enabling proactive vertical scaling of their databases. Unlike traditional reactive scaling based on lagging CPU metrics, this model incorporates platform load patterns and external signals such as cryptocurrency price volatility to forecast whether traffic will exceed critical thresholds, thereby triggering database scale-up before capacity is strained. The approach balances minimizing missed spikes—which can cause outages—and avoiding excessive scaling costs by tuning model sensitivity, converting predictions into a "scale target" metric used by an auto-scaler to adjust database resources dynamically. This solution overcomes the slow, inflexible nature of horizontal scaling and sharding in their single-writer per shard architecture, improving platform reliability and cost efficiency amid sudden market activity surges.

Slack addressed the business problem of unlocking AI-driven productivity gains for users facing information overload by building Slack AI with strict data privacy and security controls tailored for enterprise customers. Intended for Slack users, the solution employs Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with off-the-shelf large language models (LLMs) deployed within Slack’s trust boundary via an AWS-hosted escrow VPC to ensure customer data never leaves Slack’s controlled infrastructure. Slack AI operates only on data that each user is authorized to access, enforcing access control lists to prevent data leakage, while not training or fine-tuning models on customer data, preserving privacy and compliance such as FedRAMP Moderate. By combining stateless generative AI with enterprise-grade security, ephemeral data handling, and integration with Slack’s existing compliance infrastructure, the system delivers contextually relevant summarization and search, enhancing productivity without compromising data ownership or violating organizational data loss prevention policies.

Pinterest's ads ranking system faces challenges in translating offline machine learning model improvements, typically measured by ROC-AUC, into consistent online business metric gains such as cost-per-acquisition (CPA) during real-time ad serving. Intended for ads ranking engineers and data scientists, the solution involves rigorous offline training with historical data, coupled with online A/B experiments, but discrepancies arise due to misalignment between offline metrics (ROC-AUC) and online outcomes (CPA), feature delays, complex downstream bidding logic, and evolving data freshness. Bug-free scenarios expose nuanced metric correlations and limitations in modeling impacts on dynamic user traffic, while buggy scenarios highlight data inconsistencies, feature logging mismatches, model checkpoint issues, and traffic-induced latency causing null feature values. To address these, Pinterest employs advanced monitoring, feature validation pipelines, unified feature representations, robust model training frameworks, and systematic debugging processes, aiming to improve model robustness and online performance reliability in high-scale recommendation systems.

Pinterest addressed the challenge of optimizing ad conversion prediction, which suffers from sparse, noisy, and delayed conversion labels, by evolving their ads ranking system from Gradient Boosted Decision Trees with logistic regression to advanced Deep Neural Networks featuring Multi-Task Learning (MTL) that co-train multiple conversion-related objectives. Their solution integrates state-of-the-art feature interaction modules—including DCNv2, transformer-based self-attention, and MaskNet instance-guided masking—and employs in-model ensembles combining diverse backbones for improved robustness. Incorporating user sequence modeling enabled temporal and contextual understanding of user behavior, critical for sparse event prediction. To manage scalability and infrastructure costs amid complex large-scale models serving nearly 500 million monthly users, Pinterest transitioned to GPU-based serving with CUDA graph optimizations and mixed precision inference. This comprehensive approach enhanced offline and online conversion metrics, enabling advertisers to better target Promoted Pins for actions like checkouts and signups while maintaining low latency and manageable compute resources.

Mercado Libre addressed the challenge of enabling developers and business analysts to efficiently retrieve and generate accurate, company-specific technical and data documentation by implementing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system using Large Language Models (LLMs) combined with an indexed knowledge base, mitigating the limitation that LLMs lack proprietary internal knowledge. They enhanced incomplete or inconsistent documentation, especially for thousands of under-documented data tables, using LLMs to auto-generate richer, standardized descriptions which were iteratively refined through prompt engineering and quality assurance to meet user needs. Additionally, they improved natural language query understanding, such as interpreting ambiguous date references and product unit details, by leveraging LLM function-calling features to extract structured information from raw input text, exemplified in use cases like expert booking systems. This multi-faceted approach aimed to provide precise, context-aware responses to complex internal inquiries, streamline user workflows, and reduce manual documentation burdens, demonstrating the practical deployment of LLMs beyond raw language modeling through data preparation, iterative improvement, and system integration for enhanced semantic retrieval.

Dropbox’s AI/ML security research identified a novel vulnerability in ChatGPT models (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) allowing extraction of memorized training data through "repeated token divergence attacks," where sequences of repeated single or multi-token inputs cause the models to bypass prompt guardrails and produce hallucinatory or leakage-prone outputs. This security flaw, transferable to other open-source models, poses risks including exposure of sensitive data and enables adversarial denial-of-service via long running prompts causing resource exhaustion. The research led to coordinated disclosure to OpenAI, which implemented prompt filtering and request timeouts to mitigate single-token repetition, but initially overlooked multi-token sequences until Dropbox’s findings prompted expanded defenses. The intended users are AI/ML security practitioners who require detection mechanisms; Dropbox plans to release a tool to help mitigate such attacks by sanitizing prompt inputs and enforcing token usage constraints, aiming to safeguard AI-powered offerings and prevent training data leakage and computational abuse in deployed language model applications.

DoorDash addresses the complex business problem of delivering highly accurate estimated time of arrival (ETA) predictions crucial for operational efficiency and customer satisfaction in food delivery by developing an advanced machine learning model for internal and consumer use. Intended users include customers tracking deliveries and DoorDash’s operational teams optimizing logistics. The solution employs an MLP-gated mixture of experts architecture with parallel encoders—DeepNet for nonlinear feature interactions, CrossNet for explicit feature crossing, and a transformer for sequential time series features—leveraging rich embeddings of categorical variables, bucketized numerical inputs, and minute-level order volume time series to capture temporal, spatial, and contextual patterns across diverse delivery scenarios. Multitask learning with sequential training harmonizes ETA predictions across browsing and checkout stages, enhancing consistency and knowledge transfer. Additionally, probabilistic modeling with interval regression of Weibull distributions estimates uncertainty, providing not just point predictions but credible intervals for ETAs. This comprehensive approach overcame challenges like high-cardinality categorical data, temporal dynamics, and distributional tail modeling, resulting in a 20% relative accuracy improvement, reducing surprises in delivery times, improving customer trust, operational efficiency, and enabling better Dasher allocation and route planning.

Foodpanda’s Marketplace Balance project addresses the business problem of harmonizing customer demand and rider supply to optimize budget allocation for Customer Acquisition & Retention Cost (CARC) and rider incentives, ensuring efficient order fulfillment and economic sustainability. Intended for managing directors and city-level budget planners, the solution employs machine learning to analyze historical data on order trends, peak demand, and rider availability, forecasting key metrics such as Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), Fully Loaded Gross Profit per Order (FLGPO), and Cost per Order (CPO). Delivered through a Tableau dashboard, the tool offers scenario-based budget recommendations and visualizes trade-offs between growth and profitability, calibrated on daily, weekly, and monthly granularities for restaurants and delivery in specific cities. Constraints exclude external disruptions like weather and competitor promotions, focusing on predictable periods to improve accuracy. The expected outcome is a data-driven, user-friendly recommendation system that enables strategic budgeting decisions balancing demand stimulation and rider supply, thus maximizing profitability while maintaining rider satisfaction and operational efficiency.

foodpanda’s Marketplace Balance Project addresses the business problem of optimising budget allocation to maximise Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) without diminishing returns, targeting data analysts and decision-makers managing marketing spend. The solution involves predictive modeling of budget-to-GMV relationships using granular daily data to preserve detail and employing machine learning techniques that capture nonlinear dynamics, including Linear Regression, Polynomial Regression, tree-based models, and ultimately a Generalised Additive Model (GAM). Constraints include managing error rates measured by Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and ensuring the model reflects realistic budget impact patterns—specifically a saturation effect rather than a decline in GMV with increased budget. The expected outcome is an interpretable, flexible forecasting model with MAPE below 10%, enabling more accurate budget optimisation that accounts for the tapering effect on returns as budget increases.

The Marketplace Balance Project at foodpanda addresses the business problem of optimizing budget allocation amid unpredictable market dynamics, such as weather fluctuations, vendor promotions, and competitor campaigns, which are challenging to capture in data. Intended users include project stakeholders and the cross-functional team responsible for budget management. The proposed solution involves employing machine learning within an Agile framework, supported by Kanban for task tracking, to iteratively refine budget optimization despite uncertainties and volatile variables categorized as out of scope. Key constraints include incomplete access to volatile variable data and evolving stakeholder requirements, managed through transparent communication and servant leadership. The expected outcome is a flexible, data-driven project delivering optimized budgeting decisions, enhanced stakeholder alignment, and sustained project knowledge for future application in marketplace balance.

Yelp faces the business problem of maintaining content integrity by detecting and removing inappropriate user reviews containing hate speech, lewdness, threats, or harassment to preserve consumer trust. Intended users include Yelp’s User Operations team and consumers relying on trustworthy reviews. To address this, Yelp developed an AI pipeline leveraging fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) trained on a carefully curated dataset of flagged and annotated reviews, augmented with sentence embedding similarity techniques and sampling strategies to balance sub-categories of inappropriate content. Key constraints involve high precision requirements due to the low prevalence of spam in live traffic and the challenge of detecting nuanced language like sarcasm or metaphors. The deployed LLM models classify reviews in real-time with a threshold calibrated via mock traffic simulations, enabling proactive filtering before publication, resulting in the prevention of over 23,600 harmful reviews in 2023 and improving moderation efficiency while continuing to incorporate user reports for ongoing model refinement.

Yelp addresses the business problem of ensuring trust and safety by moderating inappropriate video content uploaded alongside user reviews to prevent the display of nudity, violence, extremist symbols, and other disturbing material. The intended users include both Yelp consumers and businesses relying on a safe platform. The proposed solution employs a hybrid moderation pipeline where uploaded videos first undergo similarity hashing against flagged content to auto-block repeat offenders, followed by a deep learning multi-label classification model—adapted from Yelp's proven photo moderation system—that processes selectively sampled frames to balance near real-time inference with accuracy. Videos flagged above classification thresholds are hidden and reviewed by human moderators to minimize false positives and maintain user trust. Critical constraints include managing large video data sizes, minimizing false positive rates to avoid discouraging user participation, and scaling moderation efficiently to handle increasing video upload volumes. The expected outcome is a robust, scalable system that swiftly detects and removes inappropriate videos, thereby protecting Yelp’s community and preserving its reputation as a trusted review platform.

Faire, a global wholesale marketplace, faced the business problem of improving product search relevance to help retailers reliably discover products, as irrelevant results eroded user trust. Their intended users are retailers searching for products, who benefit from more semantically relevant search results based on a clear ESCI framework that classifies relevance into Exact, Substitute, Complement, and Irrelevant tiers. The proposed solution involved fine-tuning open-source large language models—specifically Llama3–8b using parameter-efficient LoRA adapters and substantial labeled datasets—to predict semantic relevance, replacing costly manual labeling and external GPT API reliance. Key constraints included the subjectivity of relevance definitions, sparse engagement data, demand for high throughput to score tens of millions of query-product pairs daily, and operational efficiency requirements addressed through techniques like quantization, batching, and GPU scaling. The expected outcome was a 28% relative accuracy improvement in semantic relevance prediction over prior GPT models, enabling daily, scalable relevance measurements that facilitated downstream search optimization and personalization analytics, with future plans to incorporate multimodal data and real-time inference.

Faire faced the business challenge of enabling retailers on their wholesale marketplace to efficiently find relevant products despite vocabulary mismatches and ambiguous queries, which traditional keyword-based search using Elasticsearch and BM25 struggled with. The intended users are retail buyers seeking products by descriptive or nuanced terms that may not exactly match product metadata. Their solution introduces embedding-based semantic retrieval using two-tower deep learning models combining text and multimodal (image) embeddings to capture query-product relationships beyond keywords. This system integrates real-time approximate nearest neighbor search with hybrid retrieval blending embeddings and keyword matches, augmented by geographic filters and a multi-stage architecture including query parsing, ranking, re-ranking, and presentation. Key constraints included maintaining low latency and validating embedding benefits via a minimum viable product with cache-based serving before scaling. Expected outcomes comprise improved relevance, search flexibility, robustness to misspellings, scalability, and increased conversion from enhanced semantic understanding of user intent and product content.

Amazon addresses the challenge of improving product recommendations by enabling commonsense reasoning to infer contextual product relevance, such as linking "shoes for pregnant women" to slip-resistant shoes. To support this, they developed COSMO, a framework that constructs a commonsense knowledge graph from customer interaction data using a recursive process with large language models (LLMs), human annotation, and machine learning classification to identify and codify implicit relationships like used_for_audience or capableOf. The knowledge graph is built from pruned query-purchase and co-purchase data pairs and refines relationship hypotheses through filtering and human review, culminating in entity-relation-entity triples that enhance product understanding. Evaluated on the Shopping Queries Data Set from KDD Cup 2022 via bi-encoder and cross-encoder models, incorporating COSMO relationships significantly improved recommendation relevance, achieving up to 60% increase in macro F1 score with frozen encoders and maintaining over 20% improvement after fine-tuning, demonstrating COSMO’s efficacy in aiding semantic retrieval for nuanced product recommendation tasks in commerce.

Amazon's Project P.I. addresses the challenge of preventing imperfect or defective products—such as damaged, expired, or mislabeled items—from reaching customers through fulfillment centers by leveraging machine learning, computer vision (CV), optical character recognition (OCR), and generative AI models, including multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Fulfillment center imaging tunnels capture product visuals that CV models analyze for defects by comparing them against normal product images, while OCR verifies labeling like expiration dates. Customer feedback data further refines the models to detect more subtle product issues. Generative AI synthesizes image data and customer complaints to identify root causes and enable faster, targeted corrective actions. The solution employs AWS services like Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker to scale detection across millions of items monthly, improving product quality, reducing returns, and enhancing customer trust by intercepting defects prior to shipping. The approach also integrates multimodal AI for zero-shot damage recognition and supports collaboration with sellers by sharing defect insights to prevent recurring errors.

Zapier addresses the challenge of automating diverse business operations to enhance efficiency and strategic focus by enabling 97% of employees to use AI-powered workflows. Intended users span multiple departments including customer success, sales, HR, technical support, content creation, PR, user education, engineering, accounting, and revenue operations. The proposed solution leverages Zapier’s AI tools and MCP platform to build semantic retrieval–enabled automations that integrate over 9,000 apps, facilitating tasks such as summarizing calls, detecting fraudulent job applicants, generating content drafts, translating video captions, and automating personalized emails. AI models analyze and synthesize data from CRM records, Slack communications, Zendesk tickets, and internal documentation under defined constraints to deliver context-aware summaries, risk flags, search results, and dynamic content generation. The expected outcome is increased operational scalability, reduced manual overhead, improved data-driven insights, and accelerated workflows that allow employees to focus on creative and strategic initiatives while maintaining security and reliability at scale.

Algolia AI Personalization addresses the business challenge of delivering precisely tailored digital content to each online visitor by leveraging behavioral data, preferences, and attributes, even without explicit user input. Intended primarily for merchandisers and developers in commerce companies, the solution integrates AI/ML-driven personalization across multiple touchpoints including search, browse, and discovery, harmonizing user experience, business ROI, and technical scalability. Important components include personalized search results, autocomplete suggestions, faceted search prioritization, recommendation systems, and inline segmentation, all supported via APIs and a unified platform enabling continuous fine-tuning rather than a one-time setup. Expected outcomes are improved user engagement, streamlined setup and optimization, enriched customer journeys, and increased customer lifetime value through scalable, data-driven orchestration of personalized experiences.

Booking.com addresses the business challenge of delivering scalable, personalized travel recommendations to diverse users—ranging from new visitors to returning customers with browsing history—by developing a self-serve Machine Learning (ML) recommendation platform that supports various use cases such as hotels, destinations, flights, and attractions. Intended for internal product teams, the platform employs a modular recommendation pipeline that processes user requests through stages including prediction (via multiple ML models arranged in prediction graphs), dynamic filtering (e.g., for blacklisted locations or current hotel availability), enrichment with localized content, and selection/sorting based on user preferences. Features are rigorously defined and reusable, enabling teams to compose tailored recommendation strategies efficiently using registered components, promoting collaboration and scalability. The system leverages real-time data and experiment-driven design to optimize recommendation relevance and responsiveness despite evolving external factors, with the expected outcome of enhancing customer experience and empowering teams to innovate rapidly with consistent, high-quality ML-driven recommendations across Booking.com’s ecosystem.

Enterprises face escalating complexity and volume in software vulnerabilities reported in the CVE database, making traditional manual scanning and patching unmanageable. Intended for security analysts and software publishers, the proposed solution leverages a generative AI system, “Agent Morpheus,” that integrates retrieval-augmented generation and multiple fine-tuned Llama3 large language models in an event-driven workflow. By autonomously generating tailored checklists, synthesizing data from vulnerability databases, threat intelligence, source code, SBOMs, and other context, Agent Morpheus determines the exploitability of detected CVEs rather than merely their presence, thus prioritizing critical security risks. It handles challenges such as unavailable patched versions and complex dependency constraints, automates version comparisons, and runs analyses in parallel to accelerate triage from days to seconds. The system produces machine-readable VEX justification documents, integrates with container registries and security dashboards for automatic triggering and human-in-the-loop review, and continuously improves through feedback-driven model retraining, ultimately enabling enterprises to efficiently manage CVE risks at scale while minimizing unnecessary patching and operational delays.

Mercado Libre addresses the business challenge of delivering personalized marketing to distinct user profiles—Persuadable, Loyal, Unpersuadable, and Beware—by leveraging semantic retrieval-based Machine Learning (ML) and AI solutions, specifically through predictive Lookalike Models that identify new potential customers sharing characteristics with valuable existing users. Intended for marketing and business teams lacking deep ML expertise, the solution uses a no-code AutoML platform (Dataiku) enabling users to select seed groups, define relevant behavioral and demographic features across Fintech, Commerce, and Cross domains, train models with advanced algorithms like XGBoost and LightGBM, and conduct backtesting on historical campaign data for validation. This process culminates in predictive scoring of users into deciles, facilitating targeted and efficient campaign deployment via BigQuery integration. By democratizing ML through an intuitive wizard interface and structured onboarding with beta users, Mercado Libre boosts campaign conversion rates, reduces acquisition costs, and improves user engagement while minimizing spam, thus maximizing ROI and enabling scalable, self-service model management across the organization.

GetYourGuide addresses the business challenge of delivering highly personalized and relevant search rankings for millions of users by making over 30 million real-time predictions daily with strict latency requirements under 80 milliseconds. The intended users are travelers seeking tailored activity recommendations on their platform. Their solution integrates diverse, real-time user interaction and activity features sourced from Kafka streams and data warehouses, engineered via Tecton's feature platform to enable low-latency, scalable, and cost-efficient feature pipelines, including novel features like position-discounted impression counts. Model training is automated daily using Airflow with point-in-time accurate feature retrieval from Tecton's offline store, and models are managed with MLFlow and monitored in production through Arize’s observability tools to detect feature and performance drift. Serving is implemented using FastAPI within Docker on Kubernetes, supporting A/B testing with feature freshness monitoring and autoscaling to handle seasonal traffic. This end-to-end ML system facilitates rapid iteration and experimentation while maintaining performance and reliability, ultimately enhancing user personalization and business impact in travel activity discovery.

GetYourGuide addresses the challenge of managing and optimizing millions of diverse travel-related images from partners, tour providers, and travelers to enhance customer visual experience across product and marketing channels. Intended for internal teams including software engineers, branding, and marketing, the solution involves a multi-stage image lifecycle: safe-for-work moderation contextualized by tour type, virus scanning, deduplication using image hashing, and storage in an object repository. Computer vision techniques such as external API annotation (e.g., Google Vision), custom classification models for brand alignment, and generation of smart crops optimize serving images in various contexts. To tackle redundancy and enhance diversity, they employ advanced image similarity detection using EfficientNet-derived embeddings combined with FAISS for scalable nearest neighbor search, enabling filtering of near-identical images for marketing use. This approach leverages domain-specific constraints like contextual relevance and storage efficiency, resulting in improved visual content curation that elevates traveler engagement and broadens marketing reach.

The use case addresses the challenge travelers face in finding accommodations that match complex, context-specific needs, such as "family-friendly beaches," which are difficult to capture with simple attributes; the intended users are travelers seeking personalized lodging recommendations and search results. The proposed solution involves learning a common semantic embedding space for hotels and travel concepts by leveraging traveler reviews annotated with sentiment via an in-house tagging system, thereby avoiding costly human labeling. Using a two-tower neural architecture, the model generates embeddings for hotels and concepts, enabling fast similarity-based retrieval through cached embeddings and ranking loss training on positive and negative examples derived from review data. Important data includes one year of reservations and associated reviews enriched with sentiment-labeled concepts; constraints involve efficiently inferring similarity scores and capturing nuanced traveler opinions. The expected outcome is improved search and recommendation relevance, demonstrated by retrieving hotels that semantically align with queried concepts like “Sea” or “Wedding hotels,” enhancing the user experience in lodging travel domains.

The Video Annotator (VA) framework addresses the inefficiencies and high costs of traditional video classification model development, which often rely on disjointed annotation by domain experts and modeling by data scientists, leading to delays, inconsistent labels, and model drift. Targeted at domain experts and video analysts, VA integrates active learning with zero-shot vision-language models to enable an interactive, human-in-the-loop annotation and training workflow that focuses expert effort on progressively harder examples through iterative search, classification, and review steps. By using this approach, users can efficiently build and refine binary video classifiers for granular video understanding—critical for applications like content search, personalization, and promotion—without needing constant data scientist intervention. The system supports continuous annotation and rapid model deployment, monitoring, and updating, improving sample efficiency and reducing costs. In experiments over 56 diverse labels and 500k video shots, VA achieved an average precision improvement of 8.3 points compared to strong baselines, underscoring its effectiveness in producing high-quality video classifiers within scalable, extensible, self-service workflows that enhance model trust and ownership among domain experts.

Netflix addresses the business problem of accurately measuring and projecting the long-term causal impact of product changes on member engagement and revenue, serving internal data science teams and decision-makers. To solve challenges such as limited A/B test duration, heterogeneous treatment effects, and non-response bias in survey data, Netflix employs advanced causal inference techniques including surrogate indexing, synthetic control variations, double machine learning with propensity scoring, and combined propensity scores with iterative proportional fitting. These methods enable automation of annualized impact estimation from short-term experimental data, robust evaluation of game events where randomized control is infeasible, fair comparison of tradeoffs among conflicting metrics, and improved survey result validity. Thoughtful UI/UX design within their experimentation platform further facilitates user interpretation and decision-making, culminating in faster, more accurate insights that enhance member satisfaction and business growth.

Netflix developed a reverse search capability within their federated graph search system to address the challenge of dynamically notifying users like Post Production Coordinators about items of interest—for example, movies that match evolving criteria—without burdening the ecosystem with frequent broad queries. Instead of the conventional approach of retrieving documents matching a query, reverse search identifies which saved queries match a newly updated document using Elasticsearch's percolator fields and queries. Saved searches, defined in Netflix’s custom Graph Search DSL and stored in CockroachDB, are indexed as percolate queries in separate percolate indices to optimize performance and support versioning through parallel pipelines and index aliasing. This solution enables precise, efficient event-driven notifications and automatic classification tasks, such as assigning movie workflows based on complex multi-attribute criteria, by submitting movie documents to the reverse search endpoint. The system supports over 100 integrated applications with nearly 50 indices, and future extensions envision real-time subscription updates via GraphQL as index changes occur.

LinkedIn addresses the challenge of matching members with the appropriate Premium product by developing a unified machine learning platform that personalizes recommendations based on member needs, context, and feedback. Intended for LinkedIn professionals, job seekers, and small businesses, the system leverages member profile, activity, and derived AI data, combined with multi-modal creative content (text, promotions, calls to action) across various channels, to optimize which product, creative format, and channel to use or whether to withhold messaging. The platform employs a two-tower neural network architecture to pre-compute embeddings for efficient real-time inference, integrates deep matching to predict interaction likelihood, and applies an explore/exploit reinforcement learning strategy to balance personalization and data collection. Offline batch retraining with continuous feedback enables rapid experimentation and improved conversion metrics without harming retention. The approach solves the complex semantic retrieval problem of selecting the most relevant, time-sensitive product promotion to maximize member lifetime value and engagement, with future plans involving deep reinforcement learning and generative AI to enhance long-term, personalized career support.

Instacart addresses the business problem of suggesting suitable replacements for out-of-stock grocery items to enhance customer satisfaction, targeting both customers and shoppers. The proposed solution is a machine-learning-driven replacement recommendation system that generates candidate substitutes through heuristics combining engagement data, taxonomy, aisle location, and semantic similarity, followed by a supervised deep-learning ranking model using a Siamese network architecture incorporating text, categorical, binary dietary features, and pre-trained product embeddings. The model balances challenges such as the "head vs tail" problem by integrating an engagement memorization model for popular products, and mitigates retailer bias by updating the schema to a retailer-aware format, enabling tailored suggestions that consider retailer-specific inventory and customer preferences. Training data derives from customer replacement impressions, with model evaluation via validation loss, AUC, MRR, Recall@k, and A/B testing on customer approval and replacement satisfaction. The expected outcome is a more precise, personalized, and context-aware replacement system that improves replacement acceptance rates and overall shopping experience despite unavailable products.

This use case addresses the business problem of improving the speed and accuracy of customer service technical support by retrieving relevant past issue tickets to answer user inquiries. Intended users are customer service agents who rely on historical issue data for troubleshooting customer problems. The proposed solution integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a knowledge graph (KG) that captures both intra-issue structures and inter-issue relations, preserving rich hierarchical and relational information from issue tickets rather than treating them as plain text chunks. The KG construction involves parsing tickets into tree structures, linking them explicitly and implicitly via semantic similarity, and generating embeddings for efficient vector-based retrieval. During question answering, the system identifies entities and intents using large language models (LLMs), retrieves pertinent subgraphs from the KG, and uses LLMs to generate precise, complete answers. Constraints include handling structured issue tickets with hierarchical and relational links, and managing text length within embedding limits. Empirical results demonstrate a 77.6% improvement in Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) for retrieval accuracy and a 0.32 increase in BLEU score for answer quality over baselines, leading to a 28.6% reduction in median issue resolution time in production at LinkedIn.

Wayfair addresses the business problem of enhancing digital sales agents' efficiency and customer service quality during live shopping interactions by deploying Agent Co-Pilot, a generative AI assistant powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). Intended for digital sales agents, the Co-Pilot provides real-time, context-aware chat response suggestions by incorporating relevant product information, company policies, detailed conversation history, and task-specific instructions into sophisticated AI prompts. The solution relies on analyzing multi-turn conversations and dynamically generating accurate, policy-compliant, and helpful text, thereby reducing agents’ response time and cognitive load. Key constraints include maintaining adherence to internal guidelines, ensuring factual accuracy, and minimizing hallucinations or errors in product or policy data. Evaluation metrics such as average handle time reduction, edit rates, and response quality assessments guide ongoing improvements.
