Initial results show a 10% decrease in handle time with plans to augment context via Retrieval Augmented Generation and fine-tune the model’s conversational tone to better emulate top agents, aiming to boost customer satisfaction and conversion rates through enhanced semantic retrieval and AI-assisted sales dialogue.

Cloudflare addresses the challenge of detecting sophisticated bot attacks that exploit residential proxies—networks of IPs sourced from compromised residential devices often used to bypass traditional defenses like IP blocking and rate-limiting—by developing an advanced machine learning model (version 8) aimed at security engineers combating online abuse. This ML-based Bot Management system analyzes vast volumes of global HTTP request data in real time, leveraging features derived from individual request fingerprints, behavioral patterns, and large-scale network statistics. Given the high diversity and rotation of residential proxy IPs, which mimic legitimate user traffic, the solution combines network latency analysis and behavioral signals on a per-request basis rather than relying solely on IP reputation, thus minimizing false positives that could impact benign users. Training involves curated datasets, including labeled attack data and heuristics, orchestrated via Apache Airflow pipelines for robust validation and explainability using techniques like SHAP. Deployment is gradual, moving from shadow mode to active use, with demonstrated improvements including 95% accurate classification of residential proxy-driven attacks (such as account takeovers and content scraping) and enhanced detection of bot traffic from cloud provider IPs. The expected outcome is a more precise and scalable defense system that effectively mitigates distributed bot threats while preserving legitimate residential traffic.

This use case addresses the business problem of ensuring digital trust in financial services by verifying user identity and transaction authorization through continuous fraud detection in digital banking. Targeted at banks and financial institutions, the solution integrates Feedzai’s Digital Trust system, which collects heterogeneous data—including behavioral biometrics (keystrokes, mouse movements, touch gestures), device and network information, and user operation patterns—throughout a user’s digital banking session. It employs a holistic fraud detection strategy combining expert rules, heuristics, and advanced machine learning models capable of processing high-volume, imbalanced, and multimodal data to identify suspicious sessions early without disrupting legitimate users. Key constraints include minimal user friction, low latency for real-time risk scoring, and scalability to handle tens of thousands of sessions per second. The expected outcome is significantly improved fraud detection accuracy and timely risk alerts that enable financial institutions to proactively prevent fraudulent activities while maintaining a seamless user experience.

Wix addressed the challenges of real-world collections income forecasting—such as frequent retraining needs, high forecast variance, dependency on external factors, data splitting trade-offs, and costly hyperparameter tuning—by implementing the TiDE (Time-series Dense Encoder) deep learning model, which offers faster training via MLP architecture and supports exogenous covariates. Intended for data scientists and business stakeholders at Wix, their solution features regular retraining enabled by TiDE’s computational efficiency, ensemble forecasting to reduce variance and stabilize predictions, a tailored training-validation split allowing recent trends to inform long-horizon forecasts, and efficient hyperparameter optimization using Optuna with rolling cross-validation. This integrated approach led to a 40% improvement in forecast accuracy, enhancing stakeholders’ trust and enabling better decision-making in collections management.

Zectonal, a software company focused on monitoring multimodal data for defects and anomalies to protect data lakes and AI analytics, developed a high-performance, secure, and auditable autonomous AI agentic framework entirely in Rust to overcome Python’s limitations in concurrency and reliability. Their framework enables specialized AI agents to call efficient, Rust-implemented diagnostic algorithms known as “needle in the haystack” function tools, thereby scaling data quality inspection beyond predefined rules by leveraging LLM-driven function tool calling via OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama APIs. Critical to their solution is "Agent Provenance," which tracks and audits agent communications and decisions, enhancing transparency and optimizing agent behavior through embedded utility functions measuring intent and confidence. The framework supports hybrid deployment (cloud, on-premise via Ollama), enabling extensibility, cost management, and security compliance for enterprise users concerned about data sovereignty and AI hallucinations. Zectonal is also experimenting with meta AI agents capable of autonomously generating new agents and software tools to address evolving needs, fueling advanced automation while addressing governance and cost challenges inherent in scaling agent populations.

The Snorkel Flow label model addresses the business problem of efficiently generating high-quality labeled training datasets for machine learning by leveraging expert-driven labeling functions (LFs) that vote on data instances. Intended for data scientists and ML practitioners in enterprise settings, the solution improves upon traditional majority vote models—which assume equal LF quality, independent errors, and class frequency correlations—and more complex graphical models, which are computationally intensive. The Snorkel Flow label model integrates existing ground truth data to calibrate LF weights based on precision and class distribution, providing faster runtime and lower memory use without sacrificing accuracy, typically improving accuracy by 1-2%. This balance of speed, memory efficiency, and robustness enables rapid iterative refinement of labeling functions, accelerating the path to production-ready ML applications for real-world complex datasets.

Doctolib, a leading European e-health company, addresses the business problem of enhancing customer care by enabling health professionals to manage and respond efficiently to patient inquiries, aiming to reduce agent workload and improve user experience. The intended users are customer care agents and healthcare practitioners who require accurate, context-specific information beyond static FAQs. Starting with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), they combined large language models (GPT-4o) with an up-to-date FAQ knowledge base embedded in a vector database (OpenSearch), supplemented by re-ranking and daily embedding updates, to dynamically retrieve relevant documents and generate factually accurate, relevant answers with tailored metrics for evaluation such as context precision, recall, faithfulness, and answer relevancy. Constraints include maintaining data confidentiality, reducing high latency (optimized from one minute to under five seconds), and handling diverse, complex queries where simplistic rule-based bots or static LLMs fall short. The outcome was a 20% deflection in customer care cases, enabling agents to prioritize complex issues, enhanced precision through a machine learning classifier that predicts answerability of queries, and improved UX designed with interaction and latency challenges in mind. Recognizing RAG’s limitations with complex questions and conversational capabilities, Doctolib is exploring agentic AI frameworks where multiple LLM agents interact, perform actions, and enrich query understanding to further elevate system robustness and user engagement.

Agoda addressed the business challenge of long and unreliable response times—averaging eight hours and with only 55% of messages answered—from property owners on their Customer Messaging platform, which hindered users seeking specific accommodation details like amenities. Targeting travelers using Agoda’s website and app, they developed the Property AMA Bot, an AI-powered chatbot leveraging prompt engineering, Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, and integration with Agoda’s Property API to provide instant, accurate, and contextually informed answers across platforms. The system uses input topic guardrails to restrict out-of-scope queries, continuous data-driven evaluation with response labeling and A/B testing to refine performance, and aims to act as a professional customer service agent. Expected outcomes include drastically reduced response times from hours to seconds, enhanced user experience, increased engagement, and more confident booking decisions, with future expansions planned to incorporate modular AI Agents for broader, multi-domain travel-related queries.

Careem addresses the business problem of fraudulent duplicate Captain accounts—created to access excessive orders and bonuses—by using facial recognition technology to maintain platform balance and fairness for drivers and customers. Intended users include the Captains and Careem’s fraud detection team. The solution leverages machine learning-based facial recognition to process over two million Captain photos stored on Amazon S3, extracting facial embeddings via a pre-trained open-source model, which are stored and searched efficiently using FAISS-GPU for scalable similarity detection. Constraints include handling variable image quality, background noise, and false positives caused by non-face objects like portraits. The system uses Euclidean distance thresholds and manual fraud analyst reviews to flag and block active duplicate accounts while avoiding wrongful blocking of legitimate cases. The outcome is the identification and prevention of over 2,000 fraudulent accounts, improving platform integrity, trust, and operational fairness, alongside enhanced registration procedures to deter future duplicates.

Doctolib tackled the challenge of enhancing customer care by developing an advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system based on an agentic architecture utilizing LLM-based AI agents. These multi-agent frameworks enable natural language interaction through a primary assistant that routes user queries to specialized assistants confined to specific scopes, each equipped with tools such as FAQ search, data fetching, API calls, and sensitive action execution validated by user consent. Implemented using LangGraph for its multi-agent orchestration and integration with LangChain, the solution addresses complex workflows with multi-step reasoning and tool use, aiming to reduce hallucinations and increase system robustness. Key constraints include non-deterministic LLM behavior causing inconsistent tool invocation and large prompt sizes impacting performance, mitigated by limiting agent scope and improving labeled data. The system heavily relies on structured functional data governance and comprehensive API documentation to accurately translate user natural language intent into actionable applicative commands, fostering scalability and reducing ambiguity. Despite promising demonstrations like managing agenda access requests, challenges remain in evaluation, production deployment, cross-team collaboration, and maintaining up-to-date, well-structured data assets crucial for reliable and scalable AI-driven customer support.

Quora’s ML Platform team addressed the challenge of efficiently retrieving relevant content for personalized recommendations and knowledge retrieval by overhauling their embedding search system, primarily used in candidate retrieval and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for their Poe platform. Previously relying on two in-house systems—one matrix-based with slow scalability and one HNSW-based that lacked incremental update support—they sought a solution that offered low latency, horizontal scalability for hundreds of millions of embeddings, bulk loading for daily model refreshes, and operational simplicity suitable for a small team. After evaluating open-source libraries, vector databases, and SaaS options, they selected Qdrant due to its high performance, distributed architecture, built-in monitoring, support for filtering with metadata, bulk snapshot loading, and ease of operation. The new architecture incorporates a proxy service for unified API access and migration support and handles embedding updates via real-time Kafka ingestion and offline snapshot restoration, mitigating data loss through an online/offline sub-collection strategy. Key operational learnings involve judicious use of Qdrant’s standalone versus distributed modes, quantization trade-offs affecting recall and disk I/O, and managing shard transfer overhead. This transition improved search speed, flexibility, and scalability, enabling new features and better integration of embedding updates in real-time, significantly enhancing user experience on Quora’s platforms.

Coupang leverages large language models (LLMs) and multi-modal deep learning to address complex e-commerce challenges in multilingual content understanding, product categorization, recommendation, and logistics optimization. By training on large datasets comprising text, images, and user interactions in Korean, Mandarin, and English, they enhance search relevance, ad retrieval, and attribute extraction using vision-language transformers and foundation models like Qwen, LLAMA, and CLIP. To overcome sparse human-labeled data, LLMs generate high-quality weak labels at scale, enabling improved model training in under-resourced languages. Coupang’s ML platform supports hybrid multi-region GPU clusters using Nvidia A100/H100 GPUs, containerized distributed training (via Polyaxon, DeepSpeed Zero), and GPU-accelerated inference (Nvidia Triton, Ray, vLLM) to efficiently train and serve billion-parameter LLMs. Their development lifecycle includes rapid exploration, fine-tuning, distillation for real-time inference, and embedding extraction for retrieval tasks, all constrained by GPU supply and compute cost. The resulting system improves personalization, search, catalog quality, and operational forecasting, delivering better customer experiences across their marketplace.

Faire addresses the challenge of accelerating and improving code review productivity for software engineers by implementing an LLM-powered automated review pipeline integrated with GitHub webhooks. Their solution, built around Fairey, an LLM orchestrator leveraging Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), processes pull request metadata, diffs, build logs, and test coverage reports to autonomously perform generic code review tasks such as style enforcement, build failure diagnostics, backward-incompatibility detection, and test coverage analysis. A key use case is the automated test coverage review, which, using Jest-generated coverage data and source/test file mappings, identifies untested code changes and suggests new test cases, all coordinated through assistant prompts and function calls within Fairey. Review quality is continuously evaluated via an LLM-based quantitative framework and developer feedback collected through a productivity platform, enabling iterative prompt refinement and enhanced consistency, conciseness, and correctness. This semantic retrieval-driven automation reduces review latency, allowing engineers to focus on complex aspects of code quality while maintaining high user satisfaction and accuracy.

This use case addresses the business problem of identifying and linking records that refer to the same entity despite variations in data representation, targeting data engineers, data scientists, and business analysts managing large, heterogeneous datasets. It proposes a dual-approach entity resolution framework: a rule-based method leveraging predefined rules for matching standardized identifiers such as SSN or NPI, which offers transparency and speed in high-quality data environments; and a machine-learning algorithm-based method designed to handle inconsistent, text-heavy, and context-dependent data through advanced techniques like transformer-based language models (e.g., BERT) and blocking strategies for efficient candidate pair generation. Important constraints include data quality, the need for extensive preprocessing, and the challenges in interpretability and labeling for ML models. The expected outcome is improved accuracy and efficiency in resolving entities across datasets, enabling better data integration and insight generation, with future directions aimed at automating the resolution pipeline end-to-end.

Plaid addresses the business problem of slow, error-prone income verification in lending by targeting lenders as intended users with its Bank Income product, which automates real-time income identification and categorization from consumers’ bank transactions using machine learning. The solution entails extracting transactions via Plaid’s connectivity to over 12,000 financial institutions, filtering non-income data, clustering transactions into income streams, detecting income frequency with hybrid frequency detection algorithms, and employing two models: an Income Identification Model to predict user-selected valid income streams and an Income Categorization Model that classifies income into 13 specific categories like SALARY and GIG_ECONOMY. Key data constraints include noisy user-labeled training data addressed by an ML-powered label enhancement process, diverse data types requiring specialized featurization (text embeddings for transaction descriptions, categorical encoding, time series statistics, and user context features). The significance lies in improved recall and precision for income sources, streamlined user selection reducing time by 17%, and enabling faster, more accurate underwriting with a 24% increase in salary recall, thereby enhancing lender credit decisioning efficiency and reliability.

Canva's performance marketing team addressed the complex problem of managing tens of thousands of Apple Search Ads keyword bids across multiple campaigns and regions, aiming to maximize new active users while controlling cost per tap within weekly budgets. Initially relying on a labor-intensive, SQL-based rules system that primarily exploited known keyword performance but lacked exploration and responsiveness to competitor bidding, Canva developed an end-to-end automated solution leveraging a contextual multi-armed bandit (CMAB) model. This system estimates bid-to-spend relationships using survival analysis with interval-censored data, models spend-to-return curves per keyword via parametric Hill functions combined with a LightGBM prior to handle cold starts, and employs Thompson sampling to balance exploration and exploitation. Using numerical optimization constrained by daily campaign budgets, the model dynamically adjusts keyword bids, improving efficiency and reducing costs by 5–50% compared to the prior system while providing explainable outputs via a marketer-friendly interface. The solution effectively adapts to budget shifts, scales across nearly 10,000 keywords in 11 campaigns, and facilitates maintainability through modular components, with future enhancements planned to incorporate event-driven factors, budget pacing, additional ASA metrics, and multi-objective optimization.

Canva’s Shape Assist addresses the challenge of shaky, imprecise user-drawn shapes in its Draw tool by deploying a lightweight, client-side machine learning solution for real-time hand-drawn shape recognition, intended for millions of creative users seeking to easily enhance designs with polished vector graphics. Initially relying on heuristic-based computer vision for simple, single-stroke geometric shapes, the team transitioned to a recurrent neural network model trained on a large, diverse dataset of user strokes represented as sequences of x-y coordinates, enabling recognition of more complex shapes while preserving key details via a custom curve simplification algorithm. The model, comprising an LSTM layer followed by a dense layer with around 64,000 parameters (~250 KB), runs fully in-browser without internet connectivity, ensuring low latency and offline functionality. To ensure reliability, the multi-label classification approach includes confidence-based rejection to avoid incorrect automatic shape replacement, which is triggered when users hold the cursor post-drawing. This client-side ML solution enhances user experience by providing immediate, accurate shape recognition and alignment to vector templates, overcoming the variability of user drawing speeds and styles while minimizing load time and computational overhead.

The business problem addressed is improving personalization of Etsy’s sponsored search ads to increase click-through (CTR) and post-click conversion rates (PCCVR) using real-time user behavior. Intended users encompass Etsy shoppers, both logged-in and logged-out, whose short-term sequences of recent actions (e.g., views, favorites, cart adds, purchases) are encoded to represent their dynamic intent. The proposed solution is the adSformer diversifiable personalization module (ADPM), a modular approach combining three components: (1) an adSformer encoder—a transformer variant incorporating a global max pooling layer that learns salient sequential signals from variable-length user action sequences within the last hour; (2) pretrained multimodal listing embeddings that integrate visual, textual (AIR), and skip-gram representations to capture diverse item features; and (3) learned “on-the-fly” embeddings for actions/entities lacking pretrained representations, enabling real-time adaptation. ADPM outputs a comprehensive dynamic user embedding concatenated with inputs to downstream CTR and PCCVR neural ranking models, trained with wide & deep architectures and cross networks (DCN). Constraints include managing very large vocabularies (capped to top frequent entities), latency and memory efficiency in production serving, and bias correction such as position bias. Offline and robust online A/B tests demonstrated statistically significant lifts in ROC-AUC and PR-AUC metrics (+2.66% CTR, +2.42% PCCVR ROC-AUC improvements offline) and business KPIs like return on ad spend (ROAS) and gross merchandise sales (GMS). Overall, the ADPM leverages short-term behavioral sequences and heterogeneous pretrained embeddings via a flexible transformer-based architecture to personalize industrial-scale sponsored ads effectively at Etsy.

TomTom addresses the business challenge of maintaining competitiveness and operational efficiency in location technology by adopting a strategic generative AI (GenAI) approach aimed at enhancing user experiences and streamlining mapmaking and development workflows. Intended users include drivers, OEMs, developers, and internal teams across the company. The solution involves a hub-and-spoke model wherein a central GenAI innovation hub leads core applications like the ChatGPT location plugin and an AI assistant for in-car digital cockpits while empowering domain-expert teams to develop and own sponsored GenAI projects using cloud-based foundational models, particularly from Azure OpenAI, thus avoiding costly in-house model development. Constraints include managing risks such as hallucinations, data confidentiality, and prioritizing ROI-driven projects aligned with TomTom’s core business. Expected outcomes are improved task performance, enhanced product quality, increased productivity, democratized AI innovation, continuous workforce upskilling, and responsible AI use governance, all achieved without major increases in budget or headcount.

Stitch Fix addresses the business challenge of lengthy model training times for its personalized styling recommendation system, which relies on the Client Time Series Model (CTSM), a sequence-based model using temporally masked encoders built with PyTorch. Intended for machine learning engineers and data scientists, the solution involves implementing multi-GPU distributed training using PyTorch Lightning with a Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) strategy to shard data and parallelize training across multiple GPUs on a single EC2 instance. This approach reduces training time substantially, enabling faster iteration on feature additions and model improvements while balancing GPU utilization and training cost, with careful hyperparameter optimization to offset batch size effects on model performance. The outcome is a scalable, maintainable training pipeline facilitating regular model retraining and deployment, thereby improving recommendation quality and development velocity in a large-scale, production recommender system.

Stitch Fix addresses the challenge of efficiently producing engaging, brand-aligned text content for marketing and e-commerce by leveraging an expert-in-the-loop generative AI approach. Intended for copywriters and marketing teams, this solution combines large language models (LLMs) like GPT-3 with human expertise to generate ad headlines and product descriptions that reflect nuanced style attributes captured via latent style spaces and word embeddings. For ad headlines, few-shot learning enables rapid creation of varied, style-specific copy, which human experts then review and refine, significantly reducing manual effort while ensuring quality. For the more complex task of generating product descriptions at scale, Stitch Fix fine-tunes pre-trained models on expert-written examples to produce accurate, engaging, and SEO-optimized descriptions in the brand voice. This iterative process integrates human feedback to continuously improve model outputs, balancing AI-driven creativity and efficiency with the subtlety of human language understanding, thereby enhancing client experience and operational scalability without compromising content quality.

Vinted, Europe’s largest online second-hand fashion marketplace, faced the challenge of delivering personalized homepage recommendations efficiently from millions of listings by combining explicit user inputs (like clothing size) with implicit preferences inferred from interaction histories. To address limitations in their initial ANN search solution using Faiss—such as no real-time updates and lack of metadata prefiltering—they evaluated and ultimately adopted Vespa, an open-source platform offering low-latency vector search with metadata filtering, real-time data updates, and superior performance metrics compared to Elasticsearch. Vespa enabled them to implement a three-stage recommender system leveraging a two-tower embedding model for users and listings that supports approximate nearest neighbor search with prefiltering by brand and size, achieving sub-100ms recall latency and high throughput. Extensive benchmarks and AB tests confirmed Vespa’s operational ease, scalability via cluster replication, and user satisfaction gains from personalized recommendations, while experiments balancing approximate and exact search parameters helped optimize relevance versus resource use. This deployment not only improved recommendation accuracy and system architecture but also enhanced user engagement, setting the stage for future integration of dense and sparse retrieval techniques.

Expedia Group addressed the challenge of engaging price-sensitive travelers who monitor flight price fluctuations by transitioning from static rule-based push notifications to a machine learning-driven message relevancy model. Intended for travelers subscribed to flight price alerts, the solution uses a Random Forest classifier to predict the likelihood a traveler will open a notification based on features such as past interaction history, subscription profile, and flight price changes. This ML approach aims to optimize notification timing and content to enhance traveler engagement, reduce notification fatigue, and improve booking conversion rates by sending alerts only when relevant. Business success was measured by increased opt-in rates, notification open rates, reduced opt-outs, and retention, with safeguards ensuring timely alerts for subscribers, even with short subscription durations. The iterative ML enhancements, including automated hyperparameter tuning and broadened target definitions, yielded significant improvements in recall and F1 score, ultimately driving stronger trust and repeated bookings through timely, personalized price alerts.

Canva addresses the challenge of generating relevant, multi-lingual keywords for millions of diverse content templates to improve search indexing and content discovery for over 100 million users, especially aiding newer creators who struggle to choose suitable keywords. They developed a deep learning solution inspired by CLIP, employing a siamese architecture with twin multi-lingual sentence transformers to embed both template text and candidate keywords, optimizing a contrastive asymmetric loss to focus on positive keyword matches while handling class imbalance without costly hard-negative mining. Training data is carefully curated from internal creators and batched by language to avoid incorrect negative labeling, using a vocabulary of the top 1000 keywords per language, though inference can handle unlimited keywords including unseen ones. The model enhances keyword recommendation during template labeling, providing high-quality suggestions across languages, thus reducing creators' workload and improving content surfacing within Canva’s editor and marketplace.

Expedia Group addresses the challenge of sparse and inconsistent organic flight search data, which limits comprehensive price forecasting across all routes, trip dates, and passenger counts, by generating synthetic search data through automated predefined searches. This synthetic data ensures a consistent, daily dataset of flight prices for popular routes within a specific advance purchase window, enabling more reliable time series forecasting. Although synthetic data generation is resource-intensive, constrained by system capacity and storage costs, and limits route coverage, it provides a controlled, rich dataset critical for developing accurate price forecasting models. The Travel Insights and Interactions ML team plans to expand forecasting coverage by either increasing synthetic search scope or adopting generalized models that better scale to all traveler searches, with synthetic data remaining vital for curating representative datasets.

Expedia Group addresses the business problem of recommending travel properties that balance relevance and diversity to enhance user satisfaction and exploration. Targeting travelers who benefit from varied lodging options, the solution incorporates semantic retrieval techniques by generating item embeddings from numerical (e.g., review counts, transactions), categorical (e.g., star rating, price bucket), and list features (amenities) drawn from anonymized click and booking data in the Expedia Group RecTour Dataset. Key constraints include preserving recommendation relevance while increasing intra-list dissimilarity measured via metrics like inverse Euclidean or cosine similarity between embeddings. The team experiments with diversity augmentation primarily through post-processing re-ranking algorithms such as the Neighborhood Cosine Distance (an MMR-based approach) and clustering (e.g., K-means), favoring explicit feature clustering for explainability and flexibility over learned embeddings like Hotel2Vec to balance diversity with ranking quality (e.g., NDCG). Expected outcomes include a configurable tradeoff between relevance and diversity, improved variety in top recommendations across price, amenities, and ratings, and enhanced user engagement without extensive model retraining, thereby operationalizing semantic diversity in travel recommendation systems.

Expedia Group addresses the business challenge of accurately predicting Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) across its diverse travel brands to inform acquisition, retention, and marketing strategies by deploying a machine learning solution for hundreds of millions of customers. Traditional methods fall short as they either segment CLV narrowly, ignore non-monetary engagement features, or fail on new customers, so Expedia uses supervised learning with CatBoost gradient-boosted trees on over 200 engineered features encompassing detailed booking history and customer engagement metrics like email interactions and loyalty tiers. The approach segments customers by geography and booking behavior to tailor models and mitigate skewed target distributions, with predictions evaluated through Lorenz curves, Gini coefficients, and calibration plots to ensure precise differentiation of high-value customers. The system leverages a complex unified machine learning platform with data lakes on AWS S3, distributed processing via Spark and Kubernetes, workflow orchestration through Airflow, CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions and Spinnaker, and comprehensive model management and monitoring infrastructure to enable monthly retraining and daily scoring at scale. Future enhancements focus on enriching engagement features, improving model interpretability, exploring more advanced modeling techniques, and integrating drift detection, reflecting the platform’s emphasis on robust MLOps to support continuous improvement and deployment in a high-impact business context.

Netflix’s speech and music activity detection (SMAD) system addresses the need for precise audio segmentation in Film & TV production and delivery, targeting professionals involved in audio post-processing, localization, and accessibility feature creation. The solution employs a convolutional recurrent neural network trained on a large, noisy-labeled dataset (TVSM) derived from diverse, copyrighted Netflix catalog content with frame-level speech and music annotations, including overlapping classes. SMAD outputs detailed temporal metadata that enables structural audio segmentation, supports loudness normalization, dialogue intelligibility, speaker diarization, music information retrieval, and dubbing workflows while distinguishing speech, music, and sound effects despite challenging audio overlaps and ambiguous boundaries. This enables scalable, automated content understanding that improves audio quality and operational efficiency throughout Netflix’s global production lifecycle.

Netflix addressed the business problem of scaling and personalizing promotional video montages ("sizzle reels") for its members by developing Dynamic Sizzles, a system that programmatically constructs unique, personalized trailers in real time using a large, pre-edited collection of video clips called a Mega Asset. Intended for Netflix viewers, this solution leverages human-analyzed clips organized with precise timecodes via an Adobe Premiere plug-in, combined with a predefined cadence that allocates clip order and duration weighted by individual member preferences, to dynamically generate highly personalized video sequences. Utilizing Netflix’s Hollow technology enables efficient retrieval of clip timecodes for seamless playback, while player modifications were made to handle asymmetrical streaming of numerous short, discontiguous video segments with synchronized audio. This approach reduces production time and cost by up to 70%, allowing Netflix to deliver millions of personalized, engaging promotional reels at scale, ultimately enhancing user engagement and satisfaction.

Netflix addressed the challenge faced by video creators who need to quickly find specific scenes or visual elements across its vast catalog—such as a particular action shot or character moment—by building an in-video search system. The primary users are internal creative teams producing trailers, social media snippets, and promotional materials who require efficient retrieval of visually and semantically relevant clips. The solution employs a machine learning model leveraging contrastive learning to jointly embed video shots and their aligned textual descriptions into a shared space, enabling precise multimodal retrieval. Training utilized large-scale internal datasets of video clips paired with rich textual metadata to fine-tune the embeddings for improved video retrieval accuracy. The infrastructure precomputes shot-level video embeddings using GPU acceleration, stores them in a media feature store, and performs real-time nearest neighbor search via Elasticsearch. This system supports queries input as natural language and can search subsets or the entire catalog, thereby significantly accelerating creative workflows, lowering manual search effort, and enhancing the quality and engagement of Netflix’s promotional content.

Wayfair addresses the business problem of costly "incident" policy abuse fraud where malicious customers, known as account hoppers, exploit policies by making false claims to obtain free replacements or refunds while keeping original products. Intended users are Wayfair’s fraud detection teams, tasked with early identification and prevention of such fraud despite limited historical data on new accounts. The proposed solution constructs a knowledge graph linking customer accounts via shared attributes like names and payment methods, then applies Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)—specifically a two-layer GraphSAGE model—to perform node-level binary classification of accounts as fraudulent or not. This approach enables the model to learn rich representations by aggregating neighborhood information without extensive manual feature engineering. Data constraints include handling dynamic, complex graph structures and ensuring scalable training and inference, addressed through neighborhood sampling and batch processing, with ongoing efforts towards real-time serving. The expected outcome is improved precision and recall in detecting fraudsters, resulting in millions of dollars saved annually and enhanced security in Wayfair’s online retail marketplace.

Instacart addressed the challenge of predicting real-time availability for hundreds of millions of grocery items, crucial for providing customers with accurate stock information amid volatile inventory and supply chains exacerbated by the COVID pandemic. Intended for customers ordering groceries and in-store shoppers fulfilling those orders, the solution involved developing a new hierarchical machine-learning model composed of three components: General availability (long-term patterns addressing sparse data by leveraging samples from local and similar items), Trending (an XGBoost model capturing recent deviations from baseline availability), and Real-Time inference (leveraging freshest shopper and retailer signals via streaming infrastructure). These components improve interpretability, handle data sparsity, and adapt to varying business use cases such as scheduled deliveries and instant fulfillment. The model is supported by a modernized MLOps infrastructure called Griffin, enabling context-aware, multi-version scoring and stratified update frequencies (real-time, hourly, daily) based on item purchase frequency, which reduced computation costs by 80% while enhancing score freshness and relevance. This integrated system improves the customer experience by enabling timely, reliable stock predictions and efficient shopper routing, demonstrating success in both offline and online metrics with cost savings and operational scalability.

Instacart addressed the challenge of predicting real-time item availability across millions of products in over 80,000 retail locations with diverse inventory systems by developing a scalable, low-latency engineering infrastructure combined with advanced machine learning models. Intended for use by product and engineering teams to improve customer experience, the solution involves ingesting ML-generated availability scores into a database via full syncs and demand-driven lazy refreshes, enabling fast bulk retrieval during item filtering. A multi-model experimentation framework supports parallel evaluation of diverse ML models by synchronizing scores into dedicated database columns, linked with feature flags for A/B testing. To manage operational complexity across segments defined by product categories, retailers, regions, and user groups, they introduced a Deltas Framework and Threshold Resolver, dynamically adjusting selection thresholds per segment to optimize the selection-found rate curve. Further, a multi-segment optimization feedback loop employs customer behavior and outcome metrics to continuously fine-tune these thresholds, balancing global and segment-specific performance. This integrated approach enabled Instacart to restore and scale pre-pandemic levels of order fulfillment accuracy, significantly increasing found rates and experimentation velocity while maintaining consistency across user surfaces.

Nextdoor addresses the business problem of low user engagement with AI-generated content, specifically improving email subject lines for their New and Trending notifications, where traditional methods often yield generic or uninformative subjects. Intended users are the neighborhood network’s email recipients whose interaction drives platform growth. The proposed solution combines prompt-engineered Generative AI to extract authentic, hallucination-free subject lines from posts with a fine-tuned reward model trained on user click data to predict and select subject lines that outperform user-generated ones. Rejection sampling uses this reward model to filter generated candidates, ensuring only higher-engagement lines are used. Engineering optimizations like caching and daily monitoring maintain model accuracy and cost-effectiveness. The expected outcome is increased email open rates, clicks, sessions, and ultimately higher weekly active users and ad revenue, demonstrated by A/B testing showing improvement over baseline user-written subjects.

This use case addresses the business problem of gender bias in Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) systems, particularly concerning masculine, feminine, and the gender-neutral singular "they." Intended for developers and researchers working on NLP models, the proposed solution involves creating parallel datasets with gender-specific and singular "they" terms and introducing a novel data augmentation technique informed by linguistic patterns distinguishing singular from plural "they." The approach refines existing augmentation methods for masculine and feminine terms and uses these enriched training datasets to reduce gender bias in three competitive GEC systems. Important constraints include maintaining correction quality while mitigating bias. The expected outcome is enhanced fairness and inclusivity in GEC performance, promoting more equitable language processing without sacrificing accuracy.

E-commerce platforms face the challenge of meeting user expectations for fast, relevant, and personalized search with query suggestions, yet only 19% implement this effectively despite 80% having integrations. Algolia addresses this by leveraging existing click and conversion data to build a dedicated Query Suggestions index, configurable via their dashboard to handle relevance thresholds and filter inappropriate content, ensuring safe and useful autocomplete results. By integrating Algolia’s Query Suggestions plugin with their InstantSearch-based UI, developers can deliver scoped, category-specific query suggestions similar to Amazon’s interface, enhancing search frictionless experience through built-in filtering options. This solution caters to various business sizes and aims to increase search efficiency and user satisfaction by dynamically generating and displaying tailored query completions powered by Algolia AI Recommendations.

BlaBlaCar addresses the challenge of improving passenger-driver matching by deploying Smart Selection, a machine learning algorithm that predicts the likelihood of drivers accepting booking requests and hides low-scoring Boost rides—artificially created ride offers—to enhance match quality. Intended for passengers and drivers, this solution relies on acceptance data and continuous A/B/C testing to dynamically adjust the percentage of hidden Boost rides, balancing the trade-off between minimizing rejected requests and preserving ride options. By continuously monitoring model performance and incorporating stakeholder feedback via daily dashboard reporting, BlaBlaCar maintains model accuracy and alignment with business goals, resulting in increased driver acceptance rates and booked seats, thereby optimizing inventory quality and user experience in a dynamic marketplace.

BlaBlaCar addresses the challenge of improving ride match quality between drivers and passengers on its carpooling platform, where drivers publish trips and passengers search for rides, by using machine learning to predict driver acceptance of “Boost rides”—potential trips created by adding detours to drivers’ routes to better meet passenger needs. Given that Boost rides significantly increase booking opportunities but suffer from a lower acceptance rate (50% versus 80% for regular requests), BlaBlaCar frames predicting acceptance as a binary classification problem using an XGBoost model trained on historical data incorporating temporal, geographic, and driver behavior features. The model runs in production to score potential Boost rides instantly, enabling the platform to selectively hide low-probability Boost requests, balancing quantity and quality of ride options to reduce driver frustration and passenger rejection. This ML-driven selective display improves user experience, increases acceptance rates by about 30%, and grows overall passenger bookings by refining the marketplace’s self-regulating dynamics across multiple countries.

Pinterest addresses the business problem of delivering highly relevant, context- and user-aware Closeup (Related Pins) recommendations that drive user engagement and satisfaction during the inspiration-to-realization journey on its platform. Intended users are Pinterest Pinners interacting with Closeup feeds. The solution employs a deep multi-task learning approach with a sophisticated deep neural network (DNN) architecture leveraging Multi-gate Mixture of Experts (MMoE) to jointly predict multiple user outcomes like repin, closeup, clicks, and long-clicks, integrating sequential user behavior via a transformer encoder and context features. To stabilize prediction quality and reduce rank permutation, the model uses teacher-student score regularization. Post-ranking, a personalized, context-aware blending model based on learned utility optimizes real-time recommendation ordering by dynamically weighting predictions to balance organic and shopping content, enhancing engagement metrics such as repin volume and full-screen video views. The approach relies on extensive user interaction logs, embeddings from PinSage, and contextual signals, while addressing challenges like model instability and parameter tuning. Expected outcomes include significant improvements in offline prediction metrics and positive online A/B test results demonstrating increased user interactions and session duration on the Closeup surface.

Kingfisher faces the business challenge of efficiently extracting meaningful insights from large volumes of unstructured customer feedback collected via surveys and product reviews to enhance customer experience across its retail banners like B&Q and Screwfix. Intended users include data analysts and business decision-makers seeking to understand customer sentiment and reactions to initiatives such as loyalty programs or app features. The proposed solution is an innovative semantic retrieval pipeline combining unsupervised topic modeling methods—Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) to identify initial word co-occurrence topics, BERTopic leveraging BERT-based contextual embeddings for improved word-sense disambiguation, and a feedforward neural network trained to project and refine these model topics into a human-labelled topic space for enhanced interpretability. Complementing this, large language models (LLMs) are used for few-shot learning to automate and scale data labeling, reducing manual effort by over 90%, with active learning targeting labeling of underrepresented topics. This hybrid approach enables scalable, precise, and explainable extraction of latent thematic trends from qualitative customer text data, supporting both high-level trend analysis and drill-down into individual survey responses, ultimately allowing Kingfisher to monitor topic dynamics over time and geography, improve response strategies, and drive data-led customer satisfaction and revenue growth.

The e-commerce platform Whatnot addresses user search challenges caused by misspellings and abbreviations, which lead to poor content discovery and engagement, by leveraging GPT-based large language models for semantic query expansion. By analyzing logged search queries, normalizing and tokenizing them, and using GPT offline to suggest spelling corrections and expansions for common tokens—including brand names and acronyms—the system populates a query expansion cache that augments user inputs at search time to include corrected and expanded terms. This method significantly improves search result relevance, reducing irrelevant content by over 50%, and preserves low-latency requirements critical for user experience. Future enhancements include semantic query expansion beyond token-level corrections, extraction of entity and attribute keywords in product and show descriptions, and image/video content understanding to support filtered searches and advance toward full semantic search capabilities.

LinkedIn addresses the challenge of efficiently moderating massive volumes of user-generated content to ensure platform safety for its 1 billion members by deploying an AI-driven content review prioritization framework aimed at Trust & Safety teams. The solution employs XGBoost machine learning models trained on past human-labeled review data to dynamically score content in the review queue based on the probability of policy violation, continuously updating scores with new member reports. Integrated into LinkedIn’s existing review assignment system via a decision layer built on ProML, this probabilistic, real-time scoring enables prioritizing high-risk content for human reviewers while deprioritizing likely non-violative items, thereby optimizing reviewer bandwidth. The system achieves stricter precision thresholds critical for maintaining trust and reduces average detection time of violative content by 60%, significantly lowering member exposure to harmful posts. This dynamic, automated approach enhances scalability beyond linear human staffing growth and has initially been applied to feed posts and comments, with plans for broader rollout across LinkedIn’s product suite.

GitHub is evolving GitHub Copilot by experimenting with large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 to enhance developer productivity throughout the software development lifecycle. Targeting developers who routinely manage code, documentation, pull requests, and command-line tasks, the solution integrates AI-driven tools into GitHub’s ecosystem to provide context-aware, conversational, and personalized assistance. Key challenges include ensuring AI suggestions are predictable, tolerable, steerable, and verifiable, with an emphasis on UX design to present AI outputs as editable suggestions or references rather than authoritative statements, thus reducing the cost of errors and increasing user trust. Important data sources include code repositories, pull requests, and large documentation corpora accessed via retrieval-augmented generation, while constraints involve managing AI inaccuracies and designing workflows that help developers quickly evaluate and refine suggestions. The expected outcome is an AI-powered environment where Copilot seamlessly supports tasks such as summarizing pull requests, generating CLI commands, and answering complex documentation queries, thereby accelerating development and reducing friction in typical coding workflows.

Haleon's Data Science Team addresses the challenge of optimizing toothpaste manufacturing operations by leveraging Fast Dynamic Time Warping (FastDTW) to perform real-time manufacturing step detection and provide actionable insights to site operators. Intended users include manufacturing site operators who require visibility into ongoing processes and timely recommendations to maintain quality control and efficiency. The solution involves streaming sensor data collected every five seconds, comparing real-time signals against historical step templates using FastDTW to measure similarity despite temporal misalignment, and applying globally defined distance thresholds to identify manufacturing steps accurately. Constraints include managing large, continuous datasets where FastDTW’s near-linear time complexity offers a balance between computational efficiency and step detection precision, achieved also through feature scaling and logical model design to handle missed detections and ensure adequate data length for analysis. The expected outcome is a robust, scalable system enabling proactive monitoring and optimization of manufacturing workflows, improving process efficiency and product quality across similar toothpaste variants.

Haleon addresses the business problem of deriving actionable insights from multilingual consumer queries on its health product brands collected by the Consumer Relations team over two years, aiming to understand customer needs, detect emerging trends, and ensure product safety and effectiveness. Intended users include product managers and marketing teams who leverage a Power BI dashboard summarizing keyword trends and query categorizations. The solution employs a semantic retrieval pipeline involving translation to English, text preprocessing (stop word removal, lemmatization, stemming), n-gram extraction, TF-IDF scoring, and fuzzy matching for categorization, applied to sanitized, timestamped social media query data in multiple languages. This approach enables identification of evolving consumer preferences, unmet needs, and potential safety issues, resulting in informed product development, marketing decisions, and enhanced real-world evidence tracking that supports innovation and competitive advantage in consumer health markets.

Haleon's marketing team, supported by their Data Science group, developed a reinforcement learning tool using Thompson Sampling to optimize marketing spend allocation across defined AdGroups (keyword-targeted audience segments) for improved ROI. Addressing the multi-armed bandit problem, the solution balances exploration and exploitation by probabilistically modeling each AdGroup’s performance distributions based on metrics like click-through rate, cost-per-click, and cost-per-action from aggregated transactional data in Microsoft Azure. This approach dynamically recommends budget allocations through iterative Bayesian updates, which power a Power BI dashboard for marketing managers to make data-driven spending decisions. Incorporating a contextual bandit framework allows human intervention to adapt recommendations according to environmental factors, enhancing personalization and campaign effectiveness. The expected business outcomes include maximized conversion rates, minimized acquisition costs, significant marketing budget savings, and optimized marketing channel performance, demonstrating reinforcement learning's value in marketing technology.

Coinbase addresses the challenge of detecting fraudulent cryptocurrency transactions by developing a scalable Blockchain Address Risk Scoring System that predicts the risk levels of blockchain addresses using machine learning. Intended for Coinbase users and internal security teams, this system analyzes comprehensive features including aggregate transaction behaviors and graph-based structural information derived from a large-scale transaction graph of blockchain addresses, notably employing Node2Vec graph embeddings generated through an incremental, distributed MapReduce approach to accommodate the evolving and immense scale of Ethereum and Bitcoin networks. Trained on labeled data from validated sources through supervised learning, the risk scores—ranging from 0 to 1—inform user-facing products like Coinbase Retail and Wallet to warn users, delay suspicious transactions, and enable manual review, ultimately enhancing fraud detection, protecting user funds, and increasing trust in crypto investments.

Haleon addresses the challenge of managing and searching over 21 million diverse digital media assets with sparse, inconsistent metadata by leveraging computer vision and AI for semantic retrieval. Targeting marketing, supply chain, and consumer behavior teams, the proposed solution uses image analysis to generate descriptive keywords, OCR to extract text such as product branding, and fuzzy matching against a product taxonomy to enrich and validate metadata automatically. This AI-driven tagging pipeline, prototyped and scaled on Azure cloud, significantly improves asset findability and reuse by increasing tags for Brand, Category, and other attributes from under 70% to over 90%, overcoming manual remediation impracticalities due to dataset scale and metadata variability. Future extensions involve unsupervised clustering and supervised machine learning models to infer additional tags and relationships, enhancing metadata completeness and enabling more nuanced digital asset management across Haleon's global marketing operations.

Haleon's Data Science and MarTech teams address the challenge of managing and enhancing metadata for over a petabyte of diverse digital assets, including images and videos, to improve their organization, searchability, and reuse in marketing campaigns. They developed a scalable AI-driven computer vision pipeline on Microsoft Azure, integrating optical character recognition (OCR) to extract text from product imagery, preprocessing various file types, and employing fuzzy logic for error-tolerant brand matching against a product taxonomy. Video assets are processed efficiently through frame sampling based on interframe similarity and consolidated into cost-effective storyboards. Additional metadata extraction includes EXIF data mining to inform storage strategies. The pipeline's reliability is ensured via statistical sampling and bootstrapping to measure coverage and accuracy of tags at scale. This solution leverages cloud-based DevOps tools like Kubernetes, Docker, and Terraform to parallelize processing and maintain flexibility, resulting in automated, robust metadata enrichment that supports better digital asset management across global campaigns.

LinkedIn addresses the challenge of capturing and mapping professional skills embedded across diverse content—such as profiles, job postings, resumes, and LinkedIn Learning courses—to fuel its comprehensive Skills Graph, which underpins skills-first experiences like job matching, learning recommendations, and candidate search. Users including recruiters, job seekers, and members benefit from AI-driven extraction that segments text, tags skills using both token-based trie lookups and semantic models based on multilingual BERT embeddings, and employs multitask learning frameworks to score skills’ relevance and relationships (e.g., required, core) within content domains. The system handles complex inference-time constraints using knowledge distillation for model compression, combined offline and nearline serving architectures, and incorporates rich feedback loops from recruiters and members to continuously improve skill extraction accuracy. Outputs enable enhanced job recommendation relevance, member skill proficiency estimation, and dynamic updating of the Skills Graph to reflect evolving labor market demands across LinkedIn’s ecosystem.

CARS24, a leading online preowned car marketplace in India, addresses the business challenge of enhancing user experience by precisely and efficiently matching individual buyers with cars through advanced machine learning-driven personalized search and recommendation systems. Moving beyond a cohort-based model that clustered users into about 200 demand segments based on implicit behavioral data, CARS24 developed a user-level personalization framework that builds detailed profiles from both explicit signals (e.g., search filters, wishlist activity) and implicit signals (e.g., clicks, impressions). Utilizing Learning to Rank algorithms—particularly the listwise method implemented via YetiRank with CatBoost—they dynamically re-rank car listings to optimize relevance per user preference, thereby reducing cognitive overload caused by abundant choices. This personalized semantic retrieval leverages comprehensive user interactions including image and inspection report views, effectively tailoring car catalogues in near real-time through a queue-based scoring system. A/B testing demonstrated around 11% lift in overall user conversion and improved metrics like impressions-to-view (I2V) and impressions-to-booking initiated (I2BI), indicating heightened engagement and booking likelihood. The solution targets individual buyers on CARS24’s platform, aiming to increase retention, ease decision-making, and scale internationally with plans toward real-time in-session intent capture through an online scoring infrastructure.

CARS24 addresses the business problem of objectively assessing pre-owned car engine conditions—crucial for accurate pricing—by overcoming the subjectivity and intrusiveness of traditional sensor-based methods. The intended users are inspection technicians who record engine sounds via mobile phones during vehicle evaluations. The solution employs a hybrid machine learning approach combining signal processing with convolutional neural networks (CNN), specifically using Fourier transform-based frequency domain analysis, clustering of dominant frequencies, and Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) spectrograms analyzed through a ResNet-50 model adapted for audio classification. Key data include millions of engine sound recordings at idle and 2000 RPM, annotated refurbishment decisions for over 100,000 engines, and engine metadata like displacement and fuel type. Noise reduction techniques isolate engine sounds from environmental interference, while nearest neighbor algorithms and CNN outputs are combined to predict engine anomalies such as abnormal crankshaft sounds, misfires, and vibrations. The expected outcome is real-time, non-intrusive detection of engine faults to guide technicians and reduce procurement risk, enhancing inspection consistency and decision-making accuracy in vehicle refurbishment.

CARS24 addresses the critical business problem of optimally pricing used cars—an inherently subjective and variable market—by employing a machine-learning driven dynamic pricing framework aimed at sellers and platform managers. Leveraging extensive internal data from millions of car inspections, auctions, and transactions alongside external OEM pricing and classified listings, the solution predicts car-level demand and price elasticity to dynamically revise listing prices post-launch. This hybrid pricing approach integrates value-based, cost-plus, and market-based strategies to maximize portfolio margin while achieving target sell-through rates (STR), thereby reducing inventory holding costs, enhancing margin predictability, and improving pricing efficiency. The framework employs models for demand prediction, price optimization with business constraint validation, and continuous feedback loops for hyperparameter tuning, enabling faster convergence to optimal prices amid the complexities of car condition, regional demand, and market dynamics, resulting in faster inventory turnover, controlled margins, and iterative improvement of pricing strategies.

Instacart addresses challenges in leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) such as context limitations and hallucinations for internal productivity tools by developing advanced prompt engineering techniques tailored for GPT-4. Intended for internal users—employees, customers, merchants, and shoppers—the solution enhances semantic retrieval and task completion via inventive prompting methods including Chain of Thought (CoT) for stepwise reasoning, ReAct for augmenting models with external action capabilities, Monte Carlo for brainstorming multiple creative options, Self Correction for iterative refinement, Classifying for constrained multiple-choice responses with controlled token outputs, and Puppetry to guide the model into producing outputs in exact formats by simulating partial responses. These techniques rely on careful prompt design, multi-turn interactions, and API-level controls like logit biasing to ensure reliable, interpretable, and high-quality semantic retrieval outcomes that improve model accuracy, consistency, and usability in complex workflows such as pull request generation and internal knowledge search.

Digits addresses the challenge of saving time and improving client communication for accountants by employing generative machine learning models, specifically fine-tuned T5 transformer architectures, to automatically generate professional, context-aware questions about financial transactions. Intended for accountants interacting with small business clients, the solution uses transaction descriptions and customizable persona inputs to produce tailored queries that accountants can edit or send directly, preserving authenticity in diverse client relationships. The models are trained on in-house curated datasets with a preprocessing pipeline using TensorFlow Transform, deployed through TensorFlow Serving on Google Cloud Vertex AI, and rigorously evaluated using metrics such as Levenshtein distance, semantic similarity, and Rouge scores to balance linguistic diversity and relevance. Safety measures—including toxicity filtering, hallucination detection, and mandatory human review—mitigate risks of biased or erroneous outputs while safeguarding user privacy by restricting data sharing. This approach transforms mundane financial review tasks into efficient, safer interactions, enabling accountants to better serve clients with less manual effort.

This use case addresses the challenge accountants face in categorizing banking transactions, which can be subjective and vary by client context, by empowering them rather than replacing their expertise. Intended users are accountants who benefit from Digits Boost, a tool that leverages similarity-based machine learning to generate vector embeddings representing transactions semantically, allowing the system to find related, historical transactions in a high-dimensional vector space via approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search techniques like Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs (HNSW). The solution involves a three-stage pipeline: encoding transactions into embeddings, efficiently searching for similar transactions using cosine similarity and scalable ANN services (e.g., Google Cloud's Vertex AI Matching Engine), and deriving categorization suggestions based on analogous past transactions. This approach accommodates individualized classification preferences, scales to millions of transactions daily, reduces computational overhead substantially, and results in timely, context-aware recommendations that assist accountants in error detection and category assignment, enhancing workflow efficiency without undermining human judgment.

LinkedIn addresses the challenge of proactively detecting and mitigating evolving, adversarial content threats on its platform by employing an AutoML framework to automate and accelerate the development, retraining, and deployment of content abuse detection models. Intended for LinkedIn's ML engineers and data scientists, this solution tackles issues like data drift, rapid shifts in discourse due to global events, and fraudulent user behavior by automating repetitive yet critical processes including data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model evaluation. AutoML reduces the model update cycle from months to days, enabling continual learning on recent data to maintain high accuracy and robustness in content moderation classifiers. It ensures standardization and reproducibility, supports multiple model architectures in parallel, and integrates with production deployment pipelines, all while addressing scalability and usability challenges inherent to handling diverse multimodal content at scale. The expected outcome is a more efficient, reliable, and adaptive content review system that strengthens member trust and safety on the LinkedIn platform.

DoorDash addresses the challenge of personalizing retail store pages for diverse verticals—such as grocery, convenience, pets, and alcohol—where inventory spans hundreds of thousands of SKUs across thousands of categories, making manual curation untenable. Intended users are online shoppers who benefit from tailored recommendations based on their purchase history, preferences, dietary restrictions, and contextual factors like time or promotions. The solution employs a multi-stage machine learning framework including personalized collection generation, collection retrieval, item horizontal ranking, and post-processing steps to balance relevance, diversity, and business constraints (e.g., availability and visual appeal). Key models predict engagement probabilities for collections and items, incorporating features like consumer-item interactions, item attributes, semantic embeddings, and positional bias. Diversification techniques such as maximal marginal relevance prevent homogeneous recommendations within and across collections. Expected outcomes include streamlined cart-building, discovery of new favorites, improved customer retention through trust in personalized experiences, and scalable recommendation serving as DoorDash expands its retail verticals.

In the domain of financial crime detection, SumUp developed a Large Language Model (LLM) application to generate free-text narratives called "Reason for Suspicion" reports, documenting suspicious activity post human-investigation for anti-money laundering (AML) compliance. Traditional NLP metrics proved inadequate for evaluating these qualitative, unstructured texts, as they failed to capture topic coverage, supporting evidence, avoiding fabricated facts, and narrative structure. To address this, an LLM-driven evaluator was proposed that mimics human assessment by scoring generated narratives across application-specific criteria like topic coverage, customer profile consistency, supporting facts, factual accuracy, structure, and conclusion clarity. This automated evaluator aligns closely with expert agent reviews, significantly streamlining large-scale narrative assessment without adding manual workload, though it introduces biases and lacks standardization across projects. Strategies like position swapping and few-shot prompting mitigate these limitations, enabling more reliable evaluation of narrative generation quality, ultimately optimizing LLM deployment for financial crime reporting.

Leboncoin, a major French secondhand marketplace with high user and ad volumes, faced the challenge of delivering relevant and timely search results from millions of user-described ads. To address this, the Search team developed a neural network-based ads Re-Ranker using a bi-encoder architecture with large language models that separately encode ads and queries into vector embeddings, enabling efficient precomputation of ad representations stored in a vector database. Combining these embeddings with ElasticSearch's initial TF-IDF-like retrieval allows real-time re-ranking of top ads within strict latency constraints. The training dataset leveraged implicit user click feedback through contrastive learning and multimodal inputs (text and tabular data), while the deployed solution boosted click and contact rates by up to 5% and improved ranking quality metrics by around 10%, enhancing user experience and business outcomes on leboncoin's platform.

ZipRecruiter's employment marketplace addresses the challenge of efficiently matching over 36 million job-seeker resumes to 12 million active job postings in real time, amid highly diverse, dynamic, and unstructured data from multiple sources including job titles, resumes, and engagement signals. Targeting both job-seekers and employers, the solution employs multimodal machine learning architectures with pre-trained encoders that capture semantic similarity within entity types using contrastive and triplet focal loss functions, enabling zero-shot generalization for unseen entities. These encoders generate embeddings for jobs, resumes, and search queries, which are integrated using sequence-aware models to produce unified job-seeker representations, while simultaneously optimizing a symmetrized dual-contrastive loss to balance recommendations between job-seeker and employer objectives. This approach has improved job-seeker engagement by 12% and satisfaction by over 18%, driving scalable, context-aware, and fair bi-directional recommendations at marketplace scale.

Duolingo addresses the business problem of labor-intensive, slow course content creation for its 21 million daily users by equipping language learning experts with Large Language Models (LLMs) to accelerate and scale lesson development. Learning Designers create detailed prompts combining fixed and variable instructions—such as language, CEFR difficulty level, thematic focus, and grammar points—which the LLM uses to generate multiple exercise options that align with specific pedagogical constraints (e.g., A2 level Spanish using preterite and imperfect tenses). Human experts then select and refine these AI-generated exercises to ensure naturalness and learning efficacy. This semantic retrieval approach leverages AI’s ability to predict contextually appropriate language completions, producing quality exercises more rapidly while preserving expert oversight. The expected outcomes are faster content updates, deeper coverage of the CEFR scale, expanded course offerings (including less-common languages), and the reallocation of human resources to innovative features, thereby enhancing productivity, convenience, and educational value in Duolingo’s language courses.

The use case describes the deployment of ChatLTV, a generative AI chatbot integrated into Slack as a faculty co-pilot for Harvard Business School's MBA entrepreneurship course, Launching Tech Ventures (LTV), serving around 250 students. The business problem addressed was enhancing student learning and engagement with a large, complex corpus of proprietary course materials including case studies, teaching notes, books, blog posts, and historical Slack Q&A, amounting to 15 million words. Utilizing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with OpenAI's GPT-4 integrated via Microsoft Azure and a Pinecone vector database, ChatLTV provided accurate, sourced responses tailored to student queries, including course content and administrative questions, while preserving data privacy and compliance. The solution enabled private and public interactions, produced high-quality, relevant answers, and allowed faculty real-time insights into student comprehension and preparation. It improved student learning outcomes, increased engagement, and enriched classroom discussions by supporting pre-class preparation without diminishing in-class participation. Additionally, a custom GPT was created to provide automated, critical feedback on final papers, enhancing personalized academic evaluation.

This use case addresses the business problem of integrating advanced AI-powered product copilots that enable users to ask natural language questions and receive context-specific responses, a feature sought by nearly all large technology companies. Intended users are professional software engineers tasked with building these copilots, many encountering AI integration challenges for the first time. The proposed solution involves studying the software engineering process through interviews with 26 engineers, identifying pain points and challenges that existing tools and practices fail to address, followed by collaborative brainstorming of new opportunities and tool designs to support large-scale AI application development. Important constraints include the novelty and complexity of AI integration within traditional software engineering workflows and the need for community-driven, open, and privacy-respecting tools. The expected outcome is improved engineering processes and tools that facilitate scalable, efficient development of AI-powered product copilots, enabling broader adoption in software products.

GitHub Copilot addresses the business problem of enhancing developer productivity by improving its AI pair programmer’s contextual understanding to provide relevant coding suggestions. Intended for software developers using integrated development environments (IDEs), the solution leverages advanced prompt engineering techniques and transformer-based large language models (LLMs), such as Codex, to incorporate contextual data from multiple sources including current and neighboring files, pull requests, and project issues, despite constraints like transformer input size limits (~6,000 characters). Innovations like the Fill-In-the-Middle paradigm and neighboring tabs algorithm optimize prompt construction for greater context, boosting suggestion acceptance rates by 5-10%. Future enhancements involve employing vector databases and embeddings to semantically retrieve relevant snippets from vast private repositories, enabling tailored coding experiences while preserving privacy. As a result, developers code significantly faster (up to 55%), reduce repetitive effort, and can focus on more complex, fulfilling tasks, thereby improving overall software development efficiency.

GitHub engineers address challenges such as efficiently managing project dependencies, automating repetitive coding tasks like incrementing protobuf IDs, generating complex regular expressions, organizing troubleshooting notes, and learning new programming languages by leveraging GitHub Copilot's semantic retrieval and code generation capabilities integrated within their IDE. By prompting Copilot with relevant context—often through structured comments or selective data preprocessing—they receive concise, context-aware code completions, parameterized tests, and documentation quickly, significantly reducing manual effort and turnaround time from days to minutes. This approach enables better handling of large context constraints in language models, supports remote collaboration via structured Markdown outputs, and accelerates skill acquisition, ultimately enhancing developer productivity and knowledge sharing within software engineering workflows.

Wayfair addressed the challenge of evolving fraud tactics impacting customer security and trust by developing Melange, a self-supervised representation learning-based embedding system that captures complex patterns in customer session sequences. Intended for fraud detection teams, Melange automatically generates high-dimensional vector embeddings from raw customer journey data—such as page visits and interactions during sessions—without relying on manual feature engineering or costly labeled data.
